#1859. Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: Five signings the Red Devils could make in 2027 to transform themselves under Argentine

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 18:13, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 18:18

Manchester United are soon expected to confirm Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach, with Michael Carrick set to be relieved of his duties at Old Trafford.

An announcement from Man United on the removal of Carrick is likely to arrive on Thursday, with Pochettino leaving his managerial role with the United States in order to take charge of the 20-time English champions.

Man United are expected to at least attempt to add to their squad in January, but the bulk of their business for 2027 will have to wait until the summer.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five signings the Red Devils could make in the middle of next year to hand Pochettino a huge chance of enjoying a successful 2027-28 campaign.

Man United overhauled their midfield during the summer transfer window, bringing in Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, but it would be fair to say that the balance in the middle of the park is still not quite right at this moment in time.

Manuel Ugarte is likely to leave next summer, once he has recovered from a serious knee injury, while there are question marks surrounding Bruno Fernandes' long-term future.

As a result, there is expected to be space in the squad for another midfield arrival, and bringing in Scott from Bournemouth would be a huge statement of intent.

The 23-year-old - valued in the region of £80m by Bournemouth - is also wanted by Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool.

However, Man United should also be firmly in the mix for the England international, who has quickly developed into one of the leading central midfielders in the Premier League.

There is currently widespread speculation surrounding Karl's future at Bayern, with the Germany international potentially being allowed to leave Allianz Arena in 2027.

Karl, 18, has scored three goals and registered two assists in 14 appearances for Vincent Kompany's side during the 2026-27 campaign.

The versatile attacker has represented Bayern on 54 occasions, scoring 12 goals and registering 10 assists, and a recent report claimed that Man United had been 'alerted' to the possibility that the teenager could be available in 2027.

Karl is said to be valued by Bayern in the region of £50m, and he could potentially be a long-term replacement for Fernandes at Old Trafford.

There is currently a host of speculation surrounding Esposito's future, with Arsenal and Man United believed to be interested in the Italy international.

The 21-year-old has scored four times in 13 appearances for Inter this season, in addition to coming up with two assists, while he has 15 goals and nine assists in 63 appearances for the club in total since breaking into the first team.

The 6ft 3in striker is said to be valued by Inter in the region of £84m, so it would be a major deal for Man United.

Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems are a concern, and it would be some statement from the Red Devils if they were able to win the race for Esposito, who was allegedly scouted by the English giants last weekend.

Man United are long-term admirers of Branthwaite, with the Red Devils making an attempt to sign the centre-back from Everton in the summer of 2024.

It is understood that the Red Devils had at least two offers for the Englishman turned down, but it is possible that their interest could be reignited in 2027.

Branthwaite has made nine appearances for Everton this season, and the 24-year-old is producing high-level performances for the Merseyside outfit.

The Englishman has a contract with Everton until the summer of 2030, but it would be difficult for the Toffees to fight off serious interest from Man United next year.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are both likely to leave Old Trafford in 2027, and it is absolutely vital that the Red Devils boost their defence next summer.

Man United attempted to sign Hall from Newcastle over the summer, but the club were ultimately unable to secure a deal for the England international.

The 22-year-old signed a new contract with the Magpies in September, with his contract at St James' Park due to run until the summer of 2031.

However, it is not impossible to imagine Hall being on the move next summer, with Man United desperate to bring in a new left-back.

Luke Shaw could be released next summer, and Man United need a long-term option in that area of the field, with Hall said to be incredibly keen on a switch to Old Trafford.

#1858. Arsenal dealt transfer blow in pursuit of Mikel Arteta’s ‘top target’

Bournemouth have ruled out a transfer move for rumoured Arsenal target Eli Junior Kroupi this January.

Arsenal scoured the market for attacking reinforcements in the summer transfer window, with Mikel Arteta keen to add firepower to his title-winning frontline.

Christos Tzolis was signed for a fee of £34million from Club Brugge to help fill the void left by the departure of both Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli – and the Greece international has gone on to enjoy an encouraging start to life in north London.

However, it was clear the Premier League champions had ideally intended to bring in another proven talent in this area of the pitch after the club were gazumped by Chelsea in the race for Morgan Rogers.

There was genuine interest in Vinicius Junior and the Gunners were reportedly hopeful of closing a deal for the Real Madrid superstar right up until the start of August.

But Vinicius would go on to pen a new long-term contract at the Bernabeu, ultimately leaving Arsenal disappointed in their efforts to provide support and competition for the likes of Noni Madueke, Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyokeres and Tzolis.

According to talkSPORT, Arsenal are ready to reenter the transfer market to land a top-class attacker this winter and have a number of high-profile names on their shortlist of possible solutions.

It’s claimed Endrick, Vinicius’ team-mate at both club and international level, is now firmly on Arsenal’s radar after failing to win over Jose Mourinho at Madrid.

The 21-year-old Brazil international shares the same agency firm as Vinicius, with whom Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has built a healthy relationship following their dealings in the summer.

Kroupi has racked up 13 goals and one assist in 39 appearances for Bournemouth and is widely regarded to be among the most exciting young talents in Premier League football.

Arsenal will likely fall short should their step up their pursuit of Kroupi this January, though, as the Cherries are said to have ‘made it clear’ that the 20-year-old is not for sale.

The France Under-21 international underwent surgery for a foot injury back in July and made his return to first-team action as a late substitute in Bournemouth’s stunning 3-0 victory at Manchester United last month.

Marco Rose is still yet to start Kroupi this season but the former Lorient man has also featured as a substitute in Bournemouth’s recent wins over Aston Villa, Leeds and Ipswich.

The versatile forward has three-and-a-half years remaining on his current contract at the Vitality Stadium.

Last season, Kroupi scored the goal against Manchester City that ultimately sealed Arsenal’s status as champions after a painful 22-year wait for the title.

Asked if he’d been congratulated by any thankful Arsenal players at the time, he told Stadium Astro: ‘Yes I have received many messages but I tell myself that I didn’t do this for Arsenal.

‘I do this for Bournemouth. I can say I scored against Arsenal, I scored against City.

‘It doesn’t change anything, I just wanted to help my team.’

When asked about his goals and ambitions for the future, Kroupi replied: ‘Perform with my team and perform also in Europe also because it is very beautiful to be in Europe but you have to perform to play there.’

#1857. Manchester United sack Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino appointment close

Michael Carrick has officially been sacked by Manchester United after less than six months as the club’s permanent manager, with Mauricio Pochettino expected to replace him.

In a statement released on Thursday, United said that the club “has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions” after a “disappointing start to the season” and that they “intend to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible”.

United added in tribute to Carrick: “Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

“His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.”

Carrick took over as United’s interim head coach in January after Ruben Amorim’s departure and was promoted to the full-time job in May after qualifying for the Champions League last season.

He has failed to carry that momentum into the new campaign, though, and departs with United mired in the Premier League relegation zone having won only one of their first 10 matches and sitting 17th in the Champions League table. They also exited the Carabao Cup at the third round stage.

A 4-1 defeat by Como in Europe last month left Carrick on the brink and a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth then initially looked as though it would be the end of the road, but he was spared the sack and retained for the visit to Chelsea, which the Red Devils lost 2-0.

A dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League last week looked to restore some faith - at least temporarily - but a topsy-turvy performance against Aston Villa in a chaotic 4-4 draw, only salvaged at the death by Patrick Dorgu’s last-gasp equaliser, further underlined his side’s significant issues heading into the final international break of 2026.

United parted ways with Carrick following a meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada held at Carrington, where, despite the intense speculation over his position, Carrick had continued to take training this week with United’s players not currently away on international duty.

Wilcox and Berrada had been in Monaco on Wednesday for crunch talks with United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls the club’s sporting policy, where it was decided that a change in the dugout was needed to turn around their fortunes.

Pochettino is expected to replace Carrick and become the new manager at Old Trafford, despite only signing a four-year contract extension to remain in charge of the United States national team following the World Cup on home soil in the summer.

An official approach is believed to have been made to US Soccer, with Pochettino’s deal containing a release clause worth $10million (£7.5m). Pochettino is keen on the move and has spoken to United about their managerial position on multiple occasions in the past, with an agreement over personal terms reported to have been reached.

Former Chelsea and Tottenham boss Pochettino - who has seen off competition for the job from the likes of ex-Newcastle manager Eddie Howe and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann - would become United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

#1856. Andorra vs Gibraltar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 18:15

Andorra will conclude their Nations League D campaign on Friday, when they welcome Gibraltar to Estadi de la FAF d'Encamp.

The hosts are last in their three-team group with one point from their three matches so far, whereas the visitors are second with two points from two games.

Andorra were beaten 1-0 by Malta on October 4 in their latest outing in the competition, with their only point coming in a 0-0 stalemate with Gibraltar on September 27.

All three teams in their group will be competing in Nations League C in 2028-29, but while there is no jeopardy for either team on Friday, their placement in group will determine their rankings for the next campaign.

The hosts have only scored one goal in the group so far, though they have conceded just three times in the group stage.

Boss Koldo Alvarez has been in charge of the national team for 16 years, but he has only overseen 13 wins from his 146 games in the dugout, and he has lost 15, drawn five and won just one of his last 21 matches as head coach.

Andorra's performances at home have been poor considering they have been beaten in six of their past seven fixtures when playing as hosts.

Gibraltar are in arguably their best ever period of form given they are undefeated in their last six fixtures in all competitions, winning on three occasions.

The visitors managed to score 11 goals and concede just twice, and they kept four clean sheets in that time.

It should be noted that Los Llanis did play Liechtenstein, Cayman Islands, British Virgin Islands and Sao Tome and Principe in those six clashes, with the latter the highest-ranked nation by FIFA at 194th.

Head coach Scott Wiseman will hope to avoid becoming the first manager in his country's history to lose against Andorra, with his side having won two times and settled for two stalemates in four meetings with their hosts.

Gibraltar have been defeated in five of their seven most recent contests on the road, with their only victory in that period a 2-0 success against Liechtenstein on October 5.

Andorra could use a four-man defence featuring central defenders Max Llovera and Ian Bryan Olivera ahead of goalkeeper Iker Alvarez.

Midfielders Ot Remolins Planes and Eric Vales could be rewarded with their 11th and 25th caps for the national team.

In the frontline, it would not be surprising to see forward Albert Rosas partnered by Guillaume Lopez, with the duo having scored five and two goals respectively for the hosts.

As for Gibraltar, it would not be surprising to see Dan Bent, Bernardo Lopes and Julian Valarino form a back three, especially after the trio started in the reverse fixture against their hosts.

Leon Mason and Nicholas Pozo may be used as two third of a midfield three, while Tjay De Barr and Dylan Borge are set to start up front.

Alvarez; Font, Llovera, Olivera, Nicolas; Alaez, Planes, Vales, Rodrigo; Rosas, Lopez

Banda; Bent, Lopes, Valarino; Ronan, Mason, Torrilla, Pozo, Scanlon; De Barr, Borge

Neither side are likely to be at their best considering there is little to play for given all teams will be in Nations League C.

However, with Andorra backed by a home crowd, perhaps the hosts will be able take at least a point against Gibraltar, who have often travelled poorly.

#1854. Danny Murphy tells Liverpool to explore transfer move for £33m Man Utd target

Danny Murphy has urged Liverpool to strongly consider a transfer move for Barcelona misfit Alejandro Balde this winter.

Liverpool invested heavily in the summer with a view to giving Andoni Iraola the best possible chance in the hot seat following Arne Slot’s dismissal as manager.

It saw Jeremy Jacquet, Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz all added to Iraola’s squad for a combined fee of around £200million – and the trio have gone on to enjoy encouraging starts to life at Anfield.

With the Reds having dropped points in five of their opening ten matches of the Premier League campaign, though, attentions have quickly turned to the January transfer window as an opportunity to further strengthen.

Milos Kerkez has blown hot and cold since joining Liverpool for a fee of £40million from Bournemouth 18 months ago and rumours have been circulating that the club could reenter the transfer market for a new left-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The Merseyside giants have been credited with a strong interest in Juventus’ Andrea Cambiaso and Santos’ Vinicius Lira in recent days, with Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas both yet to fully convince fans that they could eventually fill the shoes left by Andy Robertson.

But according to Murphy, ‘super talent’ Balde could be the ideal signing for Liverpool given the out-of-favour Spaniard is already used to the expectations that come with playing for a ‘huge football club’.

Balde has made just three substitute appearances for Barca in La Liga this term and Manchester United have also been named as a potential escape route for the £33m-rated defender at the halfway point of the season.

‘I think Liverpool will be looking for a left-back but it’s hard because I don’t know Kerkez personally, I know he’s trying really hard and you can see it in his energy that he cares, and that’s a great start,’ the ex-Liverpool and England midfielder told Betarades.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He cares for the shirt and he’s working really hard to try and make it happen.

‘I think Balde could be great for Liverpool because he’s a super talent and he’s also got that experience of being at a huge football club with that expectation.

‘Balde’s a really good player. There’s lots of good players out there and Liverpool will be scouring the world.’

Murphy believes it could be time for Liverpool to look for ‘more established’ and ‘ready-made players’ after prioritising youth in recent transfer windows.

‘I think the most important thing is trying to bring somebody in who doesn’t make you guess whether he can deal with the pressure of a big club,’ he added.

‘It’s a delicate balance because Liverpool for years were very good at taking diamonds in from the rough, if you like. Someone like [Philippe] Coutinho, like [Andy] Robertson, like [Sadio] Mane even from Southampton. [Roberto] Firmino was about £20m.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Liverpool took those diamonds in the rough and moulded them into these superstars, and then when we’ve tried to go and spend massive money on these already made stars, it’s not quite worked.

‘I still think there are times, especially in defensive areas where you really do want ready-made players. Especially when you’re struggling.

‘I think Liverpool have got enough young players now who need to grow. I think now there’s an argument to have a few more players who are maybe a bit more established.’

Murphy has some sympathy for Kerkez but feels the Hungary international needs to get his head down and work on his composure if he is to make a success of his time at Liverpool.

‘He just lacks composure and quality in the final third when he gets there. Too often his final pass or his cross isn’t good enough,’ he continued.

‘He doesn’t have the composure of an Andy Robertson, and to be fair to him, you are filling the boots of arguably one of the best left-backs Liverpool’s ever had.”

‘I think the lack of quality at times is due to the fact he’s very fast. He’s very much 100 miles an hour. I’m surprised they’re not working with him more to slow him down in those areas and to just calm himself.

‘Now it wouldn’t be as bad if he was brilliant defensively, but he’s struggling defensively as well. His positional play is sometimes a bit off, he’s a bit erratic in terms of diving in or getting beat.

‘He likes jumping into people. It’s a dilemma for Liverpool, and I think one that they’ll definitely be looking at and trying to address, because not every signing works out.’

On Kerkez, Murphy went on: ‘I was somebody who saw him that year at Bournemouth and thought he looked like a terrific young player.

‘But the one thing that people don’t understand and it’s only when you’ve been in that position you can empathise with going from playing in one environment to being in the intense, magnified world of Liverpool Football Club.

‘Every game, every minute, every mistake is analysed by the fans, by the press, by the worldwide audience, and I think that expectation, and that pressure is a bit much for him.’

#1852. Cape Verde vs Liberia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 11 Nov 2026 18:45

Cape Verde will be looking to get their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign off the mark when they welcome Liberia to the Estadio Nacional de Cabo Verde in Praia on Friday evening.

The Blue Sharks sit third in Group K after back-to-back defeats to Mali and Rwanda, while the visitors are bottom of the table and also without a point.

Cape Verde have made a disappointing start to the post-World Cup era, losing both of their opening Group K matches under new head coach Humberto Bettencourt.

They were beaten 3-1 by Mali before suffering a 2-1 home defeat to Rwanda, in which Gilson Benchimol's 40th-minute strike was cancelled out before half-time and the visitors scored again seven minutes into the second half.

Bettencourt, who spent six years as Bubista's assistant, has overseen two defeats in his first two competitive matches, leaving the Blue Sharks winless in their last six games (D3, L3), a run that includes goalless World Cup draws with Spain and Saudi Arabia, a 2-2 draw with Uruguay and a 3-2 round-of-32 defeat to Argentina.

However, their previous meetings with Liberia offer some encouragement, as Cape Verde have won three of the four encounters between the sides, including a 4-1 home victory in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in March 2011.

Liberia, meanwhile, began their qualifying campaign with a 3-1 defeat in Kigali, where Sylvanus Nimely scored their only goal before Rwanda restored their two-goal advantage from the penalty spot in the 44th minute.

The Lone Star then suffered a 1-0 home defeat to Mali, with Martial Tia's 79th-minute strike settling the contest.

Moroccan coach Mohammed Adil Erradi, who took charge of his first competitive match in Kigali, is still waiting for his first victory.

Liberia have won just one of their last eight matches (D2, L5), with that success coming in a 3-1 friendly victory over Sierra Leone in June, while they have scored just once in their two qualifiers, making a trip to Praia a difficult assignment for a side ranked 146th in the world.

Cape Verde Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Liberia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Cape Verde have named a 26-man squad for the double-header, with goalkeeper Vozinha expected to start despite coming under scrutiny following the defeat to Rwanda.

The midfield options include Deroy Duarte, Kevin Pina, Jamiro Monteiro and Laros Duarte, while Dailon Livramento and Ryan Mendes are among the leading attacking options.

Huddersfield Town winger Derenseli Fernandes has been included, but defenders Roberto Lopes and Diney Borges are missing from the selection.

Liberia also have significant absentees, with captain Oscar Dorley ruled out after picking up a hamstring injury while playing for Saudi Arabian side Al-Taawoun.

Goalkeeper Tommy Songo is also injured, with Derrick Julu recalled to replace him.

Erradi has welcomed back Hammarby Talang striker William Gibson, while Ralph Weah has also earned a place in the 24-man squad.

Vozinha; Pina, Costa, Diney, Lopes Cabral; Pina, Duarte, Monteiro; Mendes, Livramento, Benchimol

Williams; Dweh, Sangare, Fully; Ledlum, Tweh, Kenneh, Teah, Nyenetue; Nimely, Kosiah

Cape Verde have the quality and home advantage to make them favourites, although their defensive problems should give the visitors some encouragement.

The hosts should have enough to claim their first points of the campaign, but their recent struggles suggest it may not be a comfortable evening.

Manchester United have said the decision to sack head coach Michael Carrick was “extremely difficult” and praised the 45-year-old for conducting himself with the “highest standards of dedication and professionalism.”

Carrick was relieved of his duties on Thursday morning, just 16 games into the season, with United in the relegation zone and without a Premier League win since August.

The Red Devils are now set to push ahead with negotiations for Mauricio Pochettino as they search for their fourth permanent head coach since INEOS and Sir Jim Ratcliffe took control of the day-to-day running of the club in February 2024.

Carrick becomes the first managerial casualty of the Premier League season, with United finally pulling the trigger after weeks of speculation surrounding his future.

The former midfielder first came under serious pressure after United’s 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como last month, but he remained in charge for a further four games despite failing to inspire an upturn in results.

Supporters were sympathetic to Carrick’s situation, applauding him after every game, but it always felt like a case of when, not if, the ex-England international would be sacked.

United have praised Carrick for his professionalism during an uncertain period, as it emerged that the Red Devils were actively pursuing Pochettino while their current head coach continued to attend to his duties.

“Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach,” a statement on the club’s website read.

“Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

“After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

#1847. Manchester United drop clear hint over next manager move as timeline emerges

Manchester United have announced the departure of Michael Carrick - and immediately pledged to “appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible”, with Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings.

Carrick was relieved of his duties as Man Utd boss on Thursday morning during a face-to-face meeting with CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, held at the club’s Carrington training base.

The decision to remove Carrick was made on Wednesday, when Berrada and Wilcox travelled to Monaco for talks with United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

In a statement to confirm his exit, United wrote: “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

“Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

“His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered. The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

Carrick was initially handed a stay of execution after a dismal 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth last month that followed immediately after a heavy 4-1 away loss to Como in the Champions League.

Amid more heavy speculation over his future, Carrick was left in post for United’s trip to Chelsea the following weekend - which they lost 2-0 despite an improved first-half display.

Carrick’s short permanent tenure showed brief signs of life in a comeback against Roma - a 3-2 win that ended a run of nine winless games across all competitions - before twice hitting back from a two-goal deficit to draw 4-4 at home to Aston Villa in what proved to be his final game in charge.

Carrick led training on Tuesday and Wednesday at Carrington with the United players not currently away on international duty, despite reports that he was in line to be sacked.

It has been suggested that United are comfortable with Pochettino taking charge of the USA’s two upcoming Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti during the current international window.

#1846. Morocco vs Niger - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 11 Nov 2026 18:45

Morocco will be looking to maintain their perfect start to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they welcome Niger to the Mohammed V Stadium in Casablanca on Friday.

The Atlas Lions have collected six points from their opening two Group A matches and sit top of the table after beating Gabon and Lesotho, while the visitors are third with three points, having won one and lost one of their opening two qualifiers.

Morocco have made an impressive start to their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign, winning both of their opening Group A matches against Gabon and Lesotho by identical 2-0 scorelines.

The Atlas Lions have scored four goals without conceding in the qualifiers, underlining their defensive organisation, while they have now kept clean sheets in three of their last four competitive matches.

Mohamed Ouahbi's side have since returned to action, playing out a 1-1 friendly draw with Mali in October, with Abdessamad Ezzalzouli scoring from the penalty spot in the first half before Gaoussou Diarra restored parity for the opposition.

The hosts will be looking to maintain their defensive solidity in competitive matches, and their previous meetings with Niger offer plenty of encouragement, having won all six encounters between the sides while conceding just once.

Morocco have also been particularly solid defensively in recent AFCON qualifying campaigns, conceding just twice in six matches during the previous edition of the competition and keeping four clean sheets, while they have now recorded six shutouts in their last eight matches in the tournament's qualifiers.

Niger, meanwhile, have struggled to build on their encouraging start to the qualifying campaign, opening with a 2-1 victory over Lesotho before suffering a 2-0 defeat against Gabon.

The Menas followed that loss with another 2-0 defeat, this time against Algeria in a friendly last month, leaving them with three losses from their last four matches across all competitions.

Their victory over Lesotho remains their only triumph in their last nine matches, a run that has also produced five defeats and three draws.

Niger's away record makes this an even more difficult assignment, with the Menas losing two of their last four competitive matches on the road, including a 5-0 defeat against Morocco in a previous World Cup qualifier.

Morocco have several important absentees, with Ismael Saibari, Azzedine Ounahi, Ayoub El Kaabi, Soufiane Rahimi, Chadi Riad and Hamza Igamane all missing from the squad because of injury concerns.

Sofyan Amrabat, Amine Harit and Amine Adli are also absent from the selection, while Youssef En-Nesyri has returned to the national team and Ayoub Oufkir has received his first senior call-up.

Neil El Aynaoui has also withdrawn after suffering an ankle problem during the international gathering, with Samir El Mourabet called up as his replacement.

Niger have named a largely locally based squad for the double-header, with experienced players such as Oumar Sako, Ali Mohamed, Daniel Sosah and Tidjani Amadou Moutari included.

Nabil Neghiz has also made several notable omissions from his selection, including Hainikoye Abiboulaye and Amadou Wonkoye.

#1845. Expected Points and clinical shooting: Stats highlight worries about sustainability of Milan’s Serie A form

AC Milan have collected more points than they deserved so far in the 2026-27 Serie A season, according to statistical data.

As MilanPress write, the Expected Points ranking makes for worrying reading. The metric compares the points actually earned by Serie A teams with those expected based on performances and chances created and conceded in the first 11 rounds of the league season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have earned 24 points compared to approximately 17 expected, meaning they are ‘over-performing’ by seven points. Milan are currently fourth in the table behind Lazio, Inter and Roma, but they should be a few places lower.

Inter are second with 28 actual points, but should have collected around 26, while Juventus are on 18 points earned versus the expected 21. Napoli also obtained less than the data indicated they should have, with 15 actual points compared to the approximately 19 expected.

The numbers, therefore, reveal a Milan that is particularly effective in turning its performances into tangible results. This is a positive aspect in terms of the league table, but also food for thought. Is it sustainable moving forwards?

Another interesting statistic has come from Kickest, which perhaps highlights why Ruben Amorim’s side have been able to out-perform what the data suggests.

They reveal that there are 113 players with at least 10 shots in Serie A so far in 2026-27. The top four with the best conversion rates have something in common: they play for the Diavolo.

➤ Rabiot — 41.7% (5 goals) ➤ Moreira — 40.0% (4) ➤ Cisse — 38.5% (5) ➤ Pulisic — 36.4% (4) ➤ De Bruyne — 30.0% (3)

It is reminiscent of something we published in January, when the shooting numbers under Massimiliano Allegri were similarly remarkable. As we know, a late-season collapse ended up coming.

Then there was the revelation from Sky after the Genoa game, as they looked at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. So, Milan must get much better at generating and sustaining pressure, or the results might start to regress.

Desperate for midfield reinforcements over the summer, United spent £50m to sign Brazil international Santos from Premier League rivals Chelsea.

Manchester United made midfield targets their priority after Casemiro left Old Trafford and Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious injury at the World Cup.

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 20:07, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 20:08

Arsenal are reportedly among three European heavyweights monitoring Borussia Dortmund defender Joane Gadou, with Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain also interested in the highly rated French teenager.

The 19-year-old has quickly established himself in the Bundesliga following his summer move from Red Bull Salzburg, attracting attention from some of Europe's biggest clubs after an impressive start to his Dortmund career.

According to German outlet Fussball News, citing transfer journalist Ekrem Konur, Arsenal, Real Madrid and PSG have been following Gadou's development closely and have sent scouts to watch him in action.

Dortmund are reluctant to lose the defender just months after signing him, although offers in the region of €40m to €50m (£35m to £44m) could reportedly persuade the German club to reconsider their position.

No formal asking price has been announced, and there is currently no indication that any of the interested clubs have submitted an offer.

A January transfer is considered highly unlikely, with the summer of 2027 potentially providing a more realistic opportunity for the player's admirers.

Gadou has made a rapid impression at Dortmund, having started 12 of his 15 appearances across all competitions during the opening months of the 2026-27 campaign.

The Frenchman has become a regular member of Niko Kovac's defensive unit, competing alongside established players such as Nico Schlotterbeck and Waldemar Anton.

Standing at 1.95 metres, Gadou combines an imposing physical presence with considerable pace and an ability to contribute to his team's build-up play.

His versatility has also been evident, with the teenager capable of operating on the right of a back three or filling in at right-back when required.

Those qualities have reportedly attracted scouts from Arsenal, Real Madrid and PSG, who are understood to have watched him during Dortmund's encounters with Real Betis and Bayern Munich.

For Arsenal, Gadou is already a familiar opponent.

The defender scored against the Gunners during the Emirates Cup in August, finding the net in the second half as Dortmund secured a 3-2 pre-season victory in north London.

That appearance provided an early opportunity for the Premier League champions to assess the youngster at close quarters, although there is no evidence that it directly prompted their reported transfer interest.

Gadou's development has been particularly rapid considering that he was still part of PSG's academy little more than two years ago.

He left the French champions for Salzburg in September 2024 without making a senior appearance in Paris, subsequently establishing himself in Austria before earning a move to Dortmund in May 2026.

The Bundesliga club reportedly paid approximately €19.5m (£17m) for his services, with further bonuses potentially increasing the overall fee.

Dortmund's sporting director Lars Ricken made clear at the time that the club had followed Gadou since his PSG days and expected him to play an important role immediately.

The French youth international has justified that confidence with his early performances, and his progress now appears to have attracted renewed attention from his former club.

Despite the growing interest, Dortmund are under no immediate pressure to negotiate Gadou's departure.

The defender signed a five-year contract upon his arrival from Salzburg, keeping him at Signal Iduna Park until June 2031.

That long-term agreement places the German club in a strong position should Arsenal, Real Madrid or PSG decide to formalise their interest.

According to Fussball News, bids approaching €40m to €50m could be required before Dortmund would consider changing their stance.

However, that figure represents a reported potential negotiating range rather than an official valuation communicated by the club.

Gadou's estimated market value currently stands at approximately €28m (£24.5m), highlighting the premium Dortmund could seek for a player who has already established himself in their first-team plans.

The Bundesliga side are also understood to have little appetite for selling the Frenchman during the January transfer window.

For PSG, a future move would represent an opportunity to bring back a player developed in their academy, although they would now face a substantial financial commitment to secure his return.

Arsenal and Real Madrid, meanwhile, are being linked with a defender whose early performances suggest that his reputation could continue to grow before next summer.

Much will depend on whether any of the three clubs progress beyond their reported scouting interest.

For now, Gadou remains an important part of Dortmund's plans, and his lengthy contract gives the German side considerable control over any potential transfer negotiations.

#1841. Thomas Tuchel issues England future latest as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over Manchester United

Thomas Tuchel has revealed he has no release clause in his England contract but insists he will not follow after Mauricio Pochettino and leave international football mid-contract to take a high-profile club role.

Pochettino is midway through his deal as head coach of the United States but is ready to become Michael Carrick’s replacement as Manchester United manager.

United chiefs have been in Monaco to discuss Carrick’s future, with the Englishman braced for Pochettino to replace him as the Red Devils’ head coach.

Tuchel, however, maintains there is no job that would take him away from England before they contest Euro 2028 on home soil.

The England job is the first time Tuchel has managed within international football. He previously held four of Europe’s most prestigious club roles as head coach of Borussia Dortmund, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and then Bayern Munich.

Pochettino only recently extended his United States contract to 2030 but is now ready to leave his post and head back into club football.

“No release clause and there’s no intention,” the German said when asked about his own situation.

“I signed a contract, I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.”

When asked whether there was ‘zero chance’ of him leaving if a big club came in before Euro 2028, Tuchel said: “I would say so.”

Tuchel remains unwilling to discuss his longer-term future beyond the expiry of his contract but says he is “open for everything”. The 53-year-old added: “I’m in a good place, and I love the players.”

Referring to the months of the year without international football, he said: “I miss my players, and I miss my team, and I miss the 50 [club] matches that I’m not involved in a year.

Old Trafford bosses held a review into Carrick’s position earlier this week and appear to have decided to make a change in the dugout.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the Manchester United job in recent weeks.

But United chose Pochettino as their first-choice pick this week and are currently finalising a deal to bring the Argentine back to the Premier League.

One of the biggest problems for United this season has been a fragile defence and ex-Premier League striker Charlie Austin insists Pochettino ‘needs a whole new back-four’.

#1837. GdS: A start vs. France at San Siro – Cisse’s rapid ascent continues with Mancini’s faith

Alphadjo Cisse continues to go from strength to strength, and his biggest moment yet might be coming during the break.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, beyond the confidence with which he plays and speaks, what’s truly striking is Cisse’s composure in front of goal at just 20 years of age, experiencing his first proper season in the top flight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His goal in Genoa seemed easy because he made it so, but it wasn’t. Adrien Rabiot’s pass was quite slow, the distance to the goal wasn’t that close, Genoa were exposed after losing the ball but Bijlow wasn’t in a particularly bad position, and beating him required precision.

Other strikers in those circumstances may have opted for a powerful finish. Not Cisse. He looked for the corner and found it with a lovely precise strike, one which revealed everything about the groove he has found himself in.

It was goal number five in the league for Alphadjo Cisse, making him Milan’s joint-top scorer alongside Rabiot. That extends to eight across all competitions, which puts the young Italian alone on the pedastal.

Two stats in particular stand out. The first: with his fifth goal in his ninth league appearance at 20 years and 17 days, he became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Pato (18 years and 181 days).

Second: he is one of only three players born in 2006 or later in the five major European leagues in 2026-27 to have scored at least eight goals in all competitions, along with Yamal (13) and Brunner (8).

Oh, and there’s another pretty good one: Shevchenko also scored eight goals in his first 13 games of the season with the Diavolo (although he achieved this in fewer minutes). The reward could well be a renewal, to fend off Premier League interest too.

Now, a change in dressing room awaits over the break. Roberto Mancini called him up to the senior national team for the first time, and according to La Gazzetta, the talent could start immediately.

He’s currently competing for a spot on the left in the 4-3-3 formation with Cambiaghi and Sebastiano Esposito. The Rossoneri guarantees more presence in the penalty area and quality in finishing, while Cambiaghi provides more coverage.

We’ll see if Mancini ultimately chooses to use him from the start, but what’s certain is that the former Verona man will be ready no matter what, and for a game at San Siro against France no less.

#1836. Man Utd interested in £75m Chelsea star ahead of January transfer window

Manchester United are reportedly weighing up an ambitious bid for out-of-favour Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto.

There were high hopes for Gusto when Chelsea signed the then 19-year-old for a fee of £30.7million from Lyon back in January 2023, when Graham Potter was in charge.

Gusto, now 23, has gone on to make a total of 144 appearances in all competitions for the Blues while helping the club win the Europa Conference League and the Club World Cup.

However, for the most part, Gusto has been forced to compete for minutes with Reece James when the Chelsea captain has been fit, meaning he has often struggled to get a consistent run of games under his belt.

James’ latest injury, likely to keep the Englishman sidelined until the New Year, had appeared to have opened the door for Gusto to nail down regular playing time under new head coach Xabi Alonso.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Gusto has not started a match in the Premier League since as far back as September, though, with Josh Acheampong seemingly overtaking the France international in the pecking order at Stamford Bridge.

Widespread reports earlier this week indicated Gusto was ‘assessing his options’ and ‘open’ to the prospect of leaving Chelsea in search of a fresh challenge elsewhere.

According to talkSPORT, this has put both Manchester clubs on red alert, with United and City said to be ‘interested’ and ‘keeping tabs’ on the situation should an opportunity arise.

It’s claimed it may take an offer in the region of £75million to convince Chelsea to part with Gusto.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It remains to be seen if either United or City will make a formal approach to prise the former Lyon man away from west London this winter.

City’s rumoured pursuit of Gusto stretches back for some time, with Enzo Maresca understood to have been keen on a reunion with the full-back when he took over the reins at the Etihad in the summer.

Gusto has three-and-a-half years remaining on his current contract with Chelsea.

There are, of course, complications for both United and City when it comes to potential transfer dealings this January, with the former reportedly on the verge of a managerial change and the latter still yet to learn their punishment for Premier League rule breaches.

Gusto filled in as a makeshift midfielder during Moises Caicedo’s absence from the team through injury and there were some suggestions the Frenchman could continue in the role under Alonso.

But speaking exclusively to Metro at the time, ex-Chelsea midfielder Gus Poyet insisted Gusto should look to earn Alonso’s trust by becoming the best possible right-back.

‘I do remember one of the most impressive decisions by a coach – Pep Guardiola at Bayern Munich, playing Lahm as a central midfielder,’ Poyet explained.

‘It was big news at the time, because he had the quality. Chelsea have been doing this with Reece James, because they understand it’s a possibility. Now Gusto as well.

‘But any right-back becoming a good central midfielder? No chance. Because full-backs naturally get used to playing with the line next to them, either on their right side or their left. Nobody’s coming at them from that side, because you’ve got the line.

‘Now, when you play in the middle, players come at you from everywhere, and not every player is the same. So yes, for one game [they can play there]. Yes, for twenty minutes. Not constantly. And now we see Chelsea playing a right-back as a central midfielder every game.

‘This is Chelsea — we’re not talking about a fourth-division club with no possibility of bringing in a player. So yes, it’s a little bit strange. And I don’t think it’s ideal.’

#1835. Bulgaria vs Iceland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 20:37

Iceland could clinch promotion to Nations League C by beating hosts Bulgaria on Friday at Stadion Hristo Botev.

The Icelandic national team are currently top of Group C with eight points from four matchdays, whereas their opponents are third with four points and must win if they are to make certain that they remain in the race for promotion.

Given six games will take place in the group, Bulgaria would be unable to catch Iceland if they were to take just a point on Friday, but a win for second-placed Estonia against Luxembourg on the same day would increase their points tally to nine and make them unreachable.

Unfortunately for boss Atanas Ribarski, his side have only won one of their last six games in all competitions, losing on three occasions.

The hosts did beat Luxembourg 2-0 on October 6 in their most recent Nations League outing, and that was their second clean sheet in the group stage.

At the other end of the pitch, the Lions have only scored three goals in this iteration of the competition, and they have failed to find the back of the net in eight of their 15 most recent games.

Bulgaria have lost five of their past 10 clashes at home, a stretch in which they triumphed just once and were held to four stalemates.

Only first place will guarantee progression into Nations League B, and Iceland would secure first if they beat Bulgaria and Estonia lost against Luxembourg.

Head coach Arnar Gunnlaugsson will be frustrated that his side failed to beat Estonia on October 6, when the two sides drew 0-0.

However, Strakarnir Okkar are unbeaten in four games, winning twice, though it may be a concern that they have only won two of their past 10 clashes.

The visitors managed to beat their hosts 3-0 when they met on October 3, winning for the first time in any of their five encounters, with Bulgaria claiming victory three times.

Iceland come into Friday's match having drawn one and won one of their two away fixtures in the Nations League so far, but they were winless in their prior six contests on the road, suffering four defeats.

Bulgaria must be careful to avoid needless yellow cards on Friday given eight players are at risk of picking up a suspension, though they know they will be able to welcome back goalkeeper Dimitar Mitov and winger Lukas Petkov.

Mitov is likely to be stationed behind a back four featuring centre-backs Stefan Velkov and Emil Tsenov, while Andrian Kraev and Ilia Gruev could start in a double pivot.

Petkov is set to start on the right side of attack, with Kristiyan Balov on the left flank and Atanas Iliev through the middle.

Iceland could position Andri Gudjohnsen in an advanced role behind striker Orri Oskarsson, with the pair likely to be supported by midfielders Gylfi Sigurdsson and Isak Bergmann Johannesson.

Central defenders Brynjar Ingi Bjarnason and Hordur Magnusson are candidates to start in the heart of a back four.

Mitov; Stoyanov, Velkov, Tsenov, Petrov; Kraev, Gruev; Petkov, Rusev, Balov; Iliev

Valdimarsson; Palsson, Bjarnason, Magnusson, Gretarsson; Sigurdsson, Johannesson; Haraldsson, Gudjohnsen, Anderson; Oskarsson

Though home advantage has often been crucial for many teams, Bulgaria have struggled for consistency when playing as hosts.

Iceland have also performed well on their travels in the Nations League, and they should be confident that they can take three points on Friday.

#1834. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

Andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

So far, four of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season have played on this opening matchday and all four have won:

Atletico had more possession in the second half but Liverpool were much the better side after the break.

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ

First Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a new contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

Alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

What a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

The two sides emerge from the tunnel to a cacophony of noise and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. The home fans boo the Champions League anthem and belt out “Liverpool! Liverpool!” over the top of it. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

Liverpool: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Tsimikas, Munoz, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, Danns.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.
