#1833. Man Utd sack Michael Carrick and provide update on Mauricio Pochettino arrival

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed their new head coach.

Carrick led training at Carrington this week despite it becoming clear a change was imminent as early as Monday evening.

He arrived at United’s training base at Carrington just before 8am on Thursday morning, leaving less than two-and-a-half hours later having been relieved of his duties.

Behind the scenes, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have sought approval from minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to part ways with Carrick, with a deal for Pochettino, currently serving as the USA men’s head coach, in place.

Carrick has been on the brink at various stages this season with United sat in the relegation zone in 18th place after 10 games, winning just once against newly promoted Ipswich Town.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

United opted against making a change during the international break in September and October when Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe were the leading contenders for the job.

Carrick gave himself a lifeline as United came from behind to beat Roma in the Champions League at the start of the month. United also fought back twice from 2-1 down in the same game against Aston Villa on Sunday to rescue a 4-4 draw but the decision was made the following day to part ways with the former midfielder.

His staff are also expected to leave, including former defender Jonny Evans who was pictured leaving Carrington with his belongings on Wednesday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Carrick’s departure marks the third season in a row United have sacked a manager midway through the campaign.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Pochettino’s first game in charge is expected to be the visit to Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

Carrick, who had a brief spell as interim boss in 2021, took the reins again in January following Ruben Amorim’s dismissal, securing hugely impressive wins over Manchester City and Arsenal in his opening two games.

They won 12 of their 17 games during the second-half of the 2025-26 season, securing third place and Champions League qualification with a game to spare. United picked up more points than champions Arsenal managed in the period from Carrick’s game in charge until the end of the campaign.

United clearly benefited from the lighter schedule in that run with just the Premier League to focus on. With European football back on the menu this season, reinforcements were needed.

United signed three new midfielders in the summer in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba but missed out on their top targets Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes who joined Manchester City and Tottenham respectively.

The club also failed to sign another left-back and a striker – positions they were in desperate need of cover for. United are paying the price now with Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko injured.

Before the comeback victory over Roma, United’s only wins this season came at home to Ipswich and against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah. Following a particularly harrowing defeat to Como in the Champions League, club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly challenged the manager’s tactics with the skipper dropped for the subsequent game against Chelsea.

Following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, Carrick was applauded off the pitch by supporters who instead turned their ire towards the players in a clear picture of where the frustration lies.

#1832. Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage with Thomas Frank in advanced talks over job

Crystal Palace have sacked manager Pierre Sage, with Thomas Frank in advanced talks over becoming his replacement.

The Eagles have won just two Premier League matches all season and sit bottom of the Premier League table after a run of four consecutive defeats.

The 3-1 home loss to Liverpool on Sunday was ultimately the final straw for chairman Steve Parish and the club hierarchy, with Eddie Nketiah’s injury-time penalty a mere consolation on another dark day at Selhurst Park.

Palace have won just once in their last eight games across all competitions - in the Carabao Cup last 16 against fellow strugglers Fulham last month.

That dismal run of results included a 5-0 hammering at high-flying rivals Brighton, as well as a 2-0 defeat by Tottenham, albeit after Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early red card.

“Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as Manager,” Palace said in an official statement on Thursday, shortly after Manchester United announced the sacking of Michael Carrick.

“Three members of Pierre’s coaching staff – Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard – have also left the club.

“The club would like to place on record its thanks to Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future.

“An update on the process of appointing a new Manager will be provided in due course.”

Former Spurs and Brentford boss Frank is the frontrunner to take over from Sage, in what would be a first foray back into management since his sacking by Tottenham back in February, when he was dismissed after only eight months at the helm and two wins in 17 games.

Palace only appointed Sage on a three-year contract in June to replace Oliver Glasner, who won the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League during a memorable two-and-a-half year spell in south London before leaving at the end of last season following the expiration of his deal and eventually joining Nottingham Forest.

Sage - who previously managed Lyon - left Lens for Selhurst Park after a year in charge that saw him deliver the first Coupe de France success in the club’s history and a second-place finish in Ligue 1 behind reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain, earning him manager of the year honours in the French top-flight.

However, he was unable to carry that success into a short-lived maiden stint in the Premier League, struggling to get his ideas across as Palace first contemplated his potential dismissal as early as September.

Standard Sport understands that Palace’s players became increasingly disillusioned with Sage’s methods and lack of communication, with the club possessing the worst defensive record in the division with 24 goals conceded in 10 games.

Sage is reported to have turned down the chance to quickly rejoin Lens, with Dino Toppmoller and Yannick Cahuzac having both been sacked by the club since his initial departure from the Stade Bollaert-Delelis in the summer.

Palace were interested in appointing Frank over the summer and he is now expected to take on the job, admired for his impressive work in establishing Brentford as a Premier League force despite that difficult spell with Tottenham.

Eddie Howe, Frank Lampard, Sean Dyche, Kieran McKenna, Vitor Pereira, Kim Hellberg, Vitor Matos and Tony Popovic were among the other managers to be linked with succeeding Sage.

#1831. Star of Mauricio Pochettino’s Spurs side reveals how he will change Man Utd

Former Tottenham star Toby Alderweireld says Mauricio Pochettino is the man to change the mentality at Manchester United and will bring intensity to the team.

Michael Carrick has been dismissed as Red Devils manager, with confirmation coming from the club on Thursday morning.

The club legend’s interim stint from January to the end of last season could scarcely have gone better, but his permanent spell in charge has been disastrous, with United winning just one of their 10 Premier League games this campaign.

Pochettino is now expected to be announced as Carrick’s replacement, with the USA manager set to leave his role and return to the Premier League where he has previously managed Chelsea, Southampton and Spurs.

His stint in charge of Tottenham was the most significant of his career, leading the club to a Champions League and second-place finish in the Premier League.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Alderweireld was a big part of that success, playing for Spurs from 2015-21, and he has high hopes for his former boss at Old Trafford.

‘He will make players fit, that’s for sure,’ the Belgian told talkSPORT. ‘Second of all he brings intensity. It’s not like everyone is playing their own game, he wants a team that’s going to be on the front foot. He wants to play pressure and having the ball as well.

‘A clear idea, intensity and players being fit, I think that’s the way he likes to work.’

Alderweireld reckons Pochettino is going to want the club to bend to his will to some extent, expecting the Argentine to insist on influence in the transfer market.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The summer, maybe the winter as well, the transfer window is going to be the players that he wants,’ said the former defender.

‘Also the facilities are going to be built also to the things that he wants. Making players fit, food-wise, gym-wise, everything needs to be how he wants it, that’s a big part of his philosophy.

‘Then he’ll want to buy the players. Maybe not always the biggest names, biggest talents, but guys with desire to win, desire to become better, desire to run. I think if you see the players he bought for Spurs, that’s thing number one, the desire to become better, the desire to win games, wins duels, to run.

‘That’s why I think Pochettino is the man for Man United, to change things around. In the past couple of transfer windows they’ve bought good players, good quality but they miss some chemistry, they miss the intensity and I think Pochettino will bring that.

‘He brings the mentality. If you work hard and bring your A game every single day, everything you want you can achieve. He will bring intensity and the mindset will change at Man United.’

#1830. Mali vs Rwanda - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 11 Nov 2026 23:07, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 18:01

Mali host Rwanda at the Stade du 26 Mars in Bamako on Friday, November 13, in the third round of Group K in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, with kickoff at 19:00 GMT.

Both sides won their opening two games and sit on six points with a goal difference of +3, Rwanda ahead on goals scored (five to four), and only the top two in a group with no host nation reach the finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

Anthony Da Silva's first competitive game in charge of Les Aigles ended in a 3-1 home win over Cape Verde, a side who played at this summer's World Cup, on September 25.

Ange Martial Tia scored after five minutes, Sidny Cabral equalised in the 10th minute, and Nene Dorgeles then scored in the 39th and 51st minutes.

Tia also scored the only goal in Paynesville on September 29, in the 79th minute, after which Da Silva said Liberia had defended well on a synthetic pitch.

A 1-1 friendly draw with Morocco in Tangier on October 4, in which Gaoussou Diarra cancelled out Abdessamad Ezzalzouli's 35th-minute penalty in the 77th minute, leaves Mali unbeaten in their last three games.

Mali have never lost to Rwanda, winning three and drawing one of four World Cup qualifiers, with a 7-2 aggregate goal record.

The latest two meetings were a 1-0 home win on September 1, 2021 and a 3-0 win in Kigali on November 11, 2021, yet Da Silva has still described the chances of the two teams as equal.

The Amavubi began with a 3-1 win over Liberia in Kigali on September 25, with Abeddy Biramahire scoring in the second minute, Leroy Mickels in the 33rd and Joy-Lance Mickels from the penalty spot in the 44th.

In Praia on September 29 they trailed to Gilson Benchimol's 40th-minute goal, before Claude Niyomugabo equalised in first-half stoppage time with a long-range strike from a corner.

Elie Tatou Iradukunda scored the winner in the 52nd minute after a mistake by Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, and Rwanda were outshot 19-6 over the 90 minutes.

Stephen Constantine, in his second spell as Rwanda coach, declared after that win that "the revolution has begun", and his side also drew 0-0 with Kenya on October 5 in an international friendly match in Kigali.

Rwanda are chasing a first AFCON finals appearance since 2004, and Constantine has said he will take one game at a time while rating Group K as containing two of the better teams in Africa.

They have never beaten Mali, scoring only two goals in four meetings, and have conceded in both qualifiers so far.

Mali Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Rwanda Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Tia, who has scored twice in two caps for Mali, is out with an ankle injury, while Adama Camara (hamstring) and Lassana Coulibaly (biceps femoris) are also unavailable.

West Ham midfielder Mohamadou Kante receives his first call-up after choosing Mali over France and Senegal, and Swansea City winger Moussa Yeo, 22, is also new after scoring three times in his last five club games.

Gaoussou Diakite of Red Bull Salzburg and Fode Doucoure of Nantes return in a 24-man squad that does not include Yves Bissouma, who joined Ajax in late September, with no reason given for his absence.

For the visitors, Constantine trimmed his squad on Monday, November 9, dropping Elie Ganijuru, Kevin Muhire, Taiba Mbonyumwami and goalkeeper Yves Mugisha, while Fidele Uwiyaremye had already been sent home on the first day of camp for disciplinary reasons.

Defender Thierry Manzi and midfielder Jean Bosco Ruboneka are back after missing the September qualifiers, and Bonheur Mugisha, Gilbert Mugisha and Leroy-Jacques Mickels joined the camp on Monday.

Diarra; Traore, O Camara, Guindo, Gassama; Dieng, Sangare, K. Doumbia; Dorgeles, M. Doumbia, Sinayoko

Ntwari; Niyomugabo, Kavita, Mutsinzi, Byiringiro; Bizimana, B. Mugisha; L. Mickels, J. Mickels, G. Mugisha; Biramahire

Mali have not lost to Rwanda in four attempts, and the visitors have not scored against them in either of the last two meetings.

Rwanda's winner in Praia came from a goalkeeping error and they were outshot 19-6 there, while Mali have conceded only Cabral's goal in two games, so chances should be scarce for the Amavubi in Bamako.

Tia's absence removes the scorer of two of Mali's four goals, which is why a narrow margin looks more likely than a repeat of the 3-0 in Kigali in 2021.

Rwanda have scored more than Mali, and with the return leg in Kigali on November 17 a draw in Bamako would suit them.

#1829. When Mauricio Pochettino will take over as Manchester United manager as ‘start date revealed’

Mauricio Pochettino is set to take over as Manchester United manager after Michael Carrick was sacked on Thursday.

The Red Devils parted company with the former midfielder after a run of one win in 11 games in all competitions, with the club mired in the Premier League relegation zone and 17th in the Champions League table.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino has been sounded out as INEOS’ preferred candidate, ahead of other potential options that were previously reported, like Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann.

The Argentine is currently the head coach of the United States, but it was reported by BBC Sport that United were willing to trigger the £7million clause in his contract with US Soccer to bring him to Old Trafford.

It is believed that there is an agreement in principle between United and Pochettino for the 54-year-old to take over the reins from Carrick, but there has been no official indication as of yet.

BBC Sport claims that Pochettino is likely to take up his post by November 19 at the latest, but there remains a level of uncertainty as to whether he will manage the US’ two matches against Panama in the current international break.

The United hierarchy had identified this international window as a chance to assess Carrick’s position as manager, and they pulled the trigger after days of leaked reporting claiming that the ex-England international was to be relieved of his duties following a crisis meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.

As such, it left the Red Devils with a decision to make, and it is understood that they are ‘relaxed’ over the possibility of Pochettino overseeing a last two matches with the US, who face Panama in a double-header.

United’s first game back after the international break is a trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool, which is expected to be their new boss’ first game in charge.

Pavlovic was one of six Serie A players to be called up by the Serbian national team for their UEFA Nations League games against Germany and Greece over the next week. The others were Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, Filip and Aleksandar Stankovic, Lazar Samardzic and Aleksa Terzic.

#1827. Gary Neville tells Mauricio Pochettino to reject Manchester United unless two signings are made

Gary Neville has told Mauricio Pochettino to reject the Manchester United job unless the club promise to sign two defenders in the January transfer window.

With United confirming the sacking of Michael Carrick on Thursday morning, Pochettino is now expected to take over at Old Trafford.

After Sunday’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, United sit 18th in the Premier League table after 10 games, while they are also out of the Carabao Cup following a defeat to Brighton in September.

Pochettino, who has a $10 million (£7.44m) release clause in his contract with the United States Soccer Federation, has already reached an agreement with United over a move to Old Trafford.

However, Neville believes the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager should turn down United unless the club’s hierarchy can issue guarantees over spending in the next two transfer windows.

‘I’ve actually asked for Mauricio Pochettino to be the manager of Manchester United probably for seven or eight years and he’s finally going to get it, a bit late in the day for me but he’s finally going to get it,’ Neville said on Stick to Football.

‘He’s going to be sat in the Anfield dugout a week on Sunday, do we think that this is an appointment that will take Manchester United back to a level whereby over three or five years he can keep his job and he can deliver what Klopp did at Liverpool or what Arteta did at Arsenal where there’s that gradual improvement, that feeling you’re on a journey where something can happen?

‘If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven. He’ll do that with a payoff, so do that in your contract.

‘But secondly, he needs two defenders in January. So he’s got to insist that he gets two defenders in January.

#1826. Manchester United: Biggest winners and losers from Mauricio Pochettino move revealed

Mauricio Pochettino looks set to succeed Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss currently manages the USA national team and is expected to stay in post for their upcoming two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti.

United, though, will push ahead with negotiations for Pochettino after confirming Carrick’s sacking on Thursday and are expected to have him in place ahead of next weekend’s trip to Liverpool.

Pochettino will have a huge task on his hands should he take the reins, with United in the relegation zone and without a Premier League win since August.

Their squad, a mismatch of profiles and tactical fits from different managers, is also in desperate need of an overhaul, and Pochettino, with his own strictly defined style, will have ideas about who he wants to keep and who will be shown the door.

With that in mind, Standard Sport has identified the potential winners and losers from Pochettino’s imminent appointment at Old Trafford.

Despite playing an important role in United’s resurgence towards the end of last season, Patrick Dorgu has found his minutes restricted this term.

When Pochettino will take over Man Utd as ‘start date revealed’

Tuchel issues England future latest as Pochettino set for Man Utd

Angry Man Utd fans react to Carrick sacking as new statement sent

The 22-year-old is an exciting attacking outlet but has increasingly earned a reputation as a defensive liability.

That, coupled with a hamstring injury, saw him fall out of favour under Carrick, but there could be an opportunity for the Danish left-back if Pochettino is appointed.

Pochettino has tended to deploy explosive attacking full-backs during his managerial career, and Dorgu’s physicality and instinctive attacking movement make him an unpredictable presence in the final third.

Dorgu is a raw but talented player, and Pochettino might enjoy the challenge of moulding him into a more rounded full-back while still utilising his attacking capabilities.

Massively underutilised since his breakthrough season under Erik ten Hag, Kobbie Mainoo is the sort of young, mobile presence Pochettino would be looking for in midfield.

The epicentre of Pochettino’s Spurs side was Mousa Dembele, who was lauded for his ability to withstand pressure and carry the ball from deep.

Those are attributes Mainoo has in abundance, and while his minutes have been limited over the last few seasons, his ability is not in question, and he would surely benefit from Pochettino’s nurturing personality.

In the absence of Mainoo and the injured Carlos Baleba, Man Utd’s midfield lacks pace, mobility and ingenuity.

That is a problem Pochettino will be keen to fix straight away, and he would be best served by reintegrating Mainoo rather than looking to the transfer market for solutions.

Mateus Cunha has a difficult profile to nail down, and that makes him a problem for defenders but also an issue for whoever is tasked with fitting him into their tactical setup.

Not quite a striker and not quite a No10, Cunha has shown glimpses of his quality at United and has the intensity and character to deliver under pressure.

His inconsistency is what lets him down at times, though, and he needs a manager who plays to his strengths and allows him the freedom to drift fluidly across the frontline.

Pochettino could be that coach, having played a pivotal role in developing Dele Alli into a uniquely talented player at Tottenham.

Dele was not just a goalscorer, but a ball carrier, creator and link man that got the best out of Harry Kane.

Cunha has the talent to be all those things for United. He just needs the guidance of a manager such as Pochettino to realise his ability.

Luke Shaw may have been given his break under Pochettino when the pair were at Southampton, but 14 years after first coming to prominence, the game has moved on.

Shaw, for all his talent, has been broken by injuries and simply can’t be relied upon to perform the responsibilities Pochettino needs from his full-backs.

United have been patient with Shaw, as his body has let him down time and time again, but it is now best for all parties if he moves on at the end of his contract.

If United are to get Pochettino’s appointment right, then they simply have to make these sorts of ruthless decisions.

Another player who should have left United years ago. Harry Maguire is a strong leader and a resilient character, but he simply is not and has not been good enough for United.

The 33-year-old should take some credit for how he saved his United career after being booed relentlessly by his own fans, but given the club’s situation, there is no space for sentimentality, and Pochettino would be wise to inform Maguire to look for a move away.

In Leny Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt, fitness permitting, United have two centre-backs who complement each other well and have enough years ahead of them to form a partnership under Pochettino.

Despite only arriving at the club over the summer, Youri Tielemans has struggled with the step up at United and has routinely been exposed for his lack of mobility.

A talented ball player, Tielemans’ best attributes are not particularly well suited to the style Pochettino likes to play, and he could be moved aside as United search for more pace and energy in the middle of the park.

With everyone fit and available, Mainoo and Baleba feel like the most complete midfield pairing United have at their disposal.

Tielemans, meanwhile, is an unorthodox fit for a team that lacks an identity in possession and will likely resort to a high-energy, transitional style in the first few weeks and months post-Carrick.

#1825. Mauricio Pochettino will ditch four Man Utd stars – the winners and losers under new boss

Mauricio Pochettino is poised to take the reins at Manchester United in the club’s latest attempt to reset the clock.

Having been regarded as a genuine candidate for the job at Old Trafford on three occasions in the past, the Argentine now gets his chance in Manchester where United’s situation is more dire than ever.

With Michael Carrick’s exit confirmed, Pochettino will inherit a squad that has been routinely booed off the pitch by a fanbase thoroughly disenchanted with a lack of effort on it. While there may be hopes of recruitment in the January transfer window, Pochettino will have to work with what he has at his disposal until then.

Metro looks across the United squad to identify whose prospects look brighter than ever with the new manager en route – and those who face the axe.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

With Benjamin Sesko starting just two matches this season before injury struck again, Bryan Mbeumo has spent most of the campaign operating up top. He could remain in that role until Sesko is fit again but both he and Matheus Cunha stand to benefit in their natural positions under the new regime.

Pochettino has favoured inverted wingers to help create overloads in the middle with Cunha in particular tailor made for that role.

Moussa Dembele evolved into one of the Premier League’s most dominant midfielders at Tottenham under Pochettino, carrying on the work started by Martin Jol at Fulham with the Belgian. Kobbie Mainoo lacks Dembele’s outstanding athleticism but his press resistance and running power with the ball will be regarded as key assets for Pochettino.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Mainoo does not have the constant high-energy output Pochettino has traditionally demanded of his midfielders but he has improved his engine over the last two years and his ability to break the lines could also see him play a key role.

Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick all lauded the qualities of Mason Mount despite injuries ensuring they never saw the best of him. Pochettino could be another to look favourably upon him if he can prove his fitness.

When in negotiations with Chelsea back in 2023, Pochettino was eager for the club to end a contract stand-off with the midfielder and was desperate to keep him and make him a key component of his rebuild west London. His own arrival came too late to revive negotiations however with Mount joining United that summer.

Mount’s work rate has never been in doubt and his abilities to run off the ball or intelligently drop into space could be vital. But with just one start in the Premier League this season, the same old doubts are in place.

In October, former United captain Gary Neville called time on the Mainoo-Youri Tielemans partnership, neither dynamic or athletic enough to last the course in the Premier League. There may only be one winner with the Belgian perhaps most at risk.

Tielemans is adept in keeping possession and progressing play but his lack of drive up the pitch is seemingly at odds with how Pochettino likes to set up his midfield. Pochettino was also said to have turned down the chance to sign the midfielder on at least one occasion after his name was put forward by the Tottenham board.

The same concerns for Tielemans could also apply for another summer recruit in Andrey Santos who looks to be another passive operator based on evidence to date.

The emphasis Pochettino puts on his full-backs has been huge during his time in the Premier League but it is the area of the pitch where United are perhaps at their weakest. Diogo Dalot’s shortcomings on the right continue to be exposed while a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw is well overdue.

Dalot’s prospects are brighter – while his final ball is consistently short of the required standard, his ability to get up and down the pitch will be important. Shaw can no longer offer that kind of service on the left and Pochettino may favour the energy of Patrick Dorgu.

Pochettino helped nurture Shaw at Southampton before his £27million move to Manchester in 2014 but the 31-year-old will now struggle to provide the intensity the role demands.

United’s defence has been an utter mess and with the exception of perhaps Leny Yoro, all should consider their futures uncertain. But at 34, Maguire is perhaps the most at risk.

Pochettino favours a high defensive line, requiring centre-halves with pace to live with it. Maguire will turn 34 in March and has been at the heart of a backline that has conceded 19 goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Pochettino may favour the younger legs of Yoro and Ayden Heaven while Lisandro Martinez’s ability to build from the back could keep him in the picture for now.

#1824. Slovakia vs Faroe Islands - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 23:07, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 05:09

Kosicka Futbalova Arena will be the backdrop for a crucial showdown between two unbeaten teams in UEFA Nations League C's Group 3 on Friday, when Slovakia host Faroe Islands.

The Falcons could earn a fourth win in five games, though Landslidid will be motivated by the possibility of promotion.

Vladimir Weiss's Slovakia have produced an impressive campaign in the Nations League, and head into this week's showdown on the cusp of ascension to League B.

The Falcons kicked off their group action with a 2-0 win over Moldova on September 26, which they followed up three days later by beating Kazakhstan 2-1, making it six points from six on home turf.

Weiss's side also hammered Moldova 4-0 in their most recent outing on October 6, though they were held to a 1-1 draw by Friday's opponents prior - the only match the country have failed to triumph in so far.

Ten points from four games have put Slovakia in a commanding position at the top of Nations League Group C3, six clear of second-placed Faroe Islands.

Additionally, the Falcons - who have won four of their last five when playing as the hosts - know that even a draw would be enough to see them secure promotion with room to spare.

Meanwhile, Eydun Klakstein's Faroe Islands may be ranked 126th in the world by FIFA compared to Slovakia's 46th, but they will be cautiously optimistic ahead of this clash.

Landslidid are widely known as international strugglers, but they arrive on the back of a five-game unbeaten run, having yet to taste defeat in this edition of the Nations League.

That remarkable feat has Klakstein's men second in the table, sat in the promotion playoff spot and eyeing an improbable rise through the divisions.

On the other hand, it is notable that Faroe Islands have not come out on top in any of their four Nations League contests so far, even if they remain undefeated, drawing 2-2 with Kazakhstan last time out.

Likewise, Friday's visitors are level on four points with third-placed Moldova, who could usurp them given they are set to face bottom-of-the-pile Kazakhstan.

Slovakia will be lighter in midfield than ideal without Stanislav Lobotka (ankle) and the versatile Tomas Suslov (hamstring), though Peter Pokorny could be joined by Tomas Rigo and Ondrej Duda in the centre of the park.

Further forward, Middlesbrough's David Strelec may lead the attack, supported from out wide by Tomas Bobcek and Lukas Haraslin.

As for Faroe Islands, they are missing Mjallby left wing-back Martin Agnarsson, who is suspended after being sent off against Kazakhstan.

Filling the gaps this week, Klakstein could opt for Samuel Johansen Chukwudi on the left flank, with Joannes Kalso Danielsen on the right.

Elsewhere, Petur Knudsen should be on hand to start up top, supplied by Aki Samuelsen and Hanus Sorensen.

Greif; Mesik, Skriniar, Obert, Hancko; Rigo, Pokorny, Duda; Bobcek, Strelec, Haraslin

Lamhauge; Faero, Vatnhamar, Edmundsson; Danielsen, Turi, Bjartalid, Chukwudi; Samuelsen, Knudsen, Sorensen

Slovakia are the favourites owing to the superior quality in their squad, and their 81-better FIFA ranking, though they are unlikely to pull off a second consecutive thrashing.

Faroe Islands are the only nation that have caused the Falcons to drop points in Group C3, so expect to see another close-fought contest between two unbeaten sides.

#1823. Alan Shearer hails Arsenal star as the early ‘player of the season’ in the Premier League

Alan Shearer has hailed Arsenal summer signing Ezri Konsa as the early ‘player of the season’ in the Premier League.

Konsa completed a £55m move to Arsenal over the summer after ending his seven-year spell at Aston Villa.

The England defender won the Europa League at Villa Park but has bigger ambitions with reigning Premier League champions and Champions League finalists Arsenal.

Konsa has missed just one game for Arsenal so far this season, helping Mikel Arteta’s side open up a five-point gap at the top of the Premier League and enjoy an impressive start to their European campaign.

The 29-year-old was signed partly due to the absence of William Saliba, who returned from last summer’s World Cup with a serious back injury.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Konsa’s form has led several pundits to question whether Saliba, widely regarded as one of the best defenders in the world, will even get straight back into the Arsenal team.

‘I think the player of the season up to now has been Ezri Konsa,’ Premier League record goalscorer and former England striker Shearer told Betfair.

‘I just think when you look at the performances of Arsenal defensively, and look at his performances defensively, we haven’t even really mentioned them missing William Saliba.

‘The only time we’ve mentioned him is in the last two weeks and that’s because everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in because Konsa has been that good.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Earlier this week Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand said Konsa’s brilliant start at Arsenal had created a ‘problem’ for Arteta.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Mikel Arteta has got a problem, he’s got a huge problem now,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel.

‘What is he going to do when William Saliba is fit? Ezri Konsa has come into that back-four and he looks like he’s been there for ten years.

‘He looks like an immovable object in that team. That’s what it feels like because he’s just slid in there and taken that place. He looks dominant, aggressive and accustomed to wearing the Arsenal shirt.

‘He looks like he belongs there. But let’s not forget about Saliba and what he was doing when he was in the team. It’s a problem but it’s a problem that I hope Mikel Arteta will enjoy because he’s got two top centre-backs vying to be in the team.

‘It’s a good position to be in. I think we will see Konsa sometimes playing right-back.’

Arsenal’s nearest challengers going into the November international break is Brighton, who have won seven of their ten league games to climb to second in the Premier League.

‘Brighton could be Arsenal’s main challenge to the title this season,’ Shearer added.

‘I think Liverpool are in transition. Chelsea, same thing. They still have plenty of work to do with those football clubs.

‘Brighton have been incredible. The football that they’re playing, I mean, in Europe too, whether that will hinder them the longer the season goes on I don’t know, but they’re managing really well at the minute.

‘I don’t think they’re going to go away. I think there’ll be around for the majority of the season.’

Arsenal’s first game back following the international break is a potentially tricky trip to St James’ Park to face Newcastle United.

#1822. Viktor Gyokeres reveals Arsenal transfer stance amid performance criticism

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Viktor Gyokeres has insisted he wants to stay at Arsenal, as he dismissed criticism of his performances.

The striker was the club’s top scorer in his first season at the Emirates Stadium and played his part in the Gunners ending their 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

However, he has looked an uncomfortable fit for this Arsenal side for large periods and Mikel Arteta has consistently favoured Kai Havertz over the Swede in the biggest matches.

The No14 has started only one match in the league for Arsenal this season, missing out on a place in the side even after scoring and assisting against Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

Despite that frustration, Gyokeres was clear when asked by Fotbollskanalen whether he wanted to stay at Arsenal.

“It feels good when I’ve played. We’ve won most of the games. It was a tough loss in the cup [Fleetwood]. Otherwise it’s felt good for myself and the team. I’ve been doing well lately when I’ve been playing. Right now it feels good.

“The communication with Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play. Before a match, if I’m going to start, we talk about the opponents and what I should think about.”

Gyokeres has faced criticism for his performances, particularly early in the season when he had a run of looking well off the pace.

Despite those displays improving, Troy Deeney has been among those to still take aim at the striker, claiming the Arsenal players do not trust Gyokeres to give him the ball on the pitch.

“Sometimes it might get to me, but overall not so much,” Gyokeres said in response to the critics.

“If I score goals and assists in the Champions League, I couldn’t care less what they say.

“It’s nice to do those kinds of performances. To deliver for myself and for the team. That’s where the focus lies.

“It’s natural too. It’s what gets the most headlines and what sticks the most when people listen. I understand that’s how it is.”

#1820. TMW: Milan temptation behind Palladino’s chaotic summer – the reconstruction

A report has revealed some of the background on Raffaele Palladino’s turbulent summer, mentioning AC Milan among other clubs.

TMW have provided a reconstruction of what has been a turbulent past few months for Palladino. Since he took over at Bologna, they have won five of seven games in the league – including at San Siro against Milan – to climb up to eighth in the league.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the summer, Palladino turned down a long-term contract with Atalanta because he was linked with more prestigious jobs, but this left him without a job. Then, when Bologna parted ways with Domenico Tedesco, the Italian took his talents to Reggio Emilia and has not looked back.

Why didn’t he stay in Bergamo? The question arises naturally, considering the results obtained and qualification for the Conference despite a stuttering start. Palladino – after the victory against Borussia Dortmund – was considered the future for La Dea.

There was a contract ready to continue together until 2029, but everything seemed to turn sour. The three-year contract that was then offered to Maurizio Sarri, because Atalanta needed a decision quickly and Palladino wanted time to reflect.

His contract with Atalanta expired in 2027, and he wasn’t in a hurry to sign another. The second thoughts didn’t sit well with Atalanta but Palladino later backtracked, offering to accept the previous contract, even offering to shorten it to 2028.

Meanwhile, Atalanta’s league performance worsened and they failed to reach the Coppa Italia final, against Sarri himself. Relations, now strained, finally broke down.

The truth is that the former Monza coach was waiting to see which vacancies came up. Napoli in particular were a club he was monitoring closely, when Antonio Conte announced his departure. Palladino, along with Vincenzo Italiano, was a strong name.

There could also have been an opportunity at Milan when Massimiliano Allegri departed. However, as is known, the Rossoneri decided to pursue Andoni Iraola and then turned to Ruben Amorim, clearly not inclined to bet on a coach who knows the league. Palladino would have been keen, it seems.

It’s quite a shame neither Italiano nor Palladino got a job at Napoli, instead of the Jurassic dinosaur called Allegri. However, Palladino leaving Atalanta so early was a mistake.

#1819. Liverpool transfer news: New contract 'breakthrough' with Andoni Iraola star while Alexis Mac Allister future still unclear

By Lewis Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 23:25

Liverpool could finalise a new contract for Trey Nyoni in the international break, the latest report has claimed,

The Reds' triumph against Crystal Palace on Sunday left the team fourth in the Premier League, though the Merseysiders were arguably fortunate to concede just once.

Midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai struggled all game, though Andoni Iraola's side looked more assured once Nyoni came on in the second half.

The 19-year-old has played 13 times this season in all competitions, starting six times, and he has been among the club's best performers.

A new report from GIVEMESPORT claims that Liverpool are preparing a new contract to reward the youngster for his displays, and he could extend his terms beyond 2030 in the November international break.

There is an argument that Nyoni should be in the starting XI already, with the youngster having impressed against the likes of Arsenal and Crystal Palace.

The unfortunate reality is that playing the 19-year-old every week could be dangerous as the risk of injury would increase significantly.

If the Reds want to avoid the level of their midfield dropping off in the coming months when Nyoni has to come out of the team, it would be sensible to make an addition in the January transfer window.

Whether Liverpool would sanction a deal for the likes of Alex Scott or Lamine Camara remains to be seen, but both would strengthen Iraola's depth considerably.

The report from GIVEMESPORT also states that there is currently no contract on the table for midfielder Alexis Mac Allister.

Fans have called for the Argentine to be given a new deal given he has excelled for the vast majority of the season, outshining the likes of Szoboszlai on a consistent basis.

Mac Allister will have one year left on his contract at the end of 2026-27, and Liverpool have shown no public signs that they want to extend his stay at Anfield.

Despite the 27-year-old insisting that he would like to stay at Liverpool, supporters may have to prepare themselves for a summer exit.

Carrick was sacked by United on Thursday morning, while Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be appointed ahead of the team’s next Premier League game away to Liverpool on November 22.

After Sunday’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, United sit 18th in the Premier League and are already out of the Carabao Cup after they were beaten by Brighton in September.

Carrick was forced to contend with several injury headaches during his final weeks in charge as United were without Luke Shaw and a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko sidelined until next year due to a shin injury.

#1814. ‘So much quality’ – Morgan Rogers urges Thomas Tuchel to recall Chelsea teammate after Croatia win

Morgan Rogers issued a stern defence of Cole Palmer’s committment to the England squad and urged Thomas Tuchel to recall his Chelsea teammate to the national side.

Rogers was on the scoresheet on Thursday evening as England booked their spot in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 win over Croatia.

The 24-year-old is the only Chelsea player in England’s squad for this international break, with Reece James injured and Palmer not selected by Tuchel after he pulled out of the previous camp due to injury concerns.

Speaking last week, the German suggested that Palmer ‘misses too many opportunities’ to play for his country but has insisted that his latest exclusion was ‘not personal’.

Rogers, though, would like to see his close friend back in the national team set-up and said accusiations that Palmer does not want to play for his country were a ‘lie’.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘He wants to be here,’ Rogers told BBC Radio 5 Live. ‘He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

‘We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he’s been managing them injuries ever since.

‘He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn’t feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. Of course he does, who wouldn’t?

‘But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10/15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It’s a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England.

‘You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don’t get it and he doesn’t get it. But it’s something he has to deal with but I can assure you he wants to be here and he wants to play for his country.’

Asked if he thinks Palmer should be back in the England set-up for the next camp, Rogers continued: ‘Of course I do. What a player he is. What a person he is and it’s someone you want to see in an England shirt.

‘He’s got so much quality, so much ability. We all know what we can do, what he’s done, so of course we want to see him in an England shirt and hopefully sooner rather than later.’

When asked about Rogers’ comments in his post-match press conference, Tuchel said: ‘It’s totally fine. It’s his teammate and his friend so why wouldn’t he make an emotional statement?

‘If he did it, I didn’t hear it so I will not comment on it. All I can say is I was very happy with the emotional and physical commitment of Morgan Rogers – I think he was a standout player today, offensively and defensively and that’s what matters.’

#1813. Burkina Faso vs Mauritania - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 11 Nov 2026 23:36, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 23:36

Burkina Faso will look to make it consecutive Africa Cup of Nations qualifying victories when Mauritania visit Stade du 4-Aout on Friday.

The teams are separated by just one point in a tightly packed Group F, with either side capable of ending matchday three at the summit.

Burkina Faso's consistency at the Africa Cup of Nations has soared in recent years, with eight appearances in the last nine tournaments after missing out in 2008 and 2010.

A 1-1 home draw with Benin and a 1-0 away win over the Central African Republic in their opening two qualifiers have put Moussa Sanogo’s side on course for another AFCON appearance, having collected four points from a possible six.

However, Les Etalons will need to bounce back from a 7-0 friendly defeat to Argentina in October, their joint-heaviest loss, matched only by a similar drubbing against Algeria in 1981.

Back on home turf, where they have not lost a competitive match in nearly a decade, Burkina Faso now aim to move to the top of their qualifying group with a win, or at least keep pace with Benin, who currently lead on goal difference.

Having beaten Mauritania in each of the last three meetings - including most recently in the 2024 Africa Cup of Nations group stage - Friday’s hosts will hope their psychological edge in this fixture aids their quest for maximum points and back-to-back competitive wins for the first time since December 2025.

Mauritania have not lost an opening AFCON qualifier since 2015, and they extended that streak with a 1-0 victory over the Central African Republic at Stade Larbi Zaouli in September. However, a 2-1 defeat to Benin in their next outing snapped their three-match unbeaten run.

Aritz Lopez Garai’s transition from the Under-20s to the senior side has been far from smooth. As the 46-year-old prepares for his 20th match in charge, he has recorded just five victories, giving him a win percentage of just over 26%.

With goals in the 80th minute or later in five consecutive outings, the Lions of Chinguetti have shown a tendency to stay competitive until the final whistle, but they have also struggled early on, conceding first in six of their last eight matches.

Mauritania’s upcoming double-header against Burkina Faso will go a long way in determining their chances of returning to AFCON, having missed out on the most recent edition and ending a run of three consecutive appearances.

Victory on Friday would require the visitors to achieve something they have not managed since June 2023 - win an AFCON qualifier on the road, as their last four away qualifiers have produced just one draw and three defeats.

Burkina Faso Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Mauritania Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Mohamed Ouedraogo is sidelined for Burkina Faso due to injury, but Issa Kabore appears fit to feature despite picking up a knock in his last outing for Wrexham.

In a surprise development, Issoufou Dayo has reversed his international retirement and returned to the Burkina Faso squad.

The centre-back announced his retirement from international football in January following the Africa Cup of Nations, but is now back in contention.

Abderrahmane Sarr and Guessouma Fofana, who last featured for Mauritania in March, have both been recalled by Aritz Lopez Garai.

Aboubakary Koita has recorded two goals and two assists in his last four club matches, and the AEK Athens forward will look to continue his fine form on international duty.

Koffi; Kouassi, E Tapsoba, Djiga, Kabore; Doucet; Zagre, I Ouedraogo, A Tapsoba, Bouda; Traore

Diop; Diaw, Lefort, Ba, Diadie; Ngom, Fofana; Koita, Diallo, Gassama; Camara

Only one of Burkina Faso’s last nine matches has produced fewer than two goals, and there is little to suggest a low-scoring affair is likely here.

Burkina Faso were thoroughly outclassed in their recent meeting with Argentina, but the challenge posed by a weaker Mauritania side on paper should be far more manageable.

France can secure top spot in Nations League Group A1 by winning away in Italy tonight.

#1811. Moretto: Tresoldi ‘arrived at Casa Milan’ to sign but move collapsed – the background

Nicolo Tresoldi could have already been an AC Milan player now, given that he was very close to signing a few years ago.

Tresoldi has found himself in the Milan orbit for a number of reasons in recent weeks. His continued declarations of love for the Rossoneri – his boyhood team – already had some fans clamouring to try and sign him, and that was before his Champions League hat-trick against Inter at San Siro.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the past few days, the speculation has ramped up regarding an attempt by Milan. Not put off by the painful negotiations to sign Charles De Ketelaere and Ardon Jashari, it seems Gerry Cardinale wants to try and sign yet another Brugge star.

Matteo Moretto spoke during a video on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, and he explained that the young striker was even close to signing for Milan previously, while waiting to see what the future holds.

“In the summer of 2021, Tresoldi arrived at Casa Milan because he had every intention of signing for Milan. Milan had already closed on him,” he said (via MilanNews).

“At the time, the Maldini-Massara duo were the ones at the helm. The deal was done, all that was missing was the signatures. Tresoldi didn’t sign that day: he returned to Germany, and Milan never closed the deal.

“In the summer of 2021, Milan came close to signing Tresoldi, but he then extended his contract with Hannover. We’ll see if he can become a popular option for the Rossoneri in the future.”

#1810. Gary Neville sends Mauricio Pochettino plea ahead of Manchester United appointment

Manchester United legend Gary Neville has urged incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino to “protect himself” by demanding reinforcements in the January transfer window.

The Red Devils finally look set to appoint the Argentine almost eight years on from first speaking to the former Tottenham boss about the top job at Old Trafford.

With United sat in the Premier League relegation zone after 10 games, Michael Carrick was sacked, paving the way for Pochettino to take over in the north west.

But Neville has issued a warning to the newest managerial appointment, claiming Pochettino must receive guarantees of investment in the next few transfer windows.

Speaking on The Overlap’s Stick to Football, Neville said: “I’m sure Mauricio Pochettino is doing this, but if you were coming into this job now - you’ve talked about don’t believe an owner on the way in about what they’re going to spend, moving the goalposts - if I were Mauricio Pochettino now, I would literally be protecting myself to the high heaven.

“He’ll do that with the payoff. But secondly, he needs two defenders in January. So he’s got to insist that he gets two defenders in January.

“He’s got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer window to be able to turn this around.”

United have largely restricted their major overhauls to summer transfer windows in recent seasons, attempting to improve their strikeforce in 2025 before bringing in midfield reinforcements this year.

The Red Devils have not signed a senior defender since Patrick Dorgu arrived at the club in January 2025, and Neville insists that the backline must be improved in the next transfer window.

“He’s got to insist that he gets a budget the following season,” Neville continued.

“He’s got to literally insist. They have to give it to him, otherwise he shouldn’t take the job. With that defence - and that midfield by the way, that midfield’s had some money spent on it - he’s got to insist on the way in that there’s some form of transfer control, that there’s some form of budget there that he knows he can meaningfully change the team.

“I don’t think Mauricio is the type of manager either that would say ‘give me half a billion’. I don’t think he is that type of guy. I think he’s someone a bit more responsible and will look at things, and he’ll want to bring players through, and he’ll want to develop young players.

“I just think he needs to protect himself in the next 12 months with the transfer budget.

“The only time you can insist upon it is at the very beginning. They need two defenders in January - because if they have [Patrick] Dorgu at left-back, Mazaroui at right-back, and [Ayden] Heaven and [Leny] Yoro at centre-back, he will need to do a hell of a lot of coaching to get them up the league.”

#1809. Nigeria vs Tanzania - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 11 Nov 2026 23:51

Nigeria host Tanzania in Uyo on Friday knowing that they have little room for further mistakes in their bid to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

A disastrous outing in Bissau on matchday two has left the Super Eagles second in Group L, three points behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, while Tanzania sit bottom despite already having a place at the tournament proper as co-hosts.

After missing out on the 2026 World Cup by losing the African playoff to DR Congo, falling short in another major tournament would be a bitter disappointment for Nigerian fans, especially with their team now in a delicate position in the AFCON qualifiers.

With one of the qualification places already secured by Friday's opponents, who will co-host the tournament alongside Kenya and Uganda, the Super Eagles must collect maximum points to improve their chances of finishing top of the group following a mixed start to the campaign.

After coming from behind to beat Madagascar 2-1 in their opening fixture, Eric Chelle's side suffered a 3-0 defeat against Guinea-Bissau, with Franculino Dju, Mama Balde and Alvaro Djalo all finding the net to hand Nigeria their heaviest loss in the fixture.

The Super Eagles have now recorded just one victory in their last five internationals (D2, L2) and have failed to keep a clean sheet during that period, which also includes a 3-3 comeback draw away to Russia in a friendly on October 6.

Under pressure to turn things around, Chelle has insisted that Nigeria must take maximum points from both meetings with Tanzania, with anything less likely to make their qualification task more difficult ahead of the return fixture in Zanzibar four days after Friday's encounter.

However, Uyo has proved a more reliable setting for Nigeria, who have won their last three matches at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, including September's victory over Madagascar.

Already assured of a place at the 2027 tournament as co-hosts, Tanzania arrive with less pressure than their opponents, although they will be hoping to claim their first-ever victory over Nigeria.

The Taifa Stars have drawn two and lost four of their previous six meetings with the Super Eagles, including a 2-1 defeat when the two nations met on matchday one of the 2025 AFCON.

Recent form suggests that Tanzania could struggle again on Friday, having recorded just one victory in their last 15 matches across all competitions (D5, L9), with their only success during that run coming in a 6-0 friendly victory over Macao in March's FIFA Series.

Miguel Angel Gamondi's side have since made a difficult start to their qualifying campaign, drawing 1-1 with Madagascar after losing their opening fixture 2-0 to Guinea-Bissau, and will be eager to end that winless run in Uyo.

Nigeria Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Tanzania Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Nigeria will be without Victor Osimhen, who is recovering from knee surgery, and Samuel Chukwueze, who is still working his way back from hip surgery.

Semi Ajayi has joined the squad after suffering a cramp-related scare during Hull City's defeat to Arsenal, although his fitness still needs to be assessed, while Moses Usor has retained his place in the selection despite reports of a knock.

George Ilenikhena, who scored on his Super Eagles debut against Madagascar, is also unavailable after Chelle revealed that the 20-year-old Al-Ittihad striker was left out because of fitness concerns.

As such, Taiwo Awoniyi and Akor Adams could lead the line in the manager’s favoured 4-4-2 diamond, though Tolu Arokodare remains an option.

Maduka Okoye and Kelechi Iheanacho are among the notable omissions, while Francis Uzoho has been recalled and Mubarak Suleiman receives his first senior call-up.

Tanzania will be without Clement Mzize and Dickson Job, who have withdrawn from the squad through injury, with Iddi Nado called up as a replacement.

Captain Mbwana Samatta has not been included in the 24-man selection, while Aishi Manula is likely to start in goal and Simon Msuva could lead the attack.

Nigeria have struggled for consistency in recent matches, but their strong home record and superior head-to-head results should give them the confidence to take control in Uyo, and we expect the Super Eagles to secure all three points.
