#1793. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who said: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke said: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”

"100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers says he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla

Here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he said: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”

On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady said on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the big guns came on... They were electric at times.”

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

Chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

Shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

It will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

Palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

Chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

Big cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:

Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1

Boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

There is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

Gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

Farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

Big chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

Leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu launches a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

"The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56

Barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

There is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as big as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

Big chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

Gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

Leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

Although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

Chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Daniel Farke believes Leeds can go far in the Carabao Cup this year 💪 pic.twitter.com/26ueAAUHoZ

On the Brazilian winger’s opportunity tonight, Hasselbaink said on Sky Sports: “He has to find his place. This is his opportunity... It’s not really an out-and-out left-wing [position] or a No 10 as he can play, but [with] good players it doesn’t matter where you put them on the pitch. He will find his spaces and he will be direct as he was when he came in against Arsenal. He is going to play for his place because he wants to play week-in, week-out.”

"He deserves to be there because of what he has shown" Xabi Alonso speaks about Reggie Watson with the 16-year-old set to make his Chelsea debut in their Carabao Cup game against Leeds 🌟 pic.twitter.com/AAn4Av3iEh

Tfl has closed South Kensington station after a “customer incident” meaning parts of the District Line have closed. The decision was then made to delay the match to give supporters more time to get to the stadium.

Reggie Watson will become the fourth youngest player, aged 16, in Chelsea’s history. But he will have to wait a little bit longer for his debut as kick-off has been delayed by 15 minutes to 8.15pm.

There will be a 15 minute delay to kick-off for our Carabao Cup third round tie with Leeds United tonight. The match will now begin at 20:15 BST. pic.twitter.com/MdDXpxgW09

A couple of cracking strikes from the Dutchman. Some player he was...

"Good old days!" Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reflects on his goals for Leeds against Chelsea 🎞️ pic.twitter.com/bYjyFYIVIK

ChelseaAug 24: Fulham 2 Chelsea 3Aug 27: Chelsea 2 Luton Town 0 (Carabao Cup)Aug 30: Chelsea 4 Brighton 3Sep 6: Arsenal 2 Chelsea 1

LeedsAug 22: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Aug 25: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 2Aug 30: Leeds 1 Brentford 1Sep 5: Brighton 1 Leeds 1

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

Asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke said: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”

Tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard said of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”

Reggie Watson, 16, son of former Wigan midfielder Ben (of 2013 FA Cup final fame), makes his full Chelsea debut and becomes the club’s fourth youngest player. Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck replace Alonso’s thrilling forward three, who are on the bench.

Chelsea XI Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Your Blues to face Leeds United in the #CarabaoCup! #CFC pic.twitter.com/636SOiUXVB

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

#1791. Johan Manzambi injury update as Aston Villa star sent home from international duty

Johan Manzambi has been forced to withdraw from Switzerland duty due to injury, raising concerns over the midfielder’s availability for Aston Villa in the coming weeks.

A £60million summer signing from Freiburg, Manzambi has returned to Aston Villa for further assessments on a calf issue.

According to the Swiss football federation, Manzambi joined up with the national team already carrying a knock which is said to have been sustained during Aston Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United.

Manzambi was forced off at Old Trafford in the 78th minute following a strong challenge from Manchester United defender Leny Yoro.

Despite the knock, Manzambi was still called up for Switzerland’s Nations League games against Slovenia and Scotland. But it has now been decided not to risk the 21-year-old, with Manzambi sent back to Villa to continue his recovery.

A statement from the Swiss FA read: “Johan Manzambi has been ruled out of the upcoming Nations League matches against Slovenia and Scotland.

“The midfielder joined the national team camp on Monday with a calf injury.

“Despite intensive medical treatment and further examinations, his condition has not improved sufficiently, making him unavailable for either game.

“In agreement with Aston Villa, Manzambi will therefore return to his club on Friday.”

Manzambi has quickly established himself in Unai Emery’s team, producing two goals and three assists in six Premier League starts this term.

#1790. Lens dismiss Cahuzac after record Champions League hammering

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Lens have dismissed head coach Yannick Cahuzac after a turbulent start to November, including a record Champions League defeat.

Cahuzac was in the dugout as Como hammered Lens 9-1 earlier this month in Europe.

That marked the largest home defeat in the competition's history, while the eight-goal margin also matched the overall record (Liverpool 8-0 Besiktas in 2007 and Real Madrid 8-0 Malmo in 2015).

In fact, the thrashing by Como was the joint-heaviest loss by a French club in major European competition, alongside Strasbourg's 10-2 loss at MTK Budapest way back in 1961.

No French side had previously lost a major European home match by more than five goals, and Lens followed that up by losing 2-1 to Marseille last Sunday in Ligue 1 amid protests from their home supporters.

Lens 1-9 Como (2026) Real Madrid 8-0 Malmö (2015) Liverpool 8-0 Beşiktaş (2007) Como making history #UCL https://t.co/mSbmhcLpHG

— UEFA Champions League (@ChampionsLeague) November 4, 2026

Lens announced their decision to remove Cahuzac on Thursday with a short statement.

"Racing Club de Lens announces that Yannick Cahuzac has been relieved of his duties as head of the first team," the club said.

"Called upon to assume this responsibility without a predetermined deadline, Yannick Cahuzac accompanied the professional group during a transition period in which he put all his energy and commitment at the service of Racing.

"The club thanks its former captain and coach for his commitment and the work accomplished, and wishes him every success in the continuation of his professional career."

Cahuzac is already the second manager Lens have sacked this season, with Dino Toppmoller dismissed back in September after just six games in charge – including a Trophee des Champions victory over Paris Saint-Germain.

Lens sit 11th in Ligue 1 before they return to action after the international break at home to Toulouse on November 21.

#1789. Montserrat vs Nicaragua - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 05:55

With a place in the preliminary round of the 2027 Gold Cup at stake, Montserrat will host Nicaragua for the first leg of their CONCACAF Nations League play-in showdown at Estadio Cibao, kicking off at midnight UK time on Friday.

The Emerald Boys are in excellent form after four wins on the bounce, while the Blue and White struggled in the group stage, suffering four defeats.

Gabriel Calderon's Montserrat are the underdogs on paper, owing to the fact they are the entrants into this play-in from League C, but they have put together an impressive campaign so far.

The Emerald Boys won all four of their clashes in League C's Group A, topping the table with 12 points after four games and qualifying for this tie as the highest-ranked nation in their league.

Calderon's side kicked off with a 2-0 victory over Turks and Caicos Islands, and after successive 3-0 and 2-0 triumphs against the British Virgin Islands, hammered Turks and Caicos 4-1 on home turf on October 6.

That flawless streak of wins saw Montserrat score 11 times and concede just once, a defensive record that could be crucial on Friday.

However, it remains to be seen whether the 172nd-ranked nation can maintain that level of solidity up against an opponent 35 places better in FIFA's ratings.

Meanwhile, Juan Cruz Real's Nicaragua have endured a dire Nations League term, failing to avoid defeat even once to date.

The Blue and White finished at the bottom of League A's Group A with zero points to their name, and arrive for this first leg having last earned a victory back in November 2025, when they beat Honduras 2-0 in a World Cup qualifier.

Real's men were downed 3-2 by the Dominican Republic on matchday one of the group stage, falling two goals behind within the first 15 minutes, before fighting back to 2-2 only to see Porto's Pablo Rosario snatch the points with a 97th-minute dagger.

That demoralising loss set the tone for Nicaragua, who followed up with a 6-1 battering by Curacao, a 3-0 thrashing by Costa Rica, and another defeat to the Dominican Republic last time out - 2-1 on October 5.

Looking ahead to Friday's showdown, fans of the visitors will be most concerned by the fact their team conceded 14 goals across just four group matches while netting only four of their own.

With that defensive frailty in mind, manager Real will be desperate to avoid accruing a first-leg deficit that may put the tie beyond Nicaragua before they can dig in for the second leg on home turf.

Hoping to keep up their impressive defensive record, Montserrat look set to start Trent Carter-Rogers in goal, shielded by a centre-back partnership of Nico Gordon and Reading's Jeriel Dorsett.

At the opposite end of the pitch, captain Lyle Taylor should be ready to lead the line, joined in a strike partnership by Ashley Boatswain of Gateshead, while being supported from out wide by Brandon Barzey and the versatile Lenni Cirino.

As for Nicaragua, a five-man backline featuring Justing Cano, Marvin Fletes and Juan Luis Perez at its core is likely to operate in front of San Carlos shot-stopper Jason Vega Carmona.

Joab Gutierrez and Emmanuel Gomez are expected to start as the visitors' wingbacks, aiming to provide width for the attack as well as cover for what has been a vulnerable defence so far in the Nations League.

Elsewhere, Jaime Moreno Ciorciari of Finnish side KuPS will line up as a lone striker, aided by Efrain Mejia and Raheem Cole.

Carter-Rodgers; Kirnon, Gordon, Dorsett, Townsend-West; Barzey, Comley, Dyer, Cirino; Taylor, Boatswain

Vega Carmona; Gutierrez, Cano, Fletes, Perez, Gomez; R Cole, Moncada, K Cole, Mejia; Moreno Ciorciari

Montserrat proved more than capable of dominating opponents during the group stage, and will be confident of continuing that trend this week.

By contrast, Nicaragua will be low on confidence after suffering a number of damaging defeats to this point, and keeping the scoreline down may be their aim for the first leg.

#1788. Harry Kane becomes England’s most-capped men’s player with 126th appearance

Harry Kane has broken the all-time record for the most appearances by an England men’s player.

By leading his country out against Croatia on Thursday evening, alongside his four children, the England captain overtook Peter Shilton’s long-standing record to move top of the all-time caps list with his 126th appearance.

Shilton was involved in a commemorative tribute to Kane before kick-off in the Nations League game at Wembley, before Prince William presented him with a signed ‘126’ shirt.

The 33-year-old’s tribute before the match also included him parading his Ballon d’Or trophy in front of the Wembley crowd. It is the first time the award for best player has been on English soil since Kane was crowned its winner at the London Palladium 17 days ago.

Kane is already the top scorer in the history of the national team, having netted 91 goals in 125 caps before taking the field against Croatia on Thursday evening.

The skipper has said he wants to “set a challenge” for future England players to beat his caps record.

Midfielders Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice boast 60 and 80 caps at the ages of 23 and 27, respectively, and Kane said on Wednesday: “Look at how young they are, I will try and give them a good number to catch.”

Billy Wright and Bobby Moore shared the record for the most England caps as captain for decades, having each led the Three Lions out 90 times. But having overtaken that record earlier this year, Kane is now on cap 98 as skipper, and is expected to reach a century next year.

The final of four matches during the last international break saw England defeat Czechia 3-0 with two goals from Kane and the other, an own goal, having been set up by the captain.

After the match, Bellingham said of Kane: “He is the best England player to ever wear the shirt and it is an honour to play with him.” England head coach Thomas Tuchel recently admitted he had “run out of superlatives” with which to describe Kane.

#1786. England vs Croatia LIVE: Nations League latest score, match stream, goal updates

All eyes will be on Harry Kane tonight as England host Croatia in their penultimate Nations League game. The Three Lions skipper tonight makes history as the record appearance-maker for the men’s senior team, with his 126th cap. He overtakes Peter Shilton, whose final game for England came at the 1990 World Cup.

It is yet another staggering achievement for Kane, who has already shattered the goal record with 91 strikes to date, which is 38 more than previous holder Wayne Rooney. Kane also tonight leads his country out as captain for the 98th time, which is eight more than Billy Wright and Bobby Moore.

Kane paraded the Ballon d’Or trophy, won 17 days ago down the road at the London Palladium, ahead of kick-off, before full focus was on another win over Croatia as they look to hunt down Spain and top their Nations League group. Follow the game LIVE below with our dedicated match blog, featuring expert insight and analysis from Dom Smith and Sam Tabuteau at Wembley.

86min: Garner thinks he has scored his first England goal, but Bellingham is offside in the build-up.

England’s support have not had an awful lot to get roused by tonight, but they let White know their feelings.

#1785. Thursday's UEFA Nations League predictions including England vs. Croatia, Italy vs. France

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 00:05, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 08:54

Today's UEFA Nations League predictions include England's clash with Croatia at Wembley, and a contest between Italy and France.

Armenia welcome Cyprus to the Vazgen Sargsyan Republican Stadium on Thursday evening for their penultimate League C fixture in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, the Collectives played out a goalless draw with Montenegro at the Podgorica City Stadium, while the Blue and Whites claimed a narrow 2-1 victory over Latvia in Nicosia.

With their form slipping in recent matches and a gap beginning to open up between themselves and the promotion places, it is imperative that Armenia claim all three points against Cyprus if they are to have even the slightest chance of competing in League B when the 2028-29 Nations League campaign gets underway.

However, with the Blue and Whites enjoying a promising run of form and also chasing down Montenegro in the race for automatic promotion, we believe Armenia’s hopes of progressing will run their course on Thursday as the visitors to take all three points in Yerevan.

Seeking to strengthen their hopes of qualifying for the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, Belgium travel to Gursel Aksel Stadium in Izmir to face Turkey in their penultimate League A Group 1 fixture on Thursday evening.

While the hosts’ fate is all but sealed, the visitors currently sit third in the group and are playing catch up behind both France and Italy heading into their remaining two matches this week.

Turkey will be desperate for an immediate manager bounce under Yalcin as they look to kick-start their survival bid, but Belgium are rightfully regarded as favourites following their comfortable three-goal victory over the Crescent-Stars last month.

Boosted by the return of a few key players, the Red Devils should possess enough firepower to breach a leaky Turkish backline and are well-placed to claim three important points on the road.

Albania could secure promotion from League C of the Nations League by beating visitors Finland at Arena Kombetare on Thursday.

The hosts are first in their four-team group with nine points from a possible 12, whereas Finland are third with seven points and could be eliminated if they lose.

Thursday's clash will almost certainly be closely fought, and both teams will likely create opportunities.

However, it is difficult to ignore Finland's inconsistencies on the road, and given Albania have improved considerably at home, the hosts should be seen as favourites at Arena Kombetare.

Belarus make the trip to San Marino on Thursday evening looking for the win that could see them end the night sitting in top spot of Group C1 in the UEFA Nations League.

Meanwhile, San Marino head into the game in Serravalle assured of bottom spot having lost all four of their matches.

As with the other games involving San Marino, we expect this to be largely one-way traffic. However, the minnows may be able to restrict Belarus to a goal in each half to add some respectability to the result.

Hoping to secure promotion back to League B, Montenegro welcome strugglers Latvia to Stadion Pod Goricom for a UEFA Nations League C clash on Thursday night.

Hrabri Sokoli enjoyed an unbeaten start to the current cycle during the September/October international window, whereas 11 Vilki are still searching for their maiden success of the competition.

With expectations on the rise following a good start to the Nations League campaign, Montenegro will be confident of beating Latvia on home soil this week.

The visitors face a daunting trip to Podgorica this week and are likely to suffer a fourth defeat of the section.

Two heavyweights will clash at one of football's grandest arenas on Thursday evening, as Italy and France meet for their penultimate League A Group 1 game in the UEFA Nations League.

After a 1-1 draw in Paris earlier this season, the pair resume their campaigns at San Siro, where victory would confirm top spot for Les Bleus.

Though Italy's big rebuild has started with some promise, the Azzurri's defence still looks vulnerable against top-notch opposition.

Furthermore, following almost a century without defeat in Milan, their recent results at San Siro have been very mixed.

Given that context, a strong France side can make it four wins from five in Group 1, comfortably booking their place in the knockout phase.

Already-qualified Spain will continue their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign with a contest against already-eliminated Czech Republic on Thursday night.

La Roja are currently top of Group A3, three points ahead of second-placed England, while Czech Republic are fourth, losing all four of their matches in the section.

Even without Yamal, Spain should be too strong for their opponents on Thursday - it has been a tough campaign for Czech Republic, and we are struggling to back them to secure a positive result here.

One point away from progressing to the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, England's penultimate League A Group 3 fixture sees Croatia rock up to Wembley on Thursday evening.

Thomas Tuchel has masterminded three straight triumphs in the tournament, whereas his opposite number Slaven Bilic has overseen three consecutive defeats, including the infamous 7-0 slaughter at the hands of the Three Lions.

The days of Croatia giving England a rough ride are over, and the Chequered Ones head to Wembley having kept just one clean sheet in their last 14 fixtures across all competitions.

A repeat of October's sensational seven-goal triumph is surely off the cards regardless, but we still have total faith in Tuchel's men to seal their quarter-final spot in style.

#1784. Arsenal’s Ben White again booed by England fans as animosity continues

Ben White was notably booed by a section of England fans when being substituted on during Thursday’s Nations League clash at home to Croatia.

The Arsenal defender was similarly greeted by the Three Lions faithful in March, when he made his first appearance after an almost four-year squad exile.

White left the England squad midway through the 2022 World Cup in Qatar for personal reasons. He did not play again during Gareth Southgate’s time in charge.

Thomas Tuchel is keen to reintegrate White, who was injured during the last international window, but restored to the squad ahead of this month’s Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

White conducted an interview earlier this week in which he said England’s supporters would not boo him if they knew the full story behind his abrupt exit from the World Cup.

#1783. ​Women’s Super League predictions: Chelsea backed to edge top-of-the-table showdown

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

The Women's Super League table is starting to take shape as the campaign reaches its 10th matchday, and there are plenty of intriguing fixtures on the schedule this week.

Manchester City replaced Chelsea at the top of the tree last week, as the defending champions routed West Ham 5-0 and Sonia Bompastor's Blues were held to a frustrating draw by Everton.

And as City and Chelsea prepare to go head-to-head at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, both teams have a chance to land an early blow in the title race.

London City Lionesses are lurking in third ahead of the weekend's action, and they are involved in one of three derbies to take place on Sunday.

While Alexia Putellas and company face Arsenal in another star-studded clash, there is also a second city derby between Aston Villa and Birmingham City, and an East London grudge match between West Ham and Charlton Athletic.

But who will be the winners and losers? With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we delve into the pre-match insights.

How the #BarclaysWSL table looks after Matchweek 9  Which result had the biggest impact on the standings?  #LeagueStandings | #WTWKicks https://t.co/a69A5f6R6Y

— Barclays Women's Super League (@BarclaysWSL) November 8, 2026

The Progress with Unity Stadium hosts the early kick-off on Saturday, with Manchester United hoping to continue their revival under Eva Olid.

After going unbeaten in their last 11 games in all competitions (W8 D3), United could equal their club-record unbeaten streak, having enjoyed sequences of 12 matches without losing ending in March 2023 and February 2026.

They are assigned a 71.8% chance of beating Crystal Palace – the highest win probability assigned to any team on MD10.

The Eagles' hopes of an away win are rated at a mere 12%, and United are the only team to face newly promoted sides more than twice in the WSL and never lose such a game, winning all 15 of those matches by an aggregate score of 43-5.

Palace should be buoyed by their 3-2 victory over Charlton on MD9, but this will be Palace's 32nd match in the WSL, and they are yet to win consecutive games.

The weekend's headline fixture takes place shortly afterwards at Stamford Bridge, as Chelsea and Manchester City go head-to-head for top spot.

This is the first WSL season to see two teams remain unbeaten after nine matchdays since 2020-21 (Chelsea and Man Utd on that occasion).

And this will be the third instance of two unbeaten sides meeting at least 10 matchdays into a campaign, after 2020-21 (Chelsea 2-1 United on MD11) and 2018-19 (City 2-0 Arsenal on MD10).

Chelsea suffered their joint-second-heaviest WSL defeat when they last met City in February, going down 5-1 at the Etihad Stadium with the since-departed Kerolin scoring a hat-trick. However, the Blues have not lost back-to-back league games against the Citizens since a run of four defeats between 2015 and 2017.

And Opta's predictive model makes them favourites on home turf this week, with a 49.1% win probability.

City's hopes are rated at 25.3%, while the 25.6% likelihood of a draw is the largest assigned to any game this weekend.

If Chelsea are to come out on top, they will have to keep a close eye on Khadija Shaw, who should be well-rested after being left on the bench throughout City's 4-1 victory over Inter in the Women's Champions League.

And Shaw could become the third player to net in 10 consecutive WSL starts, after Sam Kerr in November 2021 and Beth England in September 2020.

Chelsea will also need to start being more clinical in attack, following draws with Everton (1-1) and Hacken (0-0). The Blues have had 215 shots in the WSL this term, with their per-game average of 24 being the most by any side in a single campaign in the competition.

Tottenham are flying high in fourth place following back-to-back wins, and the Opta model fancies them to get the better of Everton. Saturday's hosts are assigned a 51.4% chance of taking all three points, with Everton's win probability only estimated at 22.3%.

Since the start of last season, only Man City (16) and Chelsea (12) have won more home WSL matches than Spurs' nine, and they could now win six home games in the competition within a single calendar year for the first time.

Additionally, since the start of May, only City (31), Chelsea (29) and Arsenal (23) have accumulated more WSL points than Tottenham (22).

And Everton will have to be particularly wary of their hosts' set-piece prowess; no team in the WSL can better Spurs' six goals from dead balls in 2026-27, which is already just one fewer than they scored from set-plays throughout the entirety of 2025-26 (seven in 22 matches).

Everton have spent just 6% of their total WSL game time in the lead this season, accounting for 48 minutes and seven seconds. Only pointless Charlton have led for a lower share of their time on the pitch (3%) and for fewer total minutes (28 minutes, 54 seconds).

Liverpool have gone five WSL matches without a win since overcoming Everton in September's Merseyside derby.

It has been a case of style over substance for the Reds, who are completing an average of 466 passes per game in the WSL this season – their most in a single season.

Liverpool's 58.2% possession average is also their second-highest in a campaign, behind their 58.9% in 2013, while their 84.9% passing accuracy is also their best in a season.

And, with Brighton winning their last three home games in the WSL and chasing four straight victories on their own turf for the very first time, the supercomputer favours the hosts.

Across 10,000 pre-match simulations conducted by the model, Brighton won 49.2% to Liverpool's 25.3%, with the remaining 25.5% of scenarios seeing the points shared.

Local bragging rights are on the line in all three of Sunday's games, starting with Aston Villa's clash with Birmingham City at Villa Park.

Though Villa sit ninth in the table and Birmingham are 13th, only four points separate these rivals, so the visitors could drag their neighbours into the relegation battle.

However, there are reasons for positivity if you are from the blue side of Birmingham, as Villa have lost six of their last nine home WSL matches (W1 D2), conceding an average of 2.6 goals per game in that sequence.

And only Man City star Shaw (12) has scored more WSL goals this season than Birmingham's Oceane Hurtre (seven).

The only players to net more times in a campaign for a newly promoted team are Beth Mead in 2015 (12 for Sunderland), Katie Lampson in 2022-23 (nine for Liverpool) and Amalie Thestrup in 2023-24 (nine for Bristol City).

Charlton could become the first team to start a WSL season with 10 straight defeats, having already made the joint-worst start in the competition's history (Leicester City also lost their first nine matches in 2021).

West Ham, meanwhile, have already won two London derbies in three attempts this season (L1), overcoming London City (2-1) and Palace (1-0).

That is as many victories as they managed in their previous 14 WSL games against fellow capital clubs (W2 D2 L10).

Following a 4-1 victory over Liverpool in their last home WSL match, West Ham are backed by the supercomputer to win back-to-back home games for the first time since February 2025 – they won 58.6% of our pre-match sims, compared to Charlton's 19.9%.

The action concludes at the Emirates Stadium with a huge matchup between Arsenal (64.2%) and London City Lionesses (16.7%), who are truly in the mix for Champions League qualification.

#1782. England player ratings vs Croatia: Harry Kane joined by two 8/10s on special night

Harry Kane scored on the night he broke England’s all-time men’s appearance record as the Three Lions beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring in the 24th minute as Dominik Livakovic flapped at his close-range shot, following some calamitous defending from Josko Gvardiol.

Croatia equalised just before the hour mark as Luka Sucic stole in to poke home from Jarrel Quansah’s ill-advised header, but England were back ahead minutes later as Kane scored from the penalty spot.

Sam Tabuteau was at Wembley to rate the England players…

Showed quick feet to get out of trouble near his goal line early on. Will have been cursing Quansah’s decision-making as he picked the ball out the back of his net just before the hour mark.

He and Kane enjoyed a brief period of trying to one-up each other with their sweeping passes from deep. Was not quite able to get a hold of a few presentable shooting opportunities on the edge of the box.

Undone by a couple of pieces of Croatian trickery in the first-half, and then majorly at fault for their equaliser as he tried to head the ball back to Pickford inside a packed penalty area. Involved at the other end, winning the penalty from which England quickly retook the lead.

A rogue pick from Tuchel, who you feel did not need to use a night like this to understand what Burn can offer. Enjoyed some early head tennis as Croatia made the faster start.

An assured performance. Alert to danger, willing to get his head on the ball and also offering an attacking outlet down the left. If fit, he surely has to be England’s first-choice left-back.

Bobbed and weaved his way through pressure and kept things ticking in the middle of the park. A few notable errant balls were not a fair reflection of his confidence in possession. Found himself scrambling back towards his own goal a couple of times.

Stretched the game in behind with some neat third-man runs. Was able to express himself and impose his physicality on Croatia as England coasted for much of the evening.

Smuggled the ball home as Livakovic made a hash of saving his shot from inside the six-yard box. Did not grab the game with the same drive and physicality as Bellingham.

His movement rather than the pass itself provided the opportunity for Rogers’ goal. Still, Bellingham proved again that he will always find himself in the right place at the right time. Operated comfortably above the rest of his teammates without ever having to step out of second gear.

Leading the line, leading the press and adding energy and determination to an otherwise languid England performance.

Ballon d’Or winner, England’s record appearance maker and now apparently a right-back. Kane was just showing off tonight, wowing the Wembley crowd with an array of wonderful passes, one of which played a crucial role in Rogers’ opener before getting his goal from the penalty spot.

Not given much time to show what he is all about. Tonight should have been a chance for him to get his feet under the table in an England shirt.

Thought he had scored his first England goal, only to be denied by an offside in the build-up.

Booed as he came on. He still has work to do if he is to get England’s supporters back on side it seems.

#1781. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta could enter 'war' with Liverpool for £100m Premier League star in January window

By Lewis Nolan | 12 Nov 2026 00:19

Arsenal have made contact with Bournemouth over a January move for Alex Scott but could face competition from Liverpool, the newest report has revealed.

The Gunners have enjoyed a remarkable start to the Premier League season, with the club in first place with 27 points from a possible 30.

Many view Mikel Arteta's side as clear favourites for the title, though the head coach will not be complacent in the race to win the league.

While the Gunners' squad is already strong, their status as title favourites would not be in question should they strengthen in January.

The i Paper claim that Arsenal have made an enquiry to Bournemouth for Scott, who was reportedly priced at £100m in the summer, though other teams like Liverpool have also enquired about him ahead of January and are particularly keen this winter.

Scott will have just a year left on his contract in the summer, meaning January may be the only time left that Bournemouth can extract maximum value for him.

The 23-year-old is an immense passer, with his ability to break opposition lines making him one of the standouts in the division since last season.

Arteta is known to demand significant work from his midfielders without the ball, something that Scott has excelled at for the Cherries.

In fact, the midfielder has won 63% of his ground duels in the Premier League this season, while also recovering the ball 7.2 times per game.

The problem for Arsenal in any race against Liverpool is that they may not have a spot open for him in the middle of the pitch, whereas the Reds will.

Declan Rice is certain to start for the Gunners for as long as he is at the Emirates, but the Londoners have already committed to Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal also have Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly in their squad, whereas there are concerns about the future of Alexis Mac Allister at Liverpool, while the performances of Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have been poor.

If the Merseysiders offer Scott more playing time, then the Gunners may find it difficult to beat their rivals to the midfielder.

#1780. England 2-1 Croatia: Harry Kane with the winner to cap special night

England captain Harry Kane marked his record-breaking 126th cap with a 92nd international goal as the skipper’s spot-kick sealed a 2-1 win over Croatia and set up a Nations League shootout in Spain.

The irrepressible 33-year-old enjoyed a night to remember at a sold-out Wembley, where the Bayern Munich sharpshooter’s Ballon d’Or triumph was celebrated along with his landmark appearance.

Kane became the most capped Englishman in history, having last month equalled the record held by Peter Shilton, who was on hand to make a pre-match presentation to the star along with the Prince of Wales.

The striker looked like he would be denied a customary goal on this special night as Croatia defended diligently before capitalising on a second-half error to cancel out Morgan Rogers’ opener.

Petar Sucic pounced on a poor Jarell Quansah header, but the England defender quickly won a penalty that Kane slammed home as the nation’s all-time scorer netted in a fifth successive game.

Thomas Tuchel’s men had already effectively secured qualification for March’s Nations League quarter-finals before this match, but Thursday’s victory rubberstamped it and kept hopes alive of winning Group A3 heading into Sunday’s trip to leaders Spain.

Kane makes sure it’s business as usual on his special night for England

England player ratings vs Croatia: Kane joined by two 8/10s on special night

Arsenal’s Ben White again booed by England fans

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

This was far less memorable than England’s 7-0 win in Croatia 40 days earlier and felt a bit like a case of after the Lord Mayor’s show given the pre-match presentation to Kane.

Slaven Bilic’s side were restricted to long-range efforts in a forgettable first half that took 16 minutes for the hosts to muster a shot through Elliot Anderson.

Trent Alexander-Arnold saw a drive blocked and Luka Vuskovic prevented Kane meeting a cutback from Rogers, who soon converted one provided by Jude Bellingham.

Kane clipped a diagonal pass over to the Real Madrid star, whose first-time ball bobbled through for the stretching attacking midfielder to strike into the ground and past Dominik Livakovic.

England failed to kick on after taking a 24th-minute lead and the crowd thinned, with half-time refreshments proving more appealing than the performance. The absence of added time spoke volumes.

Kane was stopped from scoring England’s second of the night six minutes into the second half as Josip Stanisic got in the way of a low Declan Rice ball.

Bellingham saw an attempt denied and Anthony Gordon tried his luck before England gifted Croatia a way back.

Josko Gvardiol was there to help bundle on a corner that Quansah attempted to nod back to Joran Pickford, only for Sucic to capitalise on the weak header and slam home in the 59th minute.

It was a costly defensive mistake, but the England centre-back soon benefitted from one at the other end after Ivan Smolcic wrestled him to the ground at a corner.

Referee Morten Krogh was sent to the monitor and awarded a penalty that Kane thumped home in the 64th minute.

Sucic was denied another leveller as Croatia looked to respond, with both sides making changes to alter the dynamics.

Ben White was among those introduced and booed by some of the England faithful. Croatia veteran Luka Modric received a far warmer reception.

Nikola Vlasic went close as the visitors pushed and Quansah blocked an Ante Budimir shot after James Garner was denied a first England goal by an offside in the build-up.

Budimir went close in stoppage time, but England held out as attention turns to Madrid.

#1779. GdS: Tactics, data and team-mates – the ‘strange case’ of Goncalo Ramos at Milan

The Goncalo Ramos enigma continues to dominate the newspaper columns, as AC Milan try unlock their record signing.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport report, Milan fans hoped they had finally found a top-class striker in Ramos, but his three goals this season are not sufficient compared to expectations and the €70m price tag for which he arrived.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

And yet, the Portuguese centre-forward is still proving to be a factor in the team’s fortunes. The reason for this lies behind statistics that the average fan might ignore, but Ruben Amorim certainly isn’t.

The coach has repeatedly emphasised how Ramos is helping the team, less so the other way around. Looking at the numbers, you can’t argue with him. Gonçalo may not be making it into the top scorers’ table, but his work is well explained by statistics that place him among the top strikers in Serie A.

Which ones? Passes (20.7 per game, first in volume among centre-forwards in the league ahead of Lazio’s Noslin) or touches (2nd), for example. But also the aerial duels won and fouls drawn (19, first among attackers) underscore the importance of his sacrifice too.

There are two considerations that don’t emerge from the statistics, but are equally important. The first concerns the movements that free up or facilitate team-mates, such as the sprint for Milan’s first goal in Genoa.

Alphadjo Cisse found himself all alone in the penalty area thanks to Ramos drawing two of the Rossoblu central defenders towards him, allowing Adrien Rabiot to easily pass to the young Italian who was in lots of space.

The second consideration concerns the pressure and coverage work, which has changed since the start of the season. In the early days, Gonçalo was the first to apply pressure up front, but in doing so, he exposed Modric to too much space to cover in front of or behind him.

Amorim therefore asked the Portuguese to instead harass the opposing playmaker, without attacking the defence in the initial possession. This move allows Luka to run less and think more during the opponent’s possession phase.

We were talking about a Milan side that is helping Ramos less than the centre-forward is helping the team, too. The former Benfica man is 19th in Serie A for shots (26) and 15th for shots on target (10).

While it’s true that the Rossoneri maintain a high standard in terms of the quality of chances created (third in the league for big chances behind Inter and Roma), it’s equally undeniable that they arrive in the final third of the pitch less often than expected. Milan are 12th for touches in the opponent’s penalty area and 12th for shots on target.

In short, Ramos sees the ball mostly where he can’t hurt the goalkeepers. Even if, in relation to goal-scoring chances, he should have scored double in the league: 4.16 xG compared to the just two scored. Still, not enough for a Milan-calibre player.

Lets be honest guys, he was 5m from the goal in central position with nobady blocking a potential shot. Why pass it on the side to Puli?

Two players were closing down on him at that moment on either side of the GK. Pulisic put the ball in the net. Why complain?

Journalist being dumb@sses. Look at all the attackers Milan has had in the past 20 years and their first 11 matches at Milan.

Look at Pulisic’s first 11 matches for us. 4 goals, 1 assists. 5 G&A. Ramos has 2 Goals and 2 Assists in the league (3 goals if you include Europa), 4 G&A. Heck Giroud was 4 goals and 0 assists in his first 11 games. Literally same G & A combined.

By contrast Rafa’s first 11 matches for us net 1 goal and 0 assists, And prior to this year, he was our most expensive signing.

Why are they being so anal just because Gerry decided to splash his money around? It’s not like because of that we couldn’t afford Gila or Moreira or Diawara is it?

Very well said. And what if he doesn’t score but he opens up the space for Rabiot, Pulisic, Moreira and Cisse to score way more goals than they could have otherwise? What if it’s true that he helps out Modric to play his best? Is het then not worth 70M? I would argue a striker who can do more than just camping in the box is worth more. From that perspective 70M doesn’t seem so crazy. Also, please take into account how hard it is to be a striker in the current Milan team. You’re almost always isolated with two central defenders breathing down your neck. A LOT of long balls forward you have to attack contiuously, which is very energy demanding. Most strikers, like Fullkrug and Gimenez, could not make themselves useful in this scenario. At least Ramos is doing everything he can to provide a contirbution. In my opinion, that makes him way more valuable than a classic number 9 at this point. Just give this team time to improve and you will see Ramos’ role change, and the goals will come.

It’s really because Pulisic cost less than Chukwueze and Giroud cost less than a loaf of bread. Ramos cost more than Nesta and Inzaghi. Now you get it?

Judging players based on transfer fee rather than their performance on the pitch is dumb. And comparing his transfer fee to players that played 25 years ago is beyond dumb. As if prices haven’t gone up since then. So if they paid 30 mil for him then he would playing great, but they paid 70 mil so now he is playing bad… It’s not your money. And it didn’t prevent the club from spending on other signings. Gila, Moreira, Hutchinson, Diawara. The team is scoring goals and he is playing a part in that. That’s all that matters.

All this hate on Ramos has been unwarranted. He has been instrumental in many of the teams best moments from the first game. Goncalo is underappreciated because he hasn’t scored as much as Cisse but he has put in a shift everytime , work other players don’t do. The work rate, fighting spirit, pulling players out of position, dropping back , pressing and assists, the guy is a real team player . Don’t judge him only on the amount of goals he has scored.

100%, well said. But this is too much logic and reasoning for the average Milan ‘fan’. They watch a bad match, and they’re the first to call every player bad, or ask for Amorim to be fired.

As a number 9 your primary objective is to score goals. Workrate etc. is nice, but you dont become qualityforward by just running after the ball when your team looses it.

Pulling players out of position is a strange argument for defending Ramos. Every player with two legs high up in the pitch will get marked by a defender and for a forward to move in space is standard for attackers in Serie C too.. There is absolute nothing magical about this..

And the price will create expectation for a player too live up to.. As he preforms today Ramos is only worth half the price.

#1778. Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: 'Contact' made with USMNT as first five games assessed ahead of Michael Carrick sacking

By Lewis Nolan | 12 Nov 2026 01:41

Manchester United have made contact with the USA national team over the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino, the latest report has revealed.

The Red Devils appear to be on the verge of making yet another managerial change, with Michael Carrick under significant pressure.

United are 18th in the Premier League after 10 matchweeks, and there is an expectation that he will lose his job over the November international break.

USMNT boss Pochettino has been consistently linked with a move to Old Trafford, and he is seen as the favourite by many at the club.

The Athletic have now reported that United have stepped up their pursuit of the Argentine, with the club having made contact with the US national team, though the Red Devils are said to be comfortable with him taking charge of the country's games against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

Taking charge of United at any point would be enough of a challenge, but Pochettino would not have wanted to start his tenure at the club with a clash against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Losing to the Red Devils' biggest rivals would arguably be the worst possible start for a new manager, though Pochettino would be expected to get the better of Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on November 25.

The 54-year-old would then take charge of the club for the first time at Old Trafford on November 28, when United would take on Brentford in the league, another difficult test.

Games against Newcastle United on December 2 and Coventry City on December 5 may be somewhat more favourable fixtures on paper, though it remains to be seen if the players in the squad would have adjusted to his demands by then.

Most United supporters would not expect the team to take anything from Anfield, but a defeat could leave the club bottom of the Premier League after matchweek 11.

The Red Devils must then target as close to nine points from nine against Brentford, Newcastle and Coventry as possible, as they may otherwise find themselves in a serious relegation battle as the Christmas period approaches.

Should Pochettino fail to hit the ground running at Old Trafford, he could find himself on the receiving end of the long-brewing toxicity surrounding the Red Devils.

#1777. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed ahead of Spain showdown

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having beaten the Czech Republic twice and Croatia during the autumn international break.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout. Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley on Thursday night to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England now face a one-game shootout with Spain to decide who will win the group, and an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - would be kept apart.

As things stand, if England finish second in Group 3, their potential Nations League quarter-final opponents would be Italy, Netherlands or Portugal.

Topping the group would set up a possible quarter-final showdown with France, Greece or Denmark.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1776. Klopp baffled by further questions over Kimmich’s Germany place

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jurgen Klopp is baffled by the debates surrounding Joshua Kimmich's role in his Germany setup, ahead of Friday's pivotal Nations League clash with Serbia.

Germany sit second in Nations League Group A2 with two games remaining, three points adrift of both the Netherlands and Greece.

Ahead of the Oranje visiting Berlin on matchday six, Klopp's side may need to beat Serbia to have any chance of reaching the quarter-finals.

But on the eve of that match in Belgrade, Klopp was frustrated to find himself fielding more questions about whether Kimmich warrants a place in his starting XI.

Kimmich started Germany's first two games under Klopp – a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a shock 1-0 defeat to Greece – before being allowed to leave the camp early to rejoin Bayern Munich, due to a minor fitness issue.

With Kimmich gone, Bayern youngsters Tom Bischof and Aleksandar Pavlovic started in the heart of midfield for a 2-0 win over Serbia and a goalless draw in the reverse fixture with Greece, winning plaudits for their displays.

But Klopp would rather focus on the qualities Bischof and Pavlovic bring to the team, rather than their suitability to replace Kimmich.

He told reporters: "We can't be happy about the performances of the two young players – because they have done a really good job – without that turning into a story about what it means for Kimmich?

"That's the narrative that gets created: What does this mean for Joshua Kimmich? It means nothing.

"I have a very positive view of this team. We have a very good mix in the squad. Tom and Aleks had a great game, and Kimmich wasn't there. Felix Nmecha wasn't there either, so I did not understand the debate."

A post shared by German Football (@germanfootball_dfb)

Klopp also believes having a high-pressure match so early in his tenure will be a major positive, as Germany build towards Euro 2028 off the back of a disappointing World Cup campaign.

"I'm looking forward to it. It's a test," he added. "We're doing all of this with one ultimate goal in mind: to be ready for the tournaments.

"[Friday] is a proper competitive match, and I expect it to be a very difficult game.

"It will be a real test for us to see where we stand, and how far we've come. We would obviously like to show that we've made good use of this time.

"We have a few hours left to make that happen, so that everyone can see it on the pitch. As I said, I'm looking forward to it."
