#1712. Report: One of the world's best has chosen Liverpool, Reds can agree deal when they want

Liverpool are the chosen club of one of the world's best. They can strike a deal whenever they want.

Liverpool have made it their mission in recent transfer windows to sign the biggest talents they can. Sometimes that's a player at the top of his game right now, other times is youth products who look destined for the very top.

Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola are perfect examples of the former. They've all performed to elite levels in top European leagues and that meant Liverpool were willing to spend an awful lot on them.

Then there are players like Victor Munoz, Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni. Stars who were destined to kick on to the elite bracket with the right development.

But there is, of course, a third way to secure elite talent.

The third way to guarantee elite talent is at your club is to lock down those you already have. And Liverpool have a couple of enormous decisions to make in that regard over the next few months.

Alisson Becker is one of those, with his contract set to expire at the end of the season. The goalkeeper, who is still performing at a truly world-class level, has voiced his preference to remain at Anfield.

And ESPN has given some details on that. They claim that there aren't currently any real negotiations between Alisson and Liverpool. Instead, both parties are happy to wait for the end of the season before committing to anything.

But Alisson has given his preference to Liverpool. That's where he wants to be and there's a sense that Liverpool could get the deal agreed whenever they want. They just prefer to wait.

We imagine that's because of Alisson's injury record. Another long-term, major injury likely ends all chance of a new deal or at least significantly weakens the goalkeeper's negotiating position.

And so if Liverpool know he wants to remain, they might as well hold off. There appears to be little fear that he'll agree terms with a different club from January 1st, certainly.

#1711. Aston Villa injury news: Unai Emery suffers blow ahead of key Sunderland match

By Darren Plant | 12 Nov 2026 11:51

Aston Villa midfielder Johan Manzambi has withdrawn from international duty with Switzerland.

The 21-year-old has quickly racked up three goals and four assists from 10 appearances since joining from Freiburg in the summer.

However, not only did Manzambi start the season with an injury, he is yet to complete 90 minutes in a Villa shirt.

Manzambi appeared to pick up an ankle issue against Manchester United last weekend having been on the receiving end of a heavy challenge from Leny Yoro.

Nevertheless, it appears that the playmaker has been suffering with a different problem.

A statement from the Switzerland camp claims that Manzambi arrived for duty with his national tram with a calf injury.

The statement read: "The midfielder arrived at the national team camp on Monday already suffering from a calf complaint.

"Despite intensive medical care and further assessment, his condition has not improved sufficiently, making it impossible for him to feature in either match."

Switzerland are due to play Slovenia and Scotland in their remaining UEFA Nations League matches on Friday and Monday respectively.

If Switzerland's medical staff feel that it was "impossible" for Manzambi to face Scotland on Monday, it puts his participation against Sunderland on November 21 firmly in doubt.

Villa will naturally have concerns over the physical condition of a player who cost close to £60m.

At the same time, there may be a sense of relief that he gets to enjoy a brief rest period after a hectic run of matches.

Since making his Villa debut on September 12, Manzambi has accumulated 889 minutes of football across 11 starts and three substitute outings for club and country.

When considering that he has little to no pre-season, that is a lot of game time, and Emery will be happy for him to spend a week or so on the sidelines to prepare for the next phase of the season.

#1709. Is the Gyokeres iron hot enough for Hull?

I’m here for our book launch which takes place tonight, but also for our game against Hull tomorrow. Mikel Arteta will meet the press this afternoon ahead of that one, and we’ll bring you all the stories on Arseblog News. I don’t think there’s gonna be anything mind-blowing, it looked like we came through the Slavia Prague game without any issues, so fingers crossed that’s the case.

I suppose I’m mildly curious as to whether Viktor Gyokeres’ performance on Wednesday will see him keep his place up front. He got a great goal, provided an assist for Noni Madueke, and probably should have had another assist when he headed back across goal for Mikel Merino, only for the Spaniard to head over the bar when we know he can do better from those situations.

He’s a player who seems to need confidence and rhythm, and on that basis it would make some sense to keep him in the starting line-up. After the last Interlull, when he scored in four successive games for Sweden, I made the case that giving him a start in our first game back would make some sense to try and harness some of what was a good goal scoring run. Strike while the iron is hot and all that.

I looked at a home game against Leeds as the kind of fixture that would suit him. He scored two against them at home last season, and one at Elland Road, but when the time came Mikel Arteta picked Kai Havertz up front. Speaking about the decision to start Gyokeres on Wednesday in Prague, the manager said:

It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use. He’s done it really well, not just for the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s really great news for him, because he really needed that performance.

The question will be does Arteta think Hull at home will be as good for him as Slavia Prague away? After a bright start to the season they haven’t won any of their last seven but they have drawn five of those. Chances are they’re going to come and sit deep, using the blueprint we’ve seen many teams deploy against Arsenal in the past. If a Gyokeres game, if we can call it that, requires the opposition to leave spaces he can use (as per Arteta’s quote above), then maybe this isn’t one of those.

However, on paper, and with all due respect to tomorrow’s opposition, if Hull at home isn’t a Gyokeres game, then it’s hard not to be a bit worried. Personally, I’d be all right to see him start this one, and if it doesn’t work then you have other options. Havertz is the obvious one, but Mikel Merino is an alternative as well with his ability to find spaces inside the opponent’s penalty area. Ideally though, it’s a bit of a building block of a game for the Swedish international. We need him to deliver goals and assists, the last few weeks have been a bit more positive in that regard, and ultimately it’s important that the manager recognises the moments in a season when he might have to choose one player over another for the overall benefit of the team.

Which is to say, I look forward very much to seeing Declan Rice starting up front against Hull tomorrow, and Arteta revealing that his tech-boffins have invented a gizmo which will allow Rice to player 180 minutes in every game. Plus injury time. I kid, obviously, but I suppose we should know by now that regardless of what we think about team selections, use of players, and everything else, this manager will never be even remotely swayed by external noise – and that’s a good thing most of the time!

#1708. Report: Julian Ward has made his mind up on 'outstanding' Liverpool star's future

Julian Ward has a lot of issues to solve ahead of his first transfer window as Liverpool's new sporting director.

The Englishman took over from Richard Hughes at the end of the 2026-27 summer window and was given a tough act to follow.

During his time as Liverpool's sporting director, Hughes spent well over £600 million on new players and, even though most fans thought that they'd be sorted for the next few years, there are still some major red flags among their ranks.

And, the fact that some star players such as Ronald Araujo don't have their futures ironed out yet is massively concerning.

However, as with every job, tough decisions need to be made and now, it seems like the Reds have come to a decision on one star.

Liverpool will not sell Jeremie Frimpong in January

Recently, a lot of talk has occurred about the future of some Liverpool players.

At the moment, the Reds are massively underperforming and find themselves fourth in the Premier League table.

The fact that they're already nine points adrift of first-place Arsenal after just 10 games is quite scary.

However, with the January window coming up soon, their fortunes could be about to change.

Many different rumours have emerged from L4 recently with some even linking Jeremie Frimpong with a move to Al-Hilal.

But, after this latest update from Football Insider, that doesn't seem to be the case.

"The Reds have no intention of cashing in on the Dutchman this winter, and are wary about potentially leaving their squad short of depth for the rest of the campaign," they wrote.

"However, sources say that if a 'big offer' were to arrive from Saudi Arabia in the summer, then it is something that both Frimpong and the club would be open to.

"Liverpool have enjoyed a bright start to the season under Iraola, but are wary that their situation in defence is a little precarious at the moment.

"The boss does not have the level of squad depth that he would like, and feels that his group is lighter than several direct rivals.

"With that in mind, the club believe that they cannot afford to let Frimpong go in January, regardless of the interest from Al-Hilal."

Jeremie Frimpong still has an important role to play at Liverpool

It's not a surprise to anyone to find out that Frimpong hasn't performed very well since he joined Liverpool last season.

The right-back was brought in to become Trent Alexander-Arnold's replacement with his goal and assist record at Bayer Leverkusen rather extraordinary.

But, for one reason or another, things just haven't clicked for the Dutchman at Anfield.

And, while Araujo may have made the right-back spot his own this season, there is still the odd game here and there where Frimpong is needed.

His pace, coupled with his attacking prowess are two pieces of skill that Liverpool are lacking in at the moment.

So, even if Al-Hilal do actually want to sign the 25-year-old at some point in the future, right now, he's too valuable for Liverpool to get rid of.

Here's hoping that, even if the "outstanding" defender does leave next summer, he manages to find some sort of form before the end of the 2026-27 campaign.

#1707. Are you ok, Noni?

Arsenal’s squad construction has given them a lot of depth and diversity in terms of profiles. Timber and White for right-back, Calafiori and Hincapie for left-back. Ezri Konsa has, incredibly, offered both protection and threat to the impregnable Saliba and Gabriel partnership. Bruno and Lewis Skelly, Rice and Zubimendi and Odegaard and Merino for midfield.

Eze and Tzolis for the left-wing. Havertz and Gyokeres for centre-forward. Of course, some of these pairings are more symbiotic than others. Mosquera is probably going to fall behind Konsa as a back up to either one of Saliba or Gabriel. In reality, Zubimendi is only going to play ahead of Rice if Rice is injured or Arsenal have a nice easy game against League Two opposition, for example…

On the face of it, Noni Madueke should really be in that third layer of the squad with Mosquera, Kepa and where Zubimendi probably now resides. The role of back-up to Bukayo Saka ought to have been one with limited opportunity. In a sense, I was always a little surprised that Madueke signed up for it when he came to the club from Chelsea last summer.

I was slightly surprised that Arsenal spent so much money on a player who was always incredibly unlikely to dislodge Saka no matter how much he improved. And how much scope was there going to be for Madueke to get the sort of rhythm and consistency of selection to hone his talents?

Now I strongly suspect that Arsenal would have had anxieties over Saka’s ability to stay fit after tearing his hamstring in December 2024 and missing a few months of football. It was the first significant injury Saka had incurred and after quickly deciding that loanee winger Raheem Sterling was not going to be an adequate replacement, they amended for his absence with a blend of 17-year-old Ethan Nwaneri and surplus left-back Kieran Tierney.

It isn’t difficult to see how Arsenal viewed the right-wing spot as a single point of failure but encouraging Madueke to see it as an attractive position must have challenged even Mikel Arteta’s powers of persuasion. Yet just over a year on from signing for Arsenal, Madueke has a league title winners medal (‘while others are tweeting and posting’) with 25 starts to his name last season, 16 of which were in the Premier League.

In reality, being Bukayo Saka’s third leg has, to this point, proved to be a savvy career move for Madueke because he is getting plenty of time on the pitch in Saka’s increasing absences. This extends to the England National Team too, where Madueke plays the same role. But it was a role that still earned him four starts for his country in a World Cup, including a start in the quarter-final against Norway.

A Premier League title winners medal, a Champions League Final appearance and four World Cup starts was not a bad return for Madueke in terms of playing time. I think we knew when Arsenal bought him that Noni was a talented but phlegmatic player, relentless in taking on his full-back but the quality of his end-product could vary markedly.

In his new signing profile of Madueke on Arseblog, Phil Costa wrote, ‘there’s a feeling that Arsenal lack penetration from their wingers (Bukayo Saka aside); chaos factor, some unpredictability, and Madueke brings this in spades. His first thought when receiving the ball is centred around provoking defenders and driving towards goal, which means you can isolate him without too much focus on the overall setup – you just wind him up and let him go.

‘There are two specific metrics to love when assessing the 23-year-old; per FBRef data, he currently sits in the 95th percentile for progressive carries (6.82 per 90) and the 98th percentile for carries into the box (4.12 per 90). Those are big numbers.’ There was never any doubt about Madueke’s ability to get the ball into threatening areas, the question has always been what he does when he gets there.

Last season, some clips of him harumphing the ball out of the stadium on his right foot went semi-viral. I also think some of his performances were impacted by a lack of balance in the front three. With technicians like Havertz and Odegaard unavailable, he was often playing alongside fellow blunderbusses like Gyokeres and Martinelli.

I admit that my tolerance for inefficiency is high when it comes to attackers. I think attacking is a volume game. The vast majority of attacks come to nothing, the vast majority of shots do not go in or even work a goalkeeper. Individual attacks are the weather but, overall, attacking is the climate. The more you do it and sustain it, the more likely you are to score.

So my ‘we can fix him’ gene for slightly wayward wingers is high. I didn’t even mind Gervinho (a frustrating player, no doubt, but the Bradford miss has become the defining image of his Arsenal career which I don’t believe was fully representative of his performances).

The video of Madueke’s right foot ballooning the ball into the upper tier against Kairat last season has been refined. Both his goals this season have been on his right foot, particularly notably against Nottingham Forest where he cut in on his right and unleashed a low and controlled shot. It might have taken a helpful deflection but that’s because he kept the attempt low.

Last season, his right footed efforts were more in danger of colliding with low flying aircraft on their way into orbit. Noni’s goal against Slavia Praha demonstrated his pace in behind. It was the sort of goal and chance Gabriel Martinelli was hoovering up in Europe last season. European games tend to offer more space in behind and with Martinelli gone, Madueke is one of the few Arsenal attackers explosive enough to exploit it.

Indeed, in my view, he ought to have won Arsenal a match winning penalty in Budapest against Paris Saint Germain in May. There are signs of greater maturity and efficiency in his game. According to WhoScored.com his pass success rate in the Premier League last season was 76.2%. This season so far it is 86.3%.

I think he has learned that he does not have to go for the full-back at 100mph every single time he gets the ball and has varied his game. In the Champions League game against Lille, he sent 15 crosses into the penalty area, having sent six into the area in the game before against Leeds. 15 crosses sounds like a lot but it was very clearly under instruction from Mikel Arteta.

After that Lille game, the manager said of Madueke, ‘I said when you talk about players being ‘clinical’, sometimes that means scoring five in every 100. It’s about generating volume, more actions and getting him into the good positions, because he will decide matches. He had a really big contribution a few days ago, today he had a contribution in the last final pass as well.’

Being omitted from the England squad in September, according to Arteta, provided additional motivation for Noni, ‘After the break, he is showing something else, another level of anger, another level of conviction as well as in his actions and he is becoming decisive in matches, which is what we expect from a player like him.’

He has now been omitted from the England squad again for the November international round. It is a decision I don’t really understand from Thomas Tuchel but I am happy if it continues to provide Madueke with an additional reason to fine tune his game and because it hopefully protects a player who has become very important.

I admit I am not entirely sure how good Madueke is going to be in, say, three years’ time. He is 24 and it’s at that age that attackers typically start to increase their decisive actions. He has Max Dowman in the rearview mirror too. I think Madueke has a really high ceiling and there are small, but encouraging, signs of improvement.

#1706. Stockport County vs Reading - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 12 Nov 2026 11:54, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 11:56

Stockport County will be looking to pick up an important victory when they welcome Reading to Edgeley Park on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts currently sit second in the League One table, while the visitors are sixth.

Stockport have collected 26 points from 14 league matches so far and sit just three points behind leaders Huddersfield Town.

Jimmy McNulty's side showed real resilience in the FA Cup at the weekend, coming from two goals down to beat Cray Wanderers 3-2 in extra time after goalkeeper Luca Ashby-Hammond was sent off.

In their most recent league game, Stockport beat Wimbledon thanks to goals from Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis.

It was a crucial victory for the Hatters, who had dropped points in their previous two games with a 1-1 draw against Notts County and a 1-0 defeat to Oxford United.

It is also worth noting that Stockport failed to beat Reading at all last season, drawing 1-1 at home before losing 1-0 at the Select Car Leasing Stadium.

Reading sit sixth with 22 points from 14 matches, leaving them just four points behind Stockport and firmly in the race for promotion.

The Royals were beaten 2-0 by rivals Oxford United in their last league game, but responded with an emphatic 5-0 FA Cup victory over Peterborough United three days later.

Daniel Kyerewaa, Jack Marriott and Charlie Savage all found the back of the net in the first half, while Jamie Reid came off the bench to bag a brace.

Reading will be looking to carry that momentum into Saturday's fixture, having rested almost all of their first team players on Tuesday when they lost on penalties to Bristol Rovers in the EFL Trophy.

Stockport County form (all competitions):

Stockport have been handed a boost after goalkeeper Oliver Whatmuff withdrew from the England Under-20 squad to remain with the club following Ashby-Hammond's dismissal against Cray Wanderers.

As a result, Stockport are expected to pick the same side that beat Wimbledon, with Kyle Wootton leading the line and Diamond and Benony Breki Andresson featuring out wide.

Reading, meanwhile, are set to be without Paudie O'Connor and Andy Rinomhota through suspension after the pair picked up their fifth yellow cards of the campaign against Oxford.

Paddy Lane, Benn Ward and George Earthy remain sidelined through injury, but Reading will be hopeful Udoka Godwin-Malife is fit after he picked up a knock against Peterborough.

Josh Knight and Liam Fraser are expected to replace O'Connor and Rinomhota, while Savage could get the nod over Josh Stokes in the No.10 role.

Stockport County possible starting lineup:

Whatmuff; Pye, Jobe, O'Connell; Dacres-Cogley, Norwood, Fiorini, Ennis; Diamond, Wootton, Andresson

Pereira; Godwin-Malife, Knight, Dorsett, Roberts; Knight, Wing; Lisbie, Savage, Kyerewaa; Marriott

Stockport have a very strong home record, having won five of their seven league games so far this season, and they should have enough to beat a Reading side that is missing several key players.

#1705. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

Haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”

9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

#MUNMCI – 59' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball. pic.twitter.com/TyTip3ACIh

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

What a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3

Haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Keane said: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”

Micah Richards said: “Because Foden doesn’t react in terms of, when he got kicked (by Fernandes) and started screaming on the floor, Fernandes would have been sent off. The fact Fernandes, as soon as he has touched him and there is minimal touching.. If Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed. As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes is screaming and rolling about the floor. Of course it (Foden kick) looks worse than it is. But I agree with Roy, Fernandes kicks him. As a player of course you are going to have some sort of reaction, I don’t agree with Foden’s reaction but Fernandes started it.”

🗣️ "Bruno [Fernandes] is the one who is violent here, I have to call it out"Roy Keane doesn't believe Phil Foden deserved to be sent off against Man Utd 🟥 pic.twitter.com/up5ZQqFShy

This fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

City threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

He was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

There will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

"You can shove your new ground up your a*rse"#MUFC protests pic.twitter.com/EMmnF8FhNo

Kostoulas has given Brighton the lead away at Coventry, who are still to pick up their first Premier League point. Around five minutes until half-time in that one. It was quite some finish.

"What an outstanding finish, absolutely brilliant!"Charalampos Kostoulas fires Brighton in front with a wonderful finish 💥 pic.twitter.com/bMKJACr2bd

Both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

#1704. CM: Monza CEO confirms interest in nine-goal star Varela – Milan among the suitors

Gustavo Varela is attracting a lot of interest after his start to the season with Monza, and AC Milan have been named as a suitor.

As Calciomercato.com report, Varela is one of the revelations of the season so far, given that he is top scorer in Serie A with nine goals in 10 appearances. Many teams are closely following the former Benfica player’s development, but Monza will not let him go without a fight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Mauro Baldissoni – the CEO of Monza – made this clear when he spoke to Sky from the Social Football Summit in Turin, explaining the position of the club.

“It’s too easy to talk about just one player and too easy to take credit. We did well, but above all, he did well: he was called upon to make a leap, to make an effort, and he did it very well,” he said.

“Now he’s calm and serene, but he knows he hasn’t achieved anything yet. The foundations are there for a great career. The goal is to have him with us until the end of the season. We know he’s being followed by clubs with great ambitions, but we want to keep him as long as possible.

“It’s still mid-November and no real discussions have been had with anyone. We know that the boy has received some interest through his agent and we’ve received some as well. But it’s all very premature.”

Interest has been confirmed, but from whom? Over the past few weeks, the Portuguese has been closely monitored by scouts from various clubs and strongly linked with several Italian big clubs.

Juventus are looking for another centre-forward to give to Spalletti. Milan want a quality alternative to Gonçalo Ramos and are in the hunt, even if Nicolo Tresoldi has been linked. Inter president Beppe Marotta denied the possibility of adding a fifth striker to the squad, but they are always lurking.

Napoli are closely monitoring the situation too. Massimiliano Allegri has outlined his needs for a striker in the summer to replace Lorenzo Lucca (who is set to leave again), so they are among the frontrunners.

Last summer, Monza paid just €2m to acquire him from Benfica and sign him to a contract until 2030. In just two months, his price has skyrocketed and the asking price is now around €25-30m. Selling in January remains unlikely, unless a big offer is forthcoming.

However, there is the Benfica factor. The Portuguese giants have two clauses in their favour: they will get a 20% share of the capital gain on the player’s future resale, and they have the ability to match any offers that may come from other teams.

#1703. Attacking efficiency key for Hull’s visit

Arsenal are in Premier League action this afternoon, taking on Hull City at home. No doubt there will be some rotation from the midweek Champions League game, with players like Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes, Myles-Lewis-Skelly, Jurrien Timber, Riccardo Calafiori, Christos Tzolis and Kai Havertz all potential inclusions. I suspect Declan Rice will start!

I wrote yesterday about Viktor Gyokeres and whether his good performance in midweek would see him keep his place. On the Swedish international, Mikel Arteta said:

I think everybody was so happy to see, not only the goals but also the performance, how free he looked, how happy he looked, the energy that he could transmit on that football pitch. That’s exactly what we need, that’s what we’re signing, that’s the type of player that can help us to make the difference and he certainly did that during the night.

So let’s see if that means he keeps his place up front. Noni Madueke has had a decent couple of weeks too, with the manager revealing he’d used the elongated Interlull in October to up the ante in terms of his own training:

What he did is he went abroad and he trained. He got somebody to train him and he went into a programme, he wanted to do that. That’s Noni and that’s his mindset – he wants to get better. I love that action that he took because at that moment he wasn’t playing.

With Bukayo Saka injured and Max Dowman suspended until after the Newcastle game, he’s more or less the only option on the right-hand side, so fingers crossed he can continue that form today against a team who are likely to try and make life difficult for us. Players who can beat a man and find some space are really valuable for fixtures like this, and he might prove very important later on.

Hull started the season brightly, but haven’t won since the end of August. All the same, five draws from their last seven games tells you they’re a relatively tough nut to crack, and with a back five they’ll surely have looked at how other teams have come to our place to frustrate us. An early goal is always useful, Ezri Konsa’s quick strike against Everton probably prevented that game from being as much of a slog as it might have been, but we might also need some patience today too.

Some of the difficult games they’ve come through and competed in, they’ve earned the right to be here and been impressive. We’ve been discussing that with the boys on what to expect from them tomorrow and to be clear on what we need to do to beat them.

Arsenal were a bit wasteful in midweek against Slavia Prague, and so making the most of our chances will be important today. Whether it’s Gyokeres or Havertz, and regardless of the construction of the midfield, we need to be more clinical as a team in general, so let’s hope we can produce that today. I take nothing for granted in this league, but hopefully this is one we can just deal with as efficiently as possible before we head into the Interlull.

I just want to mention the launch of The 22 we had at Big Red last night, a huge thanks to everyone who came along and bought a book. The reaction to it was fantastic, and it was real pleasure to meet so many of you. A massive thanks too to Martin and Louise and all the staff there who were such a great help – with the Tollington closed for a while, Big Red is open today if you’re looking for your pre-game pints.

Orders are limited to two per person, and once they sell out, that’s it. This is a real collector’s item, and the best of luck if you’re after one.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. #1702. Arsenal 1-0 Hull: Not efficient, but enough

In yesterday’s preview blog, I spoke about Arsenal’s attacking efficiency, and how that might be key to taking all three points. In yesterday’s game against Hull, Arsenal took 21 shots, 10 of which were on target, and scored one goal from that. Efficient?

Despite generally dominating possession, I thought there was a lack of precision in certain aspects of our first half play. Passes weren’t quite quick enough or accurate enough, but there were moments when we could have found the breakthrough. Gabriel almost got on the end of a Noni Madueke cross which was flicked on towards the back post, Rice had a tame shot from a free kick before a late header which he probably should have done better with.

And then there was Kai Havertz. It’s fair to say Hull didn’t leave a lot of room behind a defensive line that often had six players stretched across it, but late in the half a superb Martin Odegaard pass sent him clean through, one on one with the keeper. I haven’t seen replays but in real time I felt like he should have pulled the trigger – instead he over-complicated it. You have to be prepared to shoot from there, even if it’s on your wrong foot.

Then there was a penalty incident when he complained vociferously, play went on, the ref was then told to go to the screen and we all assumed it would be a penalty. However, the ref said it was a foul but Havertz was offside – and it felt like a massive waste of time. Afterwards, it emerged it should have been a penalty, but apparently the rule is ‘open to interpretation’. So clear as mud then.

In the second half, we seemed to play down our right a lot, with Madueke the outlet most of the time. I thought he did pretty well, much better than Christos Tzolis on the other side, but the breakthrough wouldn’t come. Mikel Merino replaced Rice (who seemed to be on the end of a wild challenge in midfield that the ref just ignored as he tumbled through the air), and Viktor Gyokeres came on for Havertz.

On 71 minutes though, we found the goal. Madueke’s shot was spilled by the keeper, Odegaard was quickest to react to poke the ball home for 1-0. And to be fair, you always felt confident that would be enough. We are the masters of the single goal margin win, and this was another one. Not a day that will live long in the memory or anything, but a 1-0 win that takes us into the Interlull in really good shape, and there’s not much arguing with that.

Or really, much more to say about this game. Mikel Arteta sounded happy enough, saying:

I’m delighted with the win. To go into the international break with a win is one of the best things about being a coach or player, I would say. Regarding the performance, I thought we were the better team, had enough chances to score and make it bigger for ourselves and we weren’t efficient enough to take them.

We then had to rely on generating volume, plenty of persisting until we finally broke them down. Martin then got the goal. Not the most beautiful one, but the most effective one, a simple ‘shoot and then follow the next action’, and that was ultimately enough to win the game.

So Arsenal sit top of the table, with 9 wins from 10 so far this season in the league, and it’s a very impressive run of form. Do I wish we had more attacking potency? Absolutely, and I do worry a bit that it might bite us in the arse somewhere down the line, but for now, we can see that this is a team that just knows how to win, and perhaps that’s the most important thing.

Right, I’m gonna leave it there for this morning. I have to head back to Dublin today. It was great to see lots of you over the weekend, until next time! And we’ll have an Arsecast Extra for you tomorrow too.

#1701. Report: There's growing belief, Liverpool have chance to sign incredible Arsenal star

Liverpool appear to have a genuine chance at signing a fantastic star from Arsenal. The door is truly opening.

Liverpool could really do with improving their midfield. That seems plain for everyone to see right now, such has been their start to the season.

Though, we felt they actually needed to invest there in the summer. The decision not to was a strange one, particularly as Curtis Jones left the club without any sort of replacement. It only took a couple of fixtures before it was apparent that the Reds lacked control through the middle.

And so everyone expects some movement in 2027. Maybe that's in January or maybe that's in the summer - it will depend on how Andoni Iraola feels about the club's prospects this season and, of course, who's available on the market.

It does seem that one of the best possible signings will be available in January, though. That's certainly the feeling among other elite clubs.

Martin Zubimendi and Liverpool's need for a midfielderLiverpool tried to sign Martin Zubimendi back in 2024. That deal collapsed as the Spaniard decided right at the last minute that he didn’t want to leave Real Sociedad. One year later, that had changed. Arsenal swooped in to sign Zubimendi and went on to deliver the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years. And yet, just one year after that, he doesn’t have a place in the team. Zubimendi has fallen to fourth choice in midfield. Declan Rice is ahead of him, which is fair enough, but so are new signing Bruno Guimaraes and academy product Myles Lewis-Skelly. It means that the World Cup-winning midfielder has played just 100 minutes in the Premier League this season with zero starts.

Liverpool tried to sign Martin Zubimendi back in 2024. That deal collapsed as the Spaniard decided right at the last minute that he didn’t want to leave Real Sociedad.

One year later, that had changed. Arsenal swooped in to sign Zubimendi and went on to deliver the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years. And yet, just one year after that, he doesn’t have a place in the team.

Zubimendi has fallen to fourth choice in midfield. Declan Rice is ahead of him, which is fair enough, but so are new signing Bruno Guimaraes and academy product Myles Lewis-Skelly. It means that the World Cup-winning midfielder has played just 100 minutes in the Premier League this season with zero starts.

The Independent reports that Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid all view this as an opportunity. It’s known that Arsenal want to sign a new forward, too, but won’t do so before they’ve made a major sale.

It’s thought that Zubimendi is the most likely sale, and that’s got clubs lining up.

And we implore Liverpool to get involved here. There was a need for Zubimendi back in 2024 and that need still exists - a midfielder who can win the ball back and control possession is exactly what this team needs.

Our Value Adder model rates Zubimendi extremely highly, too, and Arsenal’s decision to move him out of the lineup really feels like a mistake on their part. One that Liverpool can massively capitalise on.

If there’s any chance of them doing a deal in January, the Reds have got to look into it. They won’t find better.

#1700. Michael Carrick, Man Utd break unwanted all-time records after sacking confirmed with club statement

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:17

Michael Carrick has officially been sacked as Manchester United head coach and has departed Old Trafford with an unwanted all-time record.

The 45-year-old’s inevitable exit was confirmed on Thursday morning with a club statement explaining why the “extremely difficult” decision was made.

“Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025-26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

“After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

“Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

“The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

Four months after becoming Man United’s interim boss following the dismissal of Ruben Amorim, Carrick was rewarded with the permanent role in May after steering the club back into the Champions League.

However, Carrick has now left Man United sitting in 18th place in the Premier League table following the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years, accumulating only eight points from their opening 10 games (W1 D5 L4).

Although Red Devils supporters have continued to give their full backing to Carrick, acknowledging that deeper issues lie with the club's hierarchy, the decision has been made for the club to move in a new direction.

Carrick has therefore set an unwanted record of overseeing the fewest games as a permanent Man United manager (32 in total, 16 as permanent boss), overtaking Clarence "Lal" Hilditch (33) who was in charge between October 1926 and April 1927.

Across those 32 games, Carrick won 15, drew eight and lost nine in all competitions (46.9% win rate), though he only recorded four victories across his final 16 matches in charge (25% win rate).

Meanwhile, Man United have now sacked two managers (Carrick in November and Amorim in January) in the same calendar year for the first time in their 148-year history.

Carrick’s exit also means that the Red Devils have sacked managers in three successive seasons for the very first time.

Prior to the dismissals of Carrick and Amorim, Erik ten Hag was relieved of his duties in October 2024, just four months after being given a new contract.

Man United have had a total of seven permanent managers and five different interim bosses since club icon Sir Alex Ferguson called time on his legendary 26-year reign in the summer of 2013.

It is widely expected that Mauricio Pochettino will be appointed as Carrick’s successor, with an agreement in principle said to be in place for him to swap his current role as USA national team coach for the Old Trafford hotseat.

#1699. Strops, scruff, and chaos

I watched Man Utd v Aston Villa last night. When Villa conceded late on to let a two goal lead slip for the second time in the game, Unai Emery threw a strop and went down the tunnel. It’s not the first time he’s eschewed a handshake with the opposition manager, and his post-game interview where he insisted he thought the game was over was very funny because it was such obvious bullshit.

This is someone who has managed over 1000 games in his career. I’m pretty sure he knows when the final whistle blows and when it doesn’t. Can you imagine if Mikel Arteta did that? You wouldn’t be able to move for all the opinion pieces about what a sore loser he is and all the rest. But perhaps Emery gets a pass because he is ‘the best manager in the league’. Anyway, perhaps it provides a stay of execution for Michael Carrick at Man Utd, which can only be a good thing.

Meanwhile, it looks as if Pierre Sage is gonna get fired by Crystal Palace and replaced by Thomas Frank. That seems a sensible appointment to me. Enough time has passed since his spell at Sp*rs for the toxins to wear off, and he’s clearly a good manager. I’ve never been convinced by Sage, I just think he looks too scruffy. As if someone got a 10 year old to draw man and brought it to life.

I quite enjoyed this quote from Mikel Arteta in his post-game press conference after Saturday’s 1-0 win over Hull:

Sometimes we try to score the perfect goal against low blocks, but we need to be much more chaotic than that. If we open the scoring much earlier also, it changes the game.

I love it as a concept, adding some chaos to our control makes a lot of sense, but it also kinda seems at odds with what the manager asks of his players. Maybe he just means more shots from distance, maybe riskier pass when we’re trying to break the opposition down, or maybe there’s something he’s got cooking for over the Interlull and when we return we see something we never expected. He did kick the shit out of a dugout chair on Saturday, that’s a new enough development to be fair.

I wonder was he referring to the Kai Havertz chance in the first half, when he could have shot on his right foot but tried to cut back/lay it off. If you shoot, maybe you don’t score but as we saw with the winning goal from Martin Odegaard, it might end up in the path of another Arsenal player who can finish it off. Perhaps too there’s a bit of a through line between being more chaotic and what Noni Madueke is doing at the moment. He can be a bit scattergun, but as Nick Wright points out on Sky Sports, his numbers are improving. I don’t think Arteta will ever embrace full chaos, all the time, but if he can add a little more to the mix, it could certainly help.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. A bit shorter than normal, I know. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around lunchtime. Until then, have a good one.

By Ellis Stevens | 12 Nov 2026 12:34

Kosovo and Israel will clash at Stadiumi Fadil Vokrri on Saturday afternoon in UEFA Nations League B Group 3.

The hosts are second in the standings with five points from four games, while the visitors are at the bottom of the table with two points after four matches.

Kosovo got their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign underway with a deserved 1-0 victory over Ireland, with captain Vedat Muriqi scoring the late winner.

Franco Foda's side had dominated the encounter, holding 57% possession, taking 22 shots and creating 2.74 expected goals (xG) compared to Ireland's three efforts and 0.25xG.

Foda would have been looking for his team to build on that triumph in the following matches, but Kosovo have failed to win any of the subsequent three fixtures.

Kosovo suffered a 3-1 defeat to Austria on matchday two, followed by back-to-back draws with Israel (0-0) and Austria (1-1), leaving them second in the standings with five points, only ahead of third-placed Ireland thanks to their head-to-head record.

Ahead of a potentially pivotal matchday six encounter with Ireland, when both teams could be fighting to secure second place and a chance at promotion to League A, Kosovo will be eager to secure all three points on Saturday - especially as Ireland face leaders Austria.

Kosovo, despite failing to score, were in control of large periods of their 0-0 draw with Israel, and a return to their home ground for the reverse fixture will provide a considerable confidence boost.

#1695. Interlull musings and shiny distractions

We’re two days into the final Interlull of the year and, as you might expect, there’s not a huge amount going on. The senior fixtures don’t start until Thursday, so we haven’t even got a fresh batch of international press conference quotes to sink our teeth into. Slim pickings.

This time around, 20 of our 25 first-team players have been selected, which is a pretty remarkable tally. All the more so when you consider Noni Madueke can count himself unlucky to have missed out for England, while Bukayo Saka and William Saliba would ordinarily be shoo-ins.

Any concerns about the Frenchman’s absence against Hull, having travelled to Prague in midweek, were eased the following morning when he lined up for the under-21s against Aston Villa in Premier League 2. More minutes in his legs, rather than another injury to worry about.

Bolstered by Saliba and Max Dowman, whose domestic suspension kept him out of Saturday’s game, the youngsters ran out 5-2 winners. Given they’re currently 21st out of 31 teams in their Swiss-style league table, perhaps this is the way forward. Send the big guns down a level and start battering our way towards more club silverware. Relentless madman Arteta, finding new frontiers for his evil genius. He doesn’t just leave his technical area. He thinks outside it.

If you missed it, Max has been promoted to England’s under-21s for this window. He’ll join Arsenal loanees Tommy Setford and Ethan Nwaneri, as well as former Hale Enders Brooke Norton-Cuffy, who came off the bench for Hull on Saturday, and Amario Cozier-Duberry, who seems to be doing well at Middlesbrough on loan from Brighton.

Given Max has been in and around Mikel Arteta’s first team for a couple of seasons now, it’s easy to take milestones like this for granted. But playing under-21 international football at 16 is another significant step, even for someone whose talent has made rapid progress seem almost routine.

Back in September, Lee Carsley described his eventual promotion as inevitable, while stressing that the timing had to be right. The point was to bring him into a squad where he could play and compete, rather than move him up simply because everyone expected it.

Carsley referenced Nwaneri when discussing the temptation to push exceptional youngsters through the age groups. His point was that the aim is a long senior career, not winning a race to the first cap. That seems sensible enough. Max doesn’t need every appearance to become an audition for the next level.

A couple of games against Portugal and France should be a useful challenge in their own right. Carsley and Arteta also know each other from their Everton days, which ought to help when discussing what he needs.

With England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland hosting Euro 2028, you can imagine that tournament already features somewhere in Max’s ambitions. There’s plenty of football between now and then, though. For the moment, let’s see how he gets on with this next step.

Elsewhere, most of our European internationals will be occupied with the Nations League, while the South American trio rack up the air miles again. Piero Hincapie heads home to Ecuador for friendlies against Costa Rica and Bolivia, while Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes face Japan and Singapore, both in Singapore.

I appreciate Brazil’s options are more limited when European teams are tied up with UEFA fixtures, but their friendly schedule does sometimes feel like somebody has thrown a dart at a map. No doubt the commercial logic is compelling, but that doesn’t make you any less worried about tired hamstrings.

Anyway, fingers crossed they all come back with their limbs intact.

In other news, Italian publication Tuttosport has named Andrea Berta the winner of its Best Executive Award at this year’s Golden Boy Awards. The Arsenal sporting director collects the gong three transfer windows into his tenure, the latest of which ended with some fans calling for his head after the failed pursuits of Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez.

Either the bar is pretty low, he’s basking in the reflected glory of the team’s success, or it’s one of those shindigs where buying an inordinately expensive table guarantees you something shiny to take home. The cynic in me wasn’t exactly silenced by the news that Joan Laporta won Best President and Jorge Mendes Best Agent. In fact, I snorted when I read that. And lest we forget, Edu picked up a similar award from the same organisers in 2023…

Myles Lewis-Skelly was in contention for the actual Golden Boy award, which went to Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi. Hard to argue too much with that, given the 19-year-old was at the heart of Spain’s World Cup win.

Cubarsi also made the FIFPRO World 11. More pertinently for us, so did David Raya. Having finished second to compatriot Unai Simon in the Ballon d’Or’s Best Goalkeeper category, I imagine there’s some satisfaction in getting the nod from the people who actually play the game. More than 26,000 professionals from 75 countries cast their votes, which is a fairly substantial dressing room to win over.

Alessia Russo, who is in fine form even if Arsenal Women are not, also earned her third selection for the Women’s World 11.

As you’ll have gathered from the snippiness above, I find it easy to be cynical about these things. There are so many awards now that you half expect to get one for finding your seat at the ceremony. Still, sometimes it’s nice to give people a pat on the back and recognise a job well done.

On an entirely unrelated note, have you voted for us to win Best Fan Media at the upcoming FSA Awards? You’ve only got a week left. A prestigious honour, that one. 😉

Right, I think that’s as much toothpaste as I can squeeze out of a slow news day. If anything else happens, we’ll have it covered on Arseblog News. Catch you next time.
