#1694. Zubimendi addresses tiredness and transfer talk

Good morning all, hope you’re well! It’s St. Martin’s Day in Germany, a day I’d never heard of until I had a child over here. Kids will leave Kindergarten and chant as they walk through their neighbourhoods with lanterns this evening, as is tradition. Doesn’t sound creepy at all, does it?

St. Martin was, as the story goes, a 4th-Century Roman soldier and is best known for sharing his cloak with a freezing beggar.

Fitting, then, that Martin Zubimendi should be linked with a move to Chelsea (and others). It would be the saintly thing to do to share some of our midfield spoils with the desperate, downtrodden, shivering squad that Xabi Alonso has at his disposal. I hope we let them get absolutely glacial – Siberian, even, given their history – and keep our glorious cloak of midfielders all to ourselves.

The first rule of the international break is, of course, to ignore all transfer rumours. Club football goes away but there are still pages to fill, newspapers to sell, online traffic to amass, and something has to fill the void.

And, speaking to Marca, the midfielder has denied that he’s unhappy:

I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. (Not playing) is something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.

Asked about the toll that playing so much took on him last season – Zubimendi was the only Arsenal player to play in all 38 Premier League games, he started 34 of those and had the third most minutes in the squad, behind David Raya and Declan Rice, across all competitions – he admitted that that was a factor:

I don’t like to blame everything on my physical condition, but I definitely noticed it that year. It was a new year for me, with a lot of new stimuli. I played a huge number of minutes and, to be honest, I was tired. Then there were other things too, but one of them could very well have been my physical condition.

I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me. He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

And he completely dismissed any suggestion that he is talking to other clubs, given those links to the Madrid sides and Chelsea:

I haven’t wasted any energy on outside things. I’m busy enough trying to earn a place, get playing time, and fight to win this Premier League, which is looking so promising. I haven’t spent any energy on it, nor have I contacted anyone.

To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish. Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close (to a transfer), but not at all.

Still, I do think the case of Zubimendi is an interesting one. Having lost his place late last season, he returned late in the summer, and is yet to start a Premier League game in 2026-27 following the emergence of Myles Lewis-Skelly and the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes.

Here we have a player Arsenal desperately wanted and agreed a deal for a year ahead of signing him, would they really be looking to move him on again now that he’s spent what is essentially just a quarter of a season not as first choice? So much focus has been placed on building a squad that can sustain injuries or absences, and then we’d leave ourselves light again?

Maybe? You never can know how transfers pan out ahead of time, and things can change quickly in football but, as Zubimendi suggests, they can change quickly in the other direction again too. Did anyone, for instance, envisage Lewis-Skelly starting against Atletico Madrid just a week before it actually happened?

I do think his particular rise, and a stressful second half of the season, has clouded what we all thought of Zubimendi’s first half-season at Arsenal, and how much he contributed across the entire campaign. At this stage a year ago, we were two points worse off than we are now but still top of the league by six points, with more goals scored and fewer goals conceded than we are 10 games in this time around. He was a big part of that.

He was a huge part of winning the title and reaching the Champions League final – he started 43 of our 53 games across those two competitions. He started every Champions League knockout game up until the semi-final second leg and played all of extra-time in the final.

And if he was suffering physically, there was no break in the summer, as he went off to the World Cup, Spain went all the way, and he was back on the pitch for Arsenal (having had no pre-season) in Cardiff as we won the Community Shield, less than a month on from the World Cup final.

For all that, I can also see why someone would possibly want to make the case for moving on. Seeing a player not be used (Zubimendi has played in seven of our league games so far this season, by the way!) feels like an obvious place to upgrade, and we’ve been scarred before by letting players sit on the bench before then struggling to move them on for a fair fee.

We’re also going to need to refresh the age of the team and especially the midfield before long. When you don’t just look at the players themselves but actually account for who is playing the minutes, we have the third-oldest squad in the league this season. The frontline will need new faces soon – that’s not news to anyone – in terms of age as well as quality, but the midfield will need it on the age front as well.

We’ve also given the fewest minutes in the league to players under the age of 23 (around 6%) by some distance. If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it, but if you don’t get the balance right it will break in time.

Right now, though, this season, we’re likely to need our whole squad. We can’t be making it weaker. If one of Declan Rice – God forbid – or Bruno Guimaraes were to pick up a knock and miss a month, Zubimendi would suddenly be in line for a lot of football. Zubimendi who, again, was central to us winning the league last season.

It’s far too soon into the season to write his campaign off, especially when we saw how things changed so suddenly in that exact position back in May. Let’s see how things look when the summer rolls around, but there’s no need to rush into a decision.

Right then, have a great day all – and I’ll leave you with the gorgeous generosity of another St. Martin close to our hearts.

#1693. Mauricio Pochettino should not take Man Utd job - unless two 'needed' signings are made

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:38

Gary Neville has warned Mauricio Pochettino against becoming the next Manchester United head coach unless he is promised two new signings in January.

It was confirmed on Thursday morning that Michael Carrick has been relieved of his duties just six months after his permanent appointment, with the Red Devils revealing in a statement that they “intend to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

The man expected to replace Carrick is former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea boss Pochettino, who reportedly has an agreement in principle to swap his current role in charge of the USA national team with the Old Trafford hotseat.

Pochettino, 54, is set to take over a Man United side languishing inside the Premier League relegation zone following the club’s worst start to a season in 40 years.

The struggling Red Devils have looked particularly vulnerable in defence, conceding 19 goals across their opening 10 league games – only Ipswich Town (20) and basement club Crystal Palace (24) having conceded more.

Ahead of Pochettino’s expected arrival, former Man United defender Neville believes that the Argentine should be assured by the club’s hierarchy that he can make at least two defensive signings in January before accepting the manager’s job.

Speaking on The Overlap, Neville said: “If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven.

“He'll do that with a pay-off, so do that in your contract, but secondly, he needs two defenders in January, so he's got to insist that he gets two defenders in January.

“He's got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer window to be able to turn this around. He's got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

“They have to give it to him or else he shouldn't take the job.”

Neville added: “He's got to insist on the way in that there's some sort of transfer control, some form of budget there that he knows he can meaningfully change the team.

“Mauricio, I don't think is the kind of manager either who would say 'Give me half a billion' - I don't think he's that type of guy, I think he's someone who is a bit more responsible and will look at things.

"He'll want to bring players through and he'll want to develop young players - I get that and he'll do that. I just think he needs to protect himself in these next 12 months with the transfer budget. He has to.

“The only time you can insist upon it is at the very beginning and he needs two defenders in January.”

Neville, who made 602 appearances for Man United and is regarded as one of England’s greatest right-backs, did not hold back on his criticism of the Red Devils’ current defensive options.

“I mean look at the back four that he finished with on Sunday (4-4 draw with Aston Villa). It was [Diogo] Dalot left-back, [Noussair] Mazraoui right-back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven,” Neville added.

“That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League. I don't know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. I can't believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.”

Man United have been linked with a plethora of defenders throughout this calendar year, but their top left-back target Lewis Hall signed a long-term contract extension at Newcastle in September, seemingly ending their pursuit of the Englishman.

Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Rennes starlet Mahamadou Nagida are among a number of other left-backs who have been linked with Man United.

The likes of Roma’s Wesley, Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite, Fulham’s Calvin Bassey, Brentford’s Nathan Collins and Nottingham Forest’s Murillo are other defenders who are believed to be on the Red Devils’ radar ahead of the winter window.

Pochettino could be announced as Man United’s new manager before the club travels to Anfield for their next Premier League match against Liverpool on November 22.

#1692. Opinion: Andoni Iraola has decided what he wants to do with 'very strong' defender

Liverpool have got a lot of decisions to make before the January transfer window opens up.

The Anfield outfit have had a lot of questions asked about the future of their squad with several areas among their ranks still needing to be upgraded.

They may have spent well over £600 million on new players across the last couple of years but, it's still not been enough.

This has caused them to end up fourth in the Premier League which, if we're being honest, is far from ideal.

However, since the winter transfer window is now edging closer, even more decisions will need to be made about the futures of some Liverpool players with Andoni Iraola already making his mind up about one star.

Liverpool may not want to sign Ronald Araujo after Malo Gusto news

In the summer, four new players were brought to Anfield.

All four of them have had a positive impact on the way things have gone in L4 this term with each of them putting on man of the match performances this term.

Of the lot, Ronald Araujo, who has been described as "very strong" in the past, has probably been the most successful.

He's helped solidify the Reds' back line and, without him this season, Iraola's defence would have been tricky to sort out.

However, since he's only on a season-long loan with an option to buy, nobody knows exactly what Liverpool are going to do about his future.

And, thanks to this latest update from TEAMtalk about Malo Gusto, even more questions have been thrown into the mix.

"Malo Gusto is ready to leave Chelsea in the January transfer window, with the club also open to the possibility of his departure, TEAMtalk understands," they wrote.

"Liverpool also made enquiries about the defender in the summer, while Tottenham Hotspur were among the other Premier League clubs to explore his availability.

"Both could yet emerge as potential destinations if Gusto’s situation at Stamford Bridge continues to develop in the coming weeks and particularly with the Reds open to signing a specialist right-back in 2027 owing to their own well-publicised issues with the position and amid doubts that the Reds will fork out to sign Ronald Araujo on a permanent basis.

"However, if Liverpool do press the button on that deal, they will not have things all their own way, with the interest in Gusto not restricted to England, and with several European clubs also keeping tabs on the Frenchman.

"Atletico Madrid, AC Milan, Como and RB Leipzig are among those to have shown an interest, giving Gusto a number of potential routes away from West London.

"Chelsea are aware of the growing interest and are open to the prospect of a January exit."

Malo Gusto being open to leaving Chelsea could cause Liverpool to re-ignite their interest

Right-back is still a problem for Liverpool.

Nobody knows who the Reds' starting full-back is going to be next term and, with Gusto now open to leaving Chelsea, another spanner has been thrown into the works.

Because, on deadline day of the summer transfer window, the Reds made a last-ditch bid for the Frenchman to try and solve their right-back problems.

Indeed, Conor Bradley is due back in the new year but, after spending so much time on the sidelines and after such a serious injury, it's unclear whether he's going to be able to get back to his best or not.

But, with Gusto now being open to leaving and Liverpool's interest well-documented, it could mark the end of the line for Araujo.

Here's hoping that fans receive some sort of clarity soon.

#1691. The virtues of patience

It’s 13 December 2020. Arsenal versus Burnley.

It was freezing and wet at the Emirates. Only 2,000 fans had been allowed in because of Covid, and my mum, my dad, my mate Ben and I made up four of them. We were socially distanced and wearing masks. My glasses kept steaming up.

This was supposed to be fun. Watching my team.

Willian was grotesquely slow. Alex Lacazette was profligate. Rob Holding was bald. Very bald. And Granit Xhaka was angry. So angry, in fact, that in the second half he put his hands around the throat of some opposition goon and, after a VAR review, got himself sent off. There were boos. As many as 2,000 people could muster, anyway.

Then our captain, Pierre Emerick-Aubameyang, headed a corner into his own net. You couldn’t make it up. Except you could. It was the only goal of the game.

By then the steam fogging up my specs might as well have been coming out of my ears. In his player ratings, Andrew M called Xhaka the ‘King of the Idiots’ and described the match and the result as ‘utterly shit’. Which was fair.

It was our seventh defeat in 10 league games and our fourth in a row at home, something that hadn’t happened since 1953. We were 15th, five points above the relegation zone.

And who was top? Sp*rs. Managed by everyone’s favourite sociopath, Jose Mourinho. Having beaten us in the North London derby the week before, they couldn’t stop gloating.

I’d bought into the Arteta project hook, line and sinker. I still wanted him to be the right man for the job. I was just finding it harder to explain why I thought he was. The FA Cup win had been four months earlier. It felt like years.

The tree, to paraphrase our manager, was shaking.

It had been shaking for a good two and a half years by then. The soggy bottom of the Arsene Wenger era had left its scars. Those two 3-0 defeats to City in the space of a week still make me wince. Then came the hope that Unai Emery might get us back on track. By the time we’d seen how that played out, I’d got into the habit of talking myself down whenever things looked up. Maybe we’ll get better. Give it time.

The trouble with rock bottom is you never know if there’s another floor below it. Was Burnley ours? I’m still writing about it six years later, so it was probably mine. There were games against Southampton and Everton before Christmas, and I can barely remember either of them.

Then came Boxing Day and a visit from Frank Lampard’s Chelsea. Is it reductive to say that was the day everything changed for Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal? Probably. But my word, watching Bukayo Saka, Emile Smith Rowe and Gabriel Martinelli tear about the place was the fix this addict needed. We went on an unbeaten run after that. Seven whole games! And for the first time in weeks, I was looking forward to what came next.

And here we are in November 2026. Reigning champions of England. Top of the league again. Five points clear. Odds-on favourites to retain the title after 10 games. Sure, throwing hundreds of millions of American dollars at the problem helped. But if there’s a lesson in all this, it’s that hard work and patience pay off.

Which is why I’m using today’s blog to appeal directly to Sir Jim Ratcliffe to give Michael Carrick a stay of execution.

Come on, man, you’re probably still paying off Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, maybe even Ralf Rangnick. Do you really want to go back to the drawing board all over again? Carrick is the man for the Manchester United hot seat. Just look at the way he wore a poppy-embroidered armband as well as a poppy badge at the weekend. The man doesn’t do half measures. He’s a two-scoops guy. Surely that’s something you, a multibillionaire British-born petrochemicals tycoon who lives in Monaco, can get on board with?

I know Mauricio Pochettino might be tempting. He’s got floppy hair, a tan and, despite the Sp*rsy stench, has come to resemble a rather huggable teddy bear. But think it through, Jim. What if he comes in and everybody perks up? It’s much harder to make job cuts and to force out season ticket holders when people are enjoying themselves. Best get through that process first while Michael turns the oil tanker round. It’s not far off, promise, you’re on a two-game unbeaten streak!

Anyway, what would sacking Carrick say about patience? Look at Arteta. There were people who wanted him gone after Burnley and, as you’ve just read, I was close to joining them. Imagine if the club had listened to me. All those years of work, all that progress, all the joy I’ve had watching Arsenal lately. We could have thrown it all away because a man in a damp mask couldn’t see out of his glasses.

So give Carrick time. Give him January. Give him a full pre-season. And if things still haven’t picked up by this time next year, ask yourself whether one full pre-season, and £100 million on Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, was ever really enough.

I can only speak for myself, Jim, but I haven’t looked forward to watching Manchester United this much in years.

The Interlull kicks into gear tonight. David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi are in action for Spain against Czechia, Riccardo Calafiori’s Italy take on France, and England face Croatia at Wembley.

Ezri Konsa and Myles Lewis-Skelly will both miss out at Wembley. Konsa is working on his fitness but will be available to face Spain on Sunday, while our Hale Ender is suspended after picking up two bookings in the Nations League.

Elsewhere, ahead of Sweden’s game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, Viktor Gyokeres has been speaking to the press. Like Martin Zubimendi, he says he’s happy at Arsenal.

“I want to,” he said, when asked if he’s keen to stay at the Emirates.

“It feels good when I’ve played. We’ve won most of the games. It was a tough loss in the cup (against Fleetwood). Otherwise it’s felt good for myself and the team, says the forward. I’ve been doing well lately when I’ve been playing. Right now it feels good.

“The communication with (Mikel) Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play. Before a match, if I’m going to start, we talk about the opponents and what I should think about.”

He was also asked whether the criticism he gets bothers him.

“Sometimes it might get to me, but overall not so much. If I score goals and assists in the Champions League, I couldn’t care less what they say. It’s nice to do those kinds of performances. To deliver for myself and for the team. That’s where the focus lies.”

To be fair, I’ve not seen any serious chatter about selling Viktor in January. Whatever you think of him as a player, it would be a strange move unless we’re planning to spend serious money on the attack. And even then it would feel like an unnecessary risk given Kai isn’t exactly pulling up trees and new faces will need an adaptation period.

If he’s happy keeping his head down and doing his bit for the team, I’d keep him around until the summer and reassess then.

Ok. I’m going to leave it there for today. All eyes on Old Trafford, I guess.

#1690. Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. #1688. Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage: Club statement and update on ‘advanced talks’ with successor

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:40, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 14:19

Crystal Palace have announced that Pierre Sage has been relieved of his duties as head coach.

The 47-year-old has departed Selhurst Park less than five months after he was appointed the successor to Oliver Glasner, who had steered the Eagles to Conference League glory last season and a historic first FA Cup triumph the year before.

Sage arrived at Palace on the back of a successful 2025-26 campaign in charge of Lens, who finished second in Ligue 1 and won their first-ever Coupe de France trophy.

However, the Frenchman was unable to make an immediate impact in South London and has left Palace sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of his opening 10 games (W1 D2).

A 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool last weekend represented a fourth consecutive top-flight defeat for the Eagles that proved to be the final nail in the coffin for Sage, who saw his side concede a division-high 24 goals.

Palace also sit 21st in the 36-team Europa League standings with only one win from their first four games on the board thus far.

Frank de Boer (five) is the only permanent manager in Crystal Palace’s 121-year history who has overseen fewer matches than Sage (16), who departs with a 31.25% win ratio (W5 D3 L8).

Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as Manager. The club would like to place on record its thanks to Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future. https://t.co/JcVHA6FIhe https://t.co/VAM8XnpHlq

In a club statement released on Thursday, Palace said that three members of Sage's backroom staff - Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard - had also left the club.

The Eagles added: "The club thanks Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future.

"An update on the process of appointing a new manager will be provided in due course."

It is now understood that Sage already has a new managerial job lined up, with a 'verbal agreement' said to be in place.

It was reported at the end of last month that Sean Dyche was the ‘frontrunner’ to replace Sage as Palace head coach.

The likes of Anthony Barry – Thomas Tuchel’s assistant coach at England - Vitor Pereira and Rob Edwards, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner have also been linked with the Eagles job.

However, multiple reports, including one from BBC Sport, claims that Thomas Frank is now in ‘advanced talks’ to take over.

It is thought that Palace wish to finalise Frank’s appointment before their next Premier League game away against Coventry City on November 21.

Frank has been out of work since he was sacked as Tottenham Hotspur boss in February, after less than eight months in charge.

The 53-year-old, who replaced Ange Postecolgou, won only 13 of his 38 games at the helm and left the North London club languishing in 16th place in the Premier League table, five points above the relegation zone.

During a brief, trouble-filled spell in charge, Frank was unable to earn the backing of the Spurs faithful, with his tenure defined by numerous setbacks and awkward blunders including drinking from a coffee cup branded with the Arsenal badge.

However, Frank had enormous success at previous club Brentford during a memorable seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025, guiding the Bees into the Premier League and then establishing them as a competitive top-flight team, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

The Dane won 132 of his 317 games in charge of Brentford and they finished as high as ninth in the Premier League under his tutelage in the 2022-23 season.

Frank stated in June that he had no intentions of taking a new job and opted to conduct media and punditry duties during the 2026 World Cup, but he now appears to be ready to jump back into management and embark on a fresh challenge with Crystal Palace.

#1687. How Arsenal have evolved in 2026-27

There was a lot of speculation as to how Arsenal might change this season having flung a 22-year-old monkey (how long do monkeys live for?!) from their back in May by finally winning a league title. Would lifting the Premier League trophy lead to a new era of more expressive, urbane football?

I always had my doubts, not least because your style of play is always defined by your talent. Most of Arsenal’s elite talent is behind the ball. Arteta didn’t build Arsenal from the defence first, in my view, because he felt specifically that was the best way. It was just the area of the team that required the most attention when he was appointed.

In attacking areas, he had talent, even if it wasn’t balanced. Aubameyang, Lacazette and Pepe with Saka and Martinelli coming to the boil was a good collection of talent, even if the pieces didn’t always fit neatly together. The list of defenders he inherited included Mustafi, Sokratis, Holding, Chambers, Kolasinac and Mari. That’s why he went defence first, broadly speaking.

The moves the club have tried to make in recent seasons, especially this summer, shows you that Arteta wants his attack to be sharper than it is. For reasons I won’t relitigate here, the club were not able to add a number of high end attacking targets. Which means once again, Arsenal are reliant on Arteta’s coaching talents to squeeze more juice from the orange. Here are three things that have jumped out at me this season.

Arsenal spent a lot of money on Bruno Guimaraes this season and I will come onto some of the reasons why in the next section. But that signing has given Arteta a deep well of central options, with Rice, Bruno, Lewis Skelly, Odegaard, Merino and Zubimendi part of this midfield menagerie.

Arsenal use these options interchangeably and often according to game state. Art de Roche of the Athletic went into how Arteta has used the divergent profiles of Myles Lewis Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes so far in this campaign. In home games against Leeds and Everton, Lewis Skelly got the nod from the start.

In away games at Nottingham Forest and Liverpool, Bruno’s more robust approach was favoured. The pair have made significant impacts from the bench too. When the 1-0 victory at Anfield had become a little too ‘basketball’, Lewis Skelly came on and provided calm assurance in possession.

When the Gunners needed a little more belligerence away at Sunderland, Bruno came on and larruped the ball into the top corner from 25 yards. However, Arteta didn’t part with a significant part of his summer budget for a 28-year-old (he turns 29 next week but, for now, he remains 28 because that’s how it works) to be a high level rotation option.

Against Hull City last weekend, Bruno was selected and he played deeper than Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard. As Adrian Clarke pointed out in his match analysis piece, Bruno passed the ball to Odegaard 25 times in that match and the pair exchanged 35 passes in total. The idea was clear, to use Bruno’s punchiness in possession a little lower to feed Odegaard.

Against Everton, Mikel Merino was selected in midfield and Lewis Skelly started at left-back. I think this was about more than mere rotation. Arteta always highly respects the aerial capabilities of David Moyes’ Everton team, which makes sense since he played in a David Moyes Everton team for such a long time.

In 2023-24, Arteta selected Fabio Vieira ahead of Kai Havertz in midfield at Goodison Park because he wanted to keep the ball on the floor (Arsenal won that game 1-0 via a short corner routine because they did not see the logic of aerial corners against a team like Everton).

Last season at the Hill Dickinson Arsenal enjoyed a season high for passes attempted and completed because they wanted to keep the ball on the floor and avoid transitions. Arteta has a carousel available to him in midfield and a different club in the bag depending on what is called for on the day.

Per Opta, Arsenal have been caught offside 35 times so far this season, at least 11 more times than any other team. That rate of 3.5 offsides per game is the highest of any Premier League team since 2009. Kai Havertz has been flagged 15 times now, the next highest offender in the league is Dominic Calvert-Lewin with eight. Opta provide a deeper dive on those numbers here.

So what does this tell us, aside from the fact that Havertz needs to work on his timing? It means that Arsenal are far more willing to go in behind and they are willing to test the opposition backline earlier in moves. This was a big part of the reason they signed Bruno in the first place, Arteta wants to play with the risk reward dial with the ball.

Havertz also hasn’t been quite good enough to finish some of those one v one situations when he has got in behind the opponent’s back line. He fluffed his lines against Hull last weekend and in the 3-0 defeat at Brighton, he blasted his effort straight at the Brighton keeper when put through one v one.

But here, I will express my usual caveat, we need to normalise strikers missing chances and focus more on process than outcome. Most chances are missed, you want to worry when your striker is getting few shots. There have also been nascent signs that Arsenal have been using Gyokeres well in some of these situations.

That Havertz chance at the Amex was created by Gyokeres taking one touch with his back to goal and hooking the ball past the committed defensive line. Gyokeres did much the same for Madueke in Prague. It seems like Arsenal have worked on getting Gyokeres to use his physicality to initially retain the ball- something he badly struggled with last season- but creating situations where he can release it quickly.

Arsenal’s out of possession prowess is one thing that has been a constant from last season. It is Arsenal’s superpower, so even when they can only manage one goal, it is usually enough to take maximum points. To retain their superpower, Arsenal changed to stay the same, if that makes sense.

The signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa was questioned by many but his presence has made the absence of a world class centre-back like William Saliba a sidebar, which is quite a feat. Arsenal ostensibly took William Saliba’s pizza chart and looked for the most Saliba like defender they could find and bought Konsa.

The loss of Saliba ought to have offered an enormous threat to Arsenal’s defensive stability. Arsenal’s tactical organisation out of possession is elite but so too are the individuals that helm it. Raya, Saliba, Gabriel and Rice are among the best players in the world in their respective positions.

Taking out one of those pillars ought to have derailed Arsenal’s defensive stability and it hasn’t because Konsa has the quality and poise to retain the team’s biggest strength. His pass completion stats are Saliba-esque and the quality of not giving the ball away needlessly is a significant part of the Gunners’ meanness.

How much Arsenal could improve in attack without significant additions was an unknown so Arteta could not afford to sacrifice the team’s defensive ceiling while he plays with those levers. The addition of Konsa was a personnel change that allowed Arsenal to remain the same.

#1685. How Pep Guardiola feels about USA job after Mauricio Pochettino to Man Utd manager update

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 13:22

The USA national team would like to appoint Pep Guardiola as their new manager to succeed Manchester United-bound Mauricio Pochettino, according to a report.

The Red Devils officially confirmed the sacking of head coach Michael Carrick on Thursday and it is understood that an agreement in principle has been reached for Pochettino to take the reins at Old Trafford.

Man United are said to have made contact with the USA and are willing to pay the £7.4m release clause in Pochettino’s contract, though the Red Devils would be comfortable with him taking charge of international matches against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

USA would have ideally liked to have retained the services of Pochettino, who was appointed head coach in September 2024 and oversaw the country’s 2026 World Cup campaign before signing a contract extension in August to keep him in charge until the summer of 2030.

However, The Athletic reports that former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City boss Guardiola is expected to become a ‘top target’ for the USA national team in the event that Pochettino moves to Man United.

Their pursuit of Guardiola would not be straightforward, though, as the Catalan has shown little interest in an imminent return to management since ending his legendary 10-year career at the Etihad Stadium in the summer.

Guardiola turned down the opportunity to become Italy head coach earlier this year, with the president of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malago, telling La Repubblica: “Pep was honest. He took a sabbatical, partly for family reasons, but if he’d done anything, he would have done it with us.”

Nevertheless, Guardiola is said to have previously had dialogue with USA, and has long been intrigued by the possibility of working in America.

Guardiola was allegedly contacted by USA, along with Jurgen Klopp, before they ended up hiring Pochettino to replace Gregg Berhalter in 2024.

Speaking about USA after Pochettino was appointed, Guardiola told reporters: "The USA is fascinating to try to build a project for many years and be able to get the national team to the next step.

“The potential with the USA is there, given the number of people and sports, and so on.

"I wish [Pochettino] and the USA - I have friends there - the best of luck. I know he's a top-class manager, an experienced manager."

Following his 2012 departure from Barcelona, Guardiola spent a year-long sabbatical in New York City, living with his family in a luxury apartment near Central Park where he enjoyed a rare sense of anonymity.

After a decade in charge of Man City – where he won 20 trophies including six Premier League titles – Guardiola has since become a Global Ambassador for the club and stated how he plans to take an extended break from management.

"After my contract with City, I'm going to stop. I'm sure," he said in May 2025. "I don't know if I'm going to retire, but I'm going to take a break. How I want to be remembered, I don't know."

In a separate interview, he added: "So I'm not retiring, but I will take a break, for sure. When I finish here, I will take a break. I need to make a stop, that's all.”

As well as the USA, Guardiola has been tipped to manage England at some stage in the future, though Thomas Tuchel is currently in charge of the Three Lions and is expected to stay at least until the end of the 2028 European Championship.

#1683. Opinion: Liverpool transfer U-turn will be massive for wonderkid

Liverpool have already been through a lot of ups and downs this season.

They've lost three games across all competitions and, while their defeats against Manchester City and Arsenal can be accepted, their 3-2 loss against Fenerbahce was terrible.

There's no way that the Turkish Super Lig side should have even had a chance of beating Liverpool but, thanks to their poor performance, they were humbled.

These outings have caused many different transfer links to emerge from Anfield and now, the club look likely to make a transfer U-turn that could be hugely beneficial to one of their wonderkids.

Alexis Mac Allister is looking more likely to stay at Liverpool

Alexis Mac Allister has undoubtedly been the best midfielder among Liverpool's ranks this season.

But, before the campaign kicked off, that was far from the case.

Last term, he was massively underperforming which led fans to question whether he was even worth keeping around with some even begging a team such as Real Madrid to make a move for him.

Obviously, this didn't happen and, although at the end of summer this felt like a bit of a disappointment, fans will be thankful that he stayed put.

However, with his contract expiring in June 2028, a decision needs to be made on his future soon.

And, although most of the reports to emerge from Liverpool have shared that the Reds didn't want to extend his stay, a new update from journalist Ismael Mahmoud says otherwise.

"We will hear good news in the next 10 days I guess," Mahmoud wrote in response to a quote from Steven Gerrard who stated that he thinks Mac Allister should be offered a new contract.

Alexis Mac Allister staying with Liverpool is great news for Trey Nyoni

As mentioned, Mac Allister has been extremely important for Liverpool this season.

Without him, the Reds would have been way worse off and would have probably ended up even further down the Premier League table than they currently are.

But, not only has Mac Allister had a positive impact on the way things have gone at Liverpool but, he's also brought Trey Nyoni on leaps and bounds.

The 19-year-old was on the verge of joining Swansea on a season-long loan in the summer but, thanks to Curtis Jones' desire to leave and Iraola's trust in youngsters, he was asked to stay.

This is arguably one of the most important decisions that Liverpool made this season as, even though the midfielder is only 19 years old, every time he's been used, he's managed to control the game.

And, for one reason or another, whenever he's played alongside Mac Allister, the best version of the Englishman emerges.

So, keeping the Argentinian around could genuinely be the best thing for Nyoni which, in the long-run, will massively benefit Liverpool.

#1682. MK Dons vs Burton Albion - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 12 Nov 2026 13:29, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 13:29

MK Dons will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Burton Albion to Stadium MK on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts currently sit 12th in the League One table, while the visitors are 15th.

MK Dons have picked up 18 points from 13 matches so far, but their recent form has been excellent, with five consecutive victories across all competitions.

In their last league game the Dons thumped Doncaster Rovers 6-1, with Aaron Collins scoring four goals, and they followed that up with a 2-1 FA Cup victory over Swindon Town.

Paul Warne's side then beat Bromley 2-1 in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday, with Callum Paterson and Jack Burke finding the net.

The Dons will be full of confidence heading into Saturday's game and it is worth noting that they have scored 26 goals in their last seven home matches across all competitions.

Burton, meanwhile, have picked up 17 points from 14 matches and would leapfrog MK Dons with a victory on Saturday.

Gary Bowyer's side have only picked up one victory in their last six league games, but they did enjoy an impressive 4-0 FA Cup win over Rushden & Diamonds last weekend.

Mark O'Mahony, Raphael Borges Rodrigues, Charlie Webster and Zac Scutt were on target for Burton and they will take confidence from that result, although a much-changed side was beaten 3-0 by Notts County in the EFL Trophy three days later.

The Brewers also have a poor recent record against MK Dons, having not beaten them in their last seven meetings across all competitions.

MK Dons will be without in-form striker Collins, who has been called up by Wales, and Paterson is expected to partner Sam Nombe up front as a result.

Alex Gilbey, Ryan Wintle and Dan Crowley are set to continue in midfield.

Burton are missing Toby Sibbick and Gbemi Arubi due to international commitments.

O'Mahony is expected to lead the line, with support from Webster and Will Collar.

MK Dons are in excellent form, particularly at home, and they will be confident of extending their winning run against an inconsistent Burton side.

#1681. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming

Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom

Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

#1680. Opinion: Liverpool handed opportunity as Bundesliga club prepare to sell €40m-rated star

Liverpool still have a lot of work to do if they want to get back to their best.

This season, fans expected Liverpool to be challenging for plenty of silverware with Andoni Iraola's heavy-metal style of football something that massively intrigued fans.

His performances as Bournemouth's boss over the last few years have been nothing short of remarkable and, fans were hoping for a similar outcome at Anfield.

The Spaniard may have only led his men to three defeats across all competitions so far but, it does feel like a lot more could come from the Anfield outfit.

And, even though they've spent around £600 million on new players over the last couple of years, more change is needed which is why the January transfer window could end up being a huge deal for them.

Liverpool can re-ignite their interest in Bilal El Khannouss

Most areas of Liverpool's squad could do with a new player being added to it.

Their defence was supposed to be one of their strongest areas this term but, the performances of Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas have made it clear that neither of them are suited to being the Reds' first-choice left-back.

Other areas of their squad such as their midfield and attack could also do with an upgrade or two as each area of their squad has had a howler at some point this season.

The same goes for specific players such as Florian Wirtz. The midfielder was brought in for £116 million and was expected to completely transform the Reds' midfield.

That couldn't have been further from the truth with Liverpool fans actually wanting their club to consider moving him on.

So, this latest update from Florian Plettenberg about VfB Stuttgart wanting to sell Bilal El Khannouss should certainly pique the interest of the Reds' fanbase.

"VfB Stuttgart are prepared to sell Bilal El Khannouss as early as January," he wrote.

"Stuttgart would be open to offers in the region of €40m, including add-ons.

"Galatasaray are monitoring him. However, no concrete steps have been taken so far."

Liverpool have wanted to sign Bilal El Khannouss for a while now

Since Liverpool are one of the biggest clubs in the world, they get linked with so many different players.

The Anfield outfit have a lot of work to do so that they can prove they're still a genuine challenger for the Premier League title.

And, while some of their previous links have made little sense, El Khannouss isn't one of them.

Back in 2024, Anfield Watch exclusively reported that El Khannouss was on Liverpool's shortlist.

These links initially emerged when Arne Slot was using Dominik Szoboszlai and Curtis Jones as his number 10's during the Reds' last Premier League-winning season.

Both midfielder flourished in that role but, it was clear that a natural number 10 could help massively improve the Reds' ranks.

In the end, Wirtz was the midfielder chosen by Liverpool but, since he's failed to meet expectations, it's clear to see why a deal for El Khannouss should be considered.

He'd only end up costing Liverpool around £35 million which, in this day and age, is a bargain.

And, since he's already contributed to 46 goals across his career and has already spent time in the Premier League, he could be a perfect purchase for Iraola.

#1679. Bonera believes Milan Futuro were not ready for first season: “Some thought it was easier”

Daniele Bonera has revisited his time as the head coach of Milan Futuro, revealing his belief that the team wasn’t ready to compete.

The Futuro project was launched ahead of the 2024-25 season to give Milan a ‘second team’ to allow their young talents to develop at a level above that of the Primavera league. They started in Serie C but were relegated in their first season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The decision was taken to sack Bonera as the head coach given the on-field issues, even though they were competing against experienced sides with a very young side. Massimo Oddo followed him, before the club chose to go with Sergio Navarro this summer, who has the Futuro in third.

Bonera was interviewed by Fanpage and he reflected on that period with the B-team and what he learned from it even despite the rough results, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“Milan Futuro was a great opportunity for growth. Perhaps we weren’t clear – and I’m part of this – about the level of Serie C. I had an idea of ​​it, but some thought it was easier,” he said.

“The squad had been built with expectations that were too high compared to what the league is. I don’t think that structure, at that time, was ready to tackle that type of league. On an individual level, however, I felt very comfortable. Starting at home was a positive thing.

“The biggest challenge was understanding which players you actually had available. Some were promoted to the first team, others were dropped, and still others were sent to the Primavera. We had guys who perhaps weren’t playing with us and then came back up.

“From an individual growth perspective, we worked very well in some situations. After a couple of years, we saw the individual value of guys like Camarda, Bartesaghi, Liberali, and Jimenez grow. The value of the players wasn’t in question.

“I think the problem was primarily structural: it’s not always the coach who’s the problem, but the way you do things and the direction you want to take.”
