#1677. Man Utd managers since Ferguson: Every manager's record, win percentage and time in charge

By Calum Burrowes | 12 Nov 2026 13:48, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 15:21

Manchester United are expected to confirm Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach following the dismissal of Michael Carrick, who has been relieved of his duties at Old Trafford.

The former Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur boss is expected to leave his role with the United States to take charge of the 20-time English champions, with another managerial change set to begin a new chapter at the club.

Since Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, United have appointed a succession of permanent managers and interim coaches, with varying degrees of success.

Here, Sports Mole looks at every manager to take charge of the Red Devils since Ferguson's departure, examining their time in charge, overall record and win percentage.

David Moyes was selected to succeed Ferguson in July 2013 after impressing during his time at Everton, but his spell at Old Trafford proved considerably more difficult than anticipated.

The Scot won the Community Shield in his first competitive fixture, beating Championship side Wigan Athletic 2-0, but United struggled for consistency throughout the season.

Moyes was dismissed in April 2014 after the club's hopes of qualifying for the Champions League had faded, with United eventually finishing seventh in the Premier League.

Now 63, the Scottish manager is back at Everton for a second spell on Merseyside, having returned to the club in January 2025.

Record: 51 matches, 27 wins, 9 draws, 15 defeats

Following Moyes's departure, former United midfielder Ryan Giggs took temporary charge for the final four matches of the 2013-14 season.

Giggs won two, drew one and lost one of those fixtures, including a 4-0 victory over Norwich City.

His brief spell gave him a 50% win percentage, but he was not retained as the club's permanent manager.

Record: 4 matches, 2 wins, 1 draw, 1 defeat

Louis van Gaal arrived in the summer of 2014 after guiding the Netherlands to the World Cup semi-finals in Brazil, bringing considerable managerial experience to Old Trafford.

The Dutchman won 54 of his 103 matches in charge and secured the FA Cup in his second season, beating Crystal Palace in the final.

However, United's failure to qualify for the Champions League proved costly, and Van Gaal was dismissed in May 2016, just two days after lifting the trophy.

Record: 103 matches, 54 wins, 25 draws, 24 defeats

"The Special One" became United's third permanent manager since Ferguson in May 2016, going on to record the highest win percentage of any permanent appointment since the legendary Scot's departure, with 84 victories from 144 matches at a rate of 58.3%.

The Portuguese enjoyed a successful first season, winning the Community Shield, League Cup and Europa League, before guiding the Red Devils to second place in the Premier League in 2017-18.

However, results and performances deteriorated during his third campaign, and he was dismissed in December 2018.

Record: 144 matches, 84 wins, 32 draws, 28 defeats

Former United striker Ole Gunnar Solskjaer initially arrived as caretaker boss in December 2018, enjoying an impressive run of results before being handed the job permanently.

Across 168 matches, Solskjaer recorded 91 wins, 37 draws and 40 defeats, giving him a win percentage of 54.2% and cementing his status as one of the most popular managers among United fans since Ferguson's departure.

United reached the Europa League final  in 2021 and finished second in the Premier League that season, but a poor run of form during the following campaign led to his departure in November 2021.

Record: 168 matches, 91 wins, 37 draws, 40 defeats

Carrick took temporary charge following the Norwegian's dismissal, overseeing three matches between November and December 2022.

The former Tottenham and England midfielder won two and drew one, leaving him unbeaten during his first brief spell and with a win rate of 66.7%.

He subsequently left the club's coaching staff following the appointment of Ralf Rangnick and went on to manage Middlesbrough before returning to Old Trafford earlier this year.

Record: 3 matches, 2 wins, 1 draw, 0 defeats

Ralf Rangnick was appointed interim manager in December 2021 and was expected to oversee a transition before moving into a consultancy role at the end of the season.

However, his time in charge proved difficult, with United winning just 11 of their 29 matches, drawing 10 and losing eight.

His 37.9% win percentage was the lowest of any manager to take charge of the club since Ferguson at that point.

Ralf Rangnick has since spent over four years in charge of Austria, guiding the national team to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Record: 29 matches, 11 wins, 10 draws, 8 defeats

Erik ten Hag arrived in May 2022 and made an encouraging start to life in Manchester, winning the League Cup in his first season and restoring the Red Devils to the Champions League.

The Dutchman recorded 70 victories in 128 matches, giving him a win percentage of 54.7%, and added the FA Cup to his trophy collection in 2024.

Nevertheless, inconsistent league performances and a poor start to the 2024-25 campaign resulted in his dismissal in October 2024.

Record: 128 matches, 70 wins, 23 draws, 35 defeats

Van Nistelrooy stepped in as caretaker boss following Ten Hag's departure, having previously served as part of the Dutchman's coaching staff.

The former United striker made an immediate impression, winning three and drawing one of his four matches in charge.

His 75% win percentage is the highest on the list, although his spell was considerably shorter than those of the club's permanent appointments.

Since leaving the Red Devils, Van Nistelrooy has gone on to manage Leicester City, but was dismissed after winning just five of his 27 matches in charge of the Foxes.

Record: 4 matches, 3 wins, 1 draw, 0 defeats

Amorim was appointed in November 2024 after impressing at Sporting Lisbon, but his time at Old Trafford proved challenging despite arriving with a strong reputation.

The Portuguese won 24 of his 63 matches, recording a win rate of 38.1%, and struggled to establish consistency during his time in charge.

His spell ended in January 2026, with United having failed to make the progress expected.

Record: 63 matches, 24 wins, 18 draws, 21 defeats

Former United midfielder Darren Fletcher was placed in temporary charge following Amorim's departure in January 2026.

Fletcher oversaw two matches, drawing one and losing the other, before the club turned to Carrick.

His short spell therefore ended without a victory.

Carrick returned to Old Trafford in January 2026, initially taking charge until the end of the season after United dismissed Amorim, who is currently in charge of AC Milan.

His second spell began impressively, with 12 wins from his first 17 matches helping the Red Devils secure a third-place finish in the Premier League and a return to Champions League football.

Carrick subsequently signed a new contract in May, but his fortunes changed dramatically during the 2026-27 campaign.

United struggled for consistency and found themselves in the relegation zone after 10 league matches, with their dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa proving to be Carrick's final fixture.

The club confirmed his departure on November 12, bringing his second spell to an end less than six months after he signed a new deal with the club, leaving United 18th in the league.

Record: 32 matches, 15 wins, 8 draws, 9 defeats

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 09:49 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 09:53 EST, 7 November 2026

Dele Alli has risked infuriating Tottenham supporters after wearing an Arsenal jersey on a Twitch livestream.

The former England midfielder, whose once-bright career has been in freefall since his exit from Tottenham in 2022, has been keeping himself busy on a series of livestreams with fans as he continues to look for a new club.

The 30-year-old star, who has been a free agent since leaving Como in September 2025, joined iShowSpeed on stream after the American influencer challenged him to a game of EAFC 27.

Dele, who played as Saudi Arabian outfit Al-Qadsiah, was beaten 4-2 by iShowSpeed's Al-Nassr and reacted so angrily to missing a late chance that he furiously smashed his controller.

Egged on by the influencer saying, "I ain't gonna lie, throw the controller, break it", as he missed an open goal, the footballer left his chair and started repeatedly launching it against the floor.

Dele's punishment for losing the bet was to wear an Arsenal shirt live on stream, and the former Tottenham midfielder reluctantly obliged.

Dele Alli has risked infuriating Spurs fans after wearing an Arsenal jersey (@dele/instagram)

The ex-Spurs star once said he would rather retire than play for north London rivals Arsenal

Dele Alli looks good in an Arsenal kit, he must be feeling victorious 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/62cO7iYm2w

Sporting the jersey of his old team's bitter north London rivals, which had been delivered to his home by a friend, Dele burrowed his head in his hands with discomfort as fans caught a glimpse of him representing Arsenal for the first time.

Gunners supporters were greatly amused as videos and images of Dele, who in 2016 said he would rather retire than play for Arsenal, went viral on social media.

'Dele Alli looks good in an Arsenal kit, he must be feeling victorious,' one fan posted to X with a string of laughing emojis.

He later posted a selfie to his Instagram, saying: 'Sorry Spurs fans but a bet is a bet. Congrats iShowSpeed.'

Although a regular streamer nowadays, Dele was once lauded as one of English football's greatest talents, having burst on to the scene under Mauricio Pochettino and carving out almost 200 appearances for the north London club.

He is now making a habit of phoning old team-mates for a chat in front of his audience of followers on stream, having held brief conversations with both Jack Grealish and Tottenham legend Harry Kane.

#1675. Report: Liverpool face transfer dilemma that could change everything

Despite the transfer window slamming shut at the end of August, the rumour mill has never stopped turning.

Liverpool spent over £150 million on new players in the summer and, even though all four of them have had a solid impact on the Reds since they were brought in, it's clear that many issues are still plaguing Andoni Iraola's squad.

Right now, they're fourth in the Premier League and find themselves nine points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

And, even though Iraola is doing everything he can to get his men back on track, nothing would help them more than adding a couple of new players to their ranks.

The January transfer window is now just around the corner which is where Liverpool will be given their best chance to improve things and get them back to the top of the Premier League table but, before that can happen, some tough decisions will need to be made.

Liverpool must figure out if they want to keep Virgil van Dijk or use one of their wonderkids

Virgil van Dijk's contract is set to expire in June 2027.

The towering Dutchman is still one of Liverpool's most important players and, without him, Liverpool would be nowhere near as good as they are.

Van Dijk may be 35 years old but, the fact that he's still an elite-level player proves how good he actually is.

In fact, Jeremy Jacquet has even claimed that he's lucky to be able to play alongside the Liverpool captain.

But, thanks to his age, some questions have arisen about whether he can continue performing to this level for much longer.

This has led to new centre-backs being linked with Liverpool as potential replacements.

No deals have been made just yet but, a new update from The Athletic has just given fans a good idea about how far off Liverpool believe the other centre-backs among their ranks are from their captain.

"Jeremy Jacquet has enjoyed an excellent start to his Anfield career, but the 21-year-old Frenchman has admitted he feels fortunate to be playing alongside Van Dijk," they wrote.

"There are high hopes for young centre-backs Giovanni Leoni (19 years old), Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Mor Talla Ndiaye (both 18), but they are still learning their trade.

"With Joe Gomez also out of contract next summer and a decision to be made over whether Liverpool trigger their €55million (£46m; $61m) option to buy loanee Ronald Araujo from Barcelona, it is hard to envisage a scenario where waving goodbye to Van Dijk next May would make any possible sense. He is still unequivocally elite."

Liverpool must figure out their plans for the next few years

Right now, Iraola seems to be locked in with Liverpool for the long-run.

The Spaniard has done a fairly decent job at Anfield since taking over from Arne Slot so, at least the Reds are sorted in that department.

However, within their first-team squad, many different question marks are hanging over the heads of certain players.

These questions are making it hard for Iraola and Julian Ward to future-proof their squad which is why it's essential for decisions such as the future of Van Dijk to be confirmed as soon as possible.

If they don't manage to do this and leave things until April again as they did when Van Dijk's contract was last set to expire, they'll just be making things harder for themselves.

And, since they look unlikely to win the Premier League title this season, that'll almost certainly be their main goal next term.

So, for them to do this, they need a smooth transitional period and a clear idea of what moves they want to make in the summer.

Without this, they could end up doing even worse than they currently are and end up missing out on extending the stay of Van Dijk at Anfield.

#1673. Spurs finally score... but still lose

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”

Rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

His touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo said.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

"A Steven Gerrard type of strike" 😍Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady analyse Dominik Szoboszlai's wondergoal 🪄 pic.twitter.com/h9QTuP8lZc

Moments after the ball thumped into the back of the net:

Possession: Liverpool 44%-56% TottenhamShots: 12-17Shots on target: 5-6Corners: 5-9Touches in opposition box: 22-27

Andrew Robertson received a great reception from the Anfield crowd whilst warming up, when he came on and now at full-time. He catches up with old teammates as he heads off in the pouring rain, applauding the Liverpool fans.

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool book their place in the fourth round of the League Cup courtesy of a 3-1 win over Tottenham. Andoni Iraola’s side scored three stunning goals to seal their progression.

Mamardashvili does well to save from a deflection, like he did a few minutes ago. Mamardashvili did not cover himself in glory for Tottenham’s goal but has made some great saves tonight.

Oh my word! The Hungarian loves a screamer and this is another to add to the list. It is similar to a goal Suarez scored at The Kop End against Norwich a number of years ago. Szoboszlai chests it down and from nearly 30 yards out smashes across the ball. The ball flies into to the top corner, always going away from Dubravka, and Szoboszlai celebrates in front of The Kop. A quite incredible goal.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6

There will be four added minutes at Anfield.

Savio has an effort from the right side of the box but drags his shot wide of the far post.

Liverpool counter with Mamardashvili’s long ball forward for Isak, who gets the better of Gray on the left side of the box. Isak gets his shot away and the ball appeared to hit Tosin’s arm but the penalty is not given. Replays show it did hit Tosin’s arm and he is lucky there is not VAR tonight as that could well have been overturned.

Solanke is on for Tottenham in place of Tel as the visitors have a corner out on the right. Tottenham take it short before the delivery is swung in and headed away by Gakpo as the rain comes thrashing down again at Anfield.

Tottenham keep it alive and Marmoush has an effort from the left side of the box. It deflects off Araujo and Mamardashvili makes a stunning save.

Szoboszlai should bury a guilt-edge chance inside the Tottenham penalty area but his effort is saved. There was a suspicion of offside against Szoboszlai but the flag did not go up. Szoboszlai was being played onside by quite some way by Gray so a huge missed opportunity.

That is superb one-vs-one defending from Jacquet. The ball is played down the left channel but Jacquet gets the better of Marmoush.

Into the final 10 minutes we go at Anfield.

Liverpool are under pressure at the moment as Tottenham attack the Anfield Road End, where the travelling Spurs supporters are housed. Mamardashvili is again unconvincing when dealing with a corner into the box.

Double change for Tottenham as Savio and Maddison replace Kudus and Gallagher.

That is a stupid challenge from Kerkez, who is booked for a silly foul on Gallagher. Kerkez was asking for a booking for that challenge and referee Andy Madley obliges.

Change for Liverpool as Barcola replaces Ngumoha.

The visitors take advantage of very poor keeping from Mamardashvili. Fernandes’ delivery should be dealt with by Mamardashvili but the Georgian keeper flaps at empty air. It comes to Gallagher, who has a simple header from just a few yards out. A lifeline for Tottenham, who have their first goal this season against Premier League opposition.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4

Tottenham have had some decent chances tonight. The latest comes for Gallagher just inside the Liverpool box but his effort takes a deflection off Kerkez and goes behind for a corner...

That is a crucial challenge from Kerkez inside his own box. Marmoush looked like he was going to have a great opportunity from 10 yards out in the centre of Liverpool’s penalty area but Kerkez intervenes with a superbly-timed challenge to deny the Egyptian.

Double change for Liverpool as Szoboszlai and Gravenberch replace Nyoni and McConnell in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield.

Mamardashvili makes an important save. Marmoush carries the ball a long way down Tottenham’s left before cutting inside. As he gets to the Liverpool box, he plays the ball across to his right to find Kudus, whose first-time effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his left.

Robertson is going to come on for Tottenham against his former side and receives a great reception from the Liverpool fans, similarly to the reception Ray Clemence received all those years ago:

Legendary goalkeeper, Ray Clemence would've turned 78 today ❤️Not many former players get a reception as good as this when they come back to Anfield, he was a true Liverpool great 🙌 pic.twitter.com/NLH3nZUJjd

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F

Tosin decides to shoot from range but drags his effort wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

The home side double their lead at The Kop end. Kerkez perhaps should shoot from the edge of the box but instead lays it back to Mac Allister. The Argentine then plays it to his left to find Gakpo, who cuts inside onto his right and fires into the far corner. This now his tenth goal in 13 League Cup appearances.

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM

No chances to speak of in the early stages of this second half.

We are back under way at Anfield. Liverpool have made a change at the break with Jacquet coming on for Gomez. This was Gomez’s first game back after injury.

Tottenham did have two big chances through Bergvall and Kudus and there are arguments to say both of them should have scored.

Mac Allister takes but his effort is off target. That is indeed the final moment of the half and Liverpool take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of that fine Mac Allister strike.

We are past the two initial minutes added on but that is because of the delay when Senesi was given a talking-to moments ago. That allows Liverpool to win a free-kick not far outside the Tottenham box and Bentancur is booked for the foul on Gakpo.

This will be the final moment of the half.

Senesi absolutely clatters into McConnell but somehow escapes without a booking. There have been a number of soft yellows in this first yet one of the most blatant yellows is not given as a booking.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Marmoush is the first Tottenham player booked tonight for a foul on McConnell and that feels on the harsh side. Definitely a foul but was it a yellow?

That is a dreadful decision from referee Andy Madley. Frimpong gets the better of Tel in a contest down Tottenham’s left, with the former outmuscling the latter. Not only is Frimpong penalised, he is booked.

Mac Allister spurns a glorious chance to get his and Liverpool’s second of the night. Tottenham again risk it at the back and lose it. McConnell then feeds a pass into the box to pick out the run of Koumas, who squares it for Mac Allister. The Argentine cannot get his feet sorted in time and wastes the opportunity from eight yards out.

Liverpool want a penalty. Tottenham give it away cheaply inside their own box and McConnell goes down under a challenge from Senesi, who was the one who gave it away. It was a clumsy challenge from Senesi and if VAR was in action tonight it would have been interesting to see what they would have done with that as Senesi did barge into the back of McConnell.

Araujo is then booked for pulling Marmoush back.

There is no way Tottenham’s goal drought will last in perpetuity but they have missed two fabulous chances so far and you wonder what impact that will have on their confidence. At least one Tottenham player is being feted: Andy Robertson, who has just jogged down the touchline at Anfield in a different kit for the first time in nine years. He tried not to acknowledge the singing of his name too much but you could see it meant something to him.

The home fans serenade their former player Robertson as the now Tottenham left-back goes out to warm up.

That is a big chance for Kudus to equalise on the counter. Tottenham break from deep inside their own half and charge down their left. Bergvall waits for Udogie to come on the overlap before playing the pass. From the left side of the box, Udogie crosses for Kudus, who gets across the front of Kerkez. Kudus should probably score but lifts his effort over the bar from just six yards out.

What a goal......that would of been! 🫢Kudus fires over what would of been a sensational move from Spurs#ITVFootball | @Carabao_Cup pic.twitter.com/a1TPzKyJlP

Gomez gives the ball away cheaply inside his own half before McConnell is penalised for a foul on Marmoush. Will Tottenham cross it or take the shot on from around 25 yards out? The answer is the latter and Marmoush goes for goal but misses the target.

That was a chance for Udogie. Senesi clips in a lovely ball over the top in behind to pick out the run from left-back of Udogie, who tries to chest it down but cannot keep it under control. Had he done so, it would have been a great chance.

The way Alexis Mac Allister has played this past fortnight, anyone would think he is trying to secure himself a new contract. All cynicism aside, that was a quite beautiful goal and attention must be drawn to Cody Gakpo’s involvement: he took a pass on his chest from Joe Gomez before opening up the pitch. We will say it again: the idea of selling Gakpo in the last window was madness.

He scored a stunner nearly a week ago against Atletico Madrid here in the Champions League and he adds another storming strike to his repertoire. The ball finds kindly to Mac Allister on the edge of the box after Udogie tackled Ngumoha and the Argentine finds the top corner with a first-time finish.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Ngumoha slides a clinical pass into the box to pick out the run in behind of Koumas, who gets the better of Senesi. Koumas takes a great first touch before getting his shot away but is denied by Dubravka. Both goalkeepers have now been forced into good saves early doors.

Close for Lewis Koumas!The Liverpool youngster is denied by Martin Dubravka after some brilliant play by Rio Ngumoha 🪄 pic.twitter.com/YNC8QEAGGG

Given their team has been bang average this season, the huge number of travelling Spurs fans are making a magnificent noise. They could have celebrated a long-overdue goal had it not been for a magnificent save by Giorgi Mamardashvili. The Georgian needed to make it from Lucas Bergvall, as a minute beforehand he dithered while Joe Gomez was shepherding a ball back to him and those on the Kop lost their minds. It’s tense amongst Liverpool supporters. You wonder how it changes.

That is a fantastic save from Mamardashvili. Gallagher plays the ball to Udogie on the left side of the box and the latter squares it to Bergvall in the centre of the box. Bergvall is no more than eight yards out and must think he is going to score but Mamardashvili makes a great save to deny the Swede. Should Bergvall have given Mamardashvili the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku

Tottenham are dominating possession thus far, with a lot of the game being played in Liverpool’s half at the moment.

The heavens have well and truly opened at Anfield, with the rain heaving down.

Tottenham win a corner off Gomez out on the right. Kudus clips in an inswinger that Araujo heads away.

Gakpo is starting out on the left for Liverpool tonight, with Ngumoha on the right and Koumas leading the line down the centre. Gakpo was linked with a move to Tottenham and Manchester City over the summer but stayed at Liverpool.

Tottenham have a free-kick not far outside the Liverpool penalty area on the right as Kerkez is penalised for blocking Gallagher’s cross with his arm. Kudus’ delivery is headed away by Araujo.

Kudus keeps it alive and sends in another cross that ends up in Mamardashvili’s arms.

We are under way at Anfield, with a place in the fourth round at stake.

A reminder, there is no extra time so it the game is all square after 90 minutes we will go straight to penalties. Also, there is no VAR tonight.

Djaksparo is a rising musician from Paris who who gained viral fame following a social media boost from Liverpool’s summer signing Bradley Barcola, who is on the bench for the hosts this evening.

During the Spaniard’s three seasons at the helm at Bournemouth, he never made it past the fourth round in this competition. He reached the fourth round in his first season at Bournemouth during the 2023/24 season but in the last two seasons has fallen in the second round, which was the round Bournemouth entered the competition.

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

It is understood that De Zerbi’s lucrative contract did not include a survival bonus for avoiding relegation last season, but he must wish his forwards were cashing in on their goal bonuses.

Peterborough vs Barnsley 7.30pmWest Ham vs Fulham 7.45pmIpswich vs Arsenal 8pmLiverpool vs Tottenham 8pmReading vs Brentford 8pm

Our Spurs side to take on Liverpool 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/X4f3F0cl4f

Our team to take on Tottenham Hotspur 🔴 pic.twitter.com/tZSJkPpH3y

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1672. Pierre Sage already has new job ‘agreed’ after Crystal Palace sacking confirmed

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 14:07

Pierre Sage has officially been sacked by Crystal Palace, but he already has a new job lined up according to reports.

The 47-year-old arrived at Selhurst Park with big boots to fill after his predecessor Oliver Glasner won the 2025 FA Cup and Conference League last season.

Sage signed a three-year contract with the Eagles in June and has now departed his role in South London less than five months later following a disappointing start to the campaign.

The Frenchman has left Palace sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of his opening 10 top-flight matches (W1 D2), with his team conceding a division-high 24 goals.

Palace also find themselves languishing in 21st position in the 36-team Europa League standings with only one win from their first four matches so far.

Sage’s sacking was confirmed on Thursday, four days after the Eagles suffered a 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.

While many managers may prefer a period of time away from football to recharge their batteries and assess their options, it appears that Sage is ready to jump straight back in to management in familiar surroundings.

According to Foot Mercato journalists Sebastien Denis and Santi Aouna, Sage has a ‘verbal agreement’ in place to return to Lens, where he left in the summer to join Palace.

Lens are on the lookout for a new head coach after parting ways with Yannick Cahuzac, who lost six of his nine games during a brief 56-day spell in charge which concluded with a humiliating 9-1 Champions League home defeat to Como.

Le Sang et Or have, in fact, had two managers since Sage left in the summer, as Cahuzac had taken over from Dino Toppmoller who was sacked after just 91 days at the helm following disagreements around structural changes at the club.

It is understood that Lens chiefs have set a ‘very clear deadline’ for Sage to be re-appointed within the next 72 hours, giving him time to prepare for their next Ligue 1 match against Toulouse on November 21.

Sage would allegedly return to Lens on a 'very decent salary' within the limits set by the Lens hierarchy.

A return to Lens for Sage would seemingly be warmly welcomed by the club’s supporters who enjoyed a memorable 2025-26 campaign under his leadership.

Sage was named Ligue 1 Manager of the Year last season after steering Lens to an impressive second-placed finish behind champions Paris Saint-Germain, qualifying for the Champions League.

The former Lyon boss also guided Lens to their first-ever Coupe de France triumph in their 120-year history, and departed after only one season in charge with a respectable 67.5% win rate.

Lens currently sit down in 11th place in the Ligue 1 table, five points above the relegation zone and seven points adrift of the top three after 10 matches.

In the Champions League, Le Sang et Or occupy 33rd position in the 36-team League Phase standings after losing three of their opening four matches, but they still have a chance of securing at least a knockout round playoff place.

#1671. Reports: Spurs and Juventus call Milan as on-loan midfielder continues to shine

AC Milan made the decision to loan Youssouf Fofana out in the summer window, and he is attracting interest from clubs around Europe.

Fofana’s situation ended up being quite a dramatic one. He was excluded from the plans by Ruben Amorim and seemed set to join Lyon on loan, but that fell through on deadline day. A move to Turkey didn’t materialise, but Sevilla stepped forward and managed to get a year-long loan deal done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Since moving to Spain, Fofana has found his best form again. Having played nine LaLiga games for the Andalusian side so far, he has four goal contributions to his name, with one goal and three assists.

Calciomercato.com cite TEAMtalk and Spanish sources, who claim Fofana is attracting the interest of clubs like Tottenham and Juventus. They have already initiated preliminary discussions with Milan to assess the feasibility of a deal for next summer.

The club coached by Roberto De Zerbi has reportedly made concrete moves, beginning initial dialogue with Milan management, while Juve were linked in the summer and are still looking for midfield reinforcements.

#1670. Man United were right to sack Michael Carrick - but the club's handling of the situation has been terrible

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 14:11

Following Manchester United's decision to sack Michael Carrick as head coach, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses the major news coming out of Old Trafford.

It's a tricky one. You never like to see managers, or anyone, lose their jobs. In any walk of life, it's always a sad time. That is especially so for someone like Michael Carrick, who is undoubtedly a legend of the club.

He always acted in the right way and has conducted himself in the right way. So there is an added sense of emotion with him. That's not discounting Ten Hag, Louis van Gaal and Ruben Amorim, managers that have left of late.

But Carrick is deeply rooted to the club. His son is in the academy. He loves that football club. He's not from Manchester, but he is very much a part of their history.

I'm sure he will remain a supporter of the club moving forward. So it's never easy. I think a lot of people expected it to happen after the Bournemouth game at the end of October.

Ultimately he was given three extra games: the Chelsea game, the Roma game and the Villa game. They were a lot better against Chelsea, but were undone by that red card. Roma managed to get the job done in the end. Then there was that crazy game against Villa where they nicked a point at the death.

It's been coming. We know about the transfer failings over the summer. United have not had much problem scoring goals this season.

They are a good attacking team, but the defensive issues have been there for all to see. That's not to say that Carrick hasn't made bad decisions and bad choices at times.

Of course he has, and he was always going to make mistakes. He is a manager that is very much in the early stages of his career, and I'm sure he will go on.

He showed decent signs at Middlesbrough, but it didn't end great in the end there. He has now taken charge of 35 games for Man United, including that caretaker spell at the back end of 2021.

He's won 15 games in this spell and two in the last spell, so 17 overall out of 35. It's not terrific. His work last season getting the club back in the Champions League will be remembered incredibly fondly by the fans, as will the football that was played during a period we thought it couldn't get any lower under Ruben Amorim.

But the table doesn't lie at this stage of the season. United are 18th in the Premier League table with one win all season. They are only a point off the bottom. You can't paper over those facts. They are what they are. The table is what it is.

It's been a difficult start to the season. Carrick was going to lose his job. The way it's happened is not ideal. But I think we all expected it, certainly from a United supporters' point of view.

Interestingly, the briefing coming out of the club after the Villa game was that it was very much business as usual. He was expected to keep his job.

Then very quickly that changed, with reports earlier this week that he would ultimately be losing his job. So he's gone now. I'm sure he'll go on at some stage and step back into the management game.

But Man United need to move forward now. As difficult as it was, I think it is the right decision. But it was not conducted how it should have been done. I think it's been done very badly by the club.

Carrick wasn't in on Monday. On Tuesday he took training, largely academy players. There are first team players that aren't on international duty, such as Harry Maguire, but he has picked up a little injury.

He took training on Wednesday as well, and arrived at Carrington this morning. But he knew. The reports have been rife.

Everyone has some form of internet access and would have seen the meeting that happened in Monaco between Berrada, Jason Wilcox and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Very much what we expected to happen has happened. They briefed Ratcliffe that they recommend the decision is made to remove Carrick.

They presented their evidence of the struggles that have happened. But Berrada and Wilcox get more airtime on the TV. I can't remember any director of football or CEO having as much focus on them, and that's not a good thing.

The best CEOs in football, the best directors of football, sporting directors, technical directors, whatever you want to call them, are the ones in the background.

You don't hear from them ever. You don't see them. You hear their names. You know the ones at Brentford and Brighton and teams like that. We see Berrada and Wilcox all the time.

The disgruntlement among the fans is very much towards the football department: Ratcliffe, INEOS, the Glazers, Wilcox and Berrada.

That's not going to change with the appointment of a new manager. There are failings there that are deeply rooted and, in my opinion, need to be outed and let the club move in a new direction. It doesn't look like that's going to happen.

It looks like Berrada and Wilcox will be staying put for the time being. But on how it's been handled, I think it's been terrible.

Carrick's not a silly man, by absolutely no means. He would have known at the start of this week, as everyone has, that he was going to lose his job.

It was just a matter of time. To make him go in and carry on. I understand that in employment you have to continue until you're told otherwise. There's no way he could have not gone in to Carrington on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the way it's happened is really disappointing from a lot of people's views. It's always difficult to predict what will happen in management in general, let alone at Man United, who have had difficulties in that area.

But I think what's interesting is how this develops, not just in the coming days, but in the coming hours. The last line of the statement from Man United is that the club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.

#1669. Wrexham's Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney jet in to watch clash with Wolves after surprise exit of club's CEO - and catch up with poppy-protest footballer James McClean in the stands

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:39 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 10:40 EST, 7 November 2026

Wrexham's celebrity owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney have travelled to watch their side's Championship clash with Wolves less than a day after announcing chief executive Michael Williamson's surprise departure.

Reynolds and McElhenney announced in a joint statement on Friday that Williamson was leaving the club after two years at the Racecourse Ground, with club director Shaun Harvey set to take the reins as acting CEO while they seek a successor.

'We thank Michael Williamson for his two years at Wrexham and for his work taking the club from League 1 to the Championship,' the Hollywood actors' statement read.

'Since our takeover five years ago, Wrexham have had historic success on the pitch and won hearts all over the globe.

'We remain focused on our most important task: to make the Wrexham community proud.

'Shaun Harvey has been an integral part of this journey from the beginning, and we know Shaun will give every support to (manager) Phil Parkinson and the lads on the pitch while keeping the broader Wrexham community roaring us on.'

Rob McElhenney and Ryan Reynolds pictured watching Wrexham take on Wolves on Saturday

The American actor takes photos with supporters as he arrives at the Racecourse Ground

Williamson arrived at Wrexham in 2024 and oversaw a period that saw the club win promotion from League One to the Championship and consolidate themselves in the second tier, narrowly missing out on the playoffs with a seventh-place finish.

Wrexham's form this campaign has been less fruitful, with just four wins so far leaving Parkinson's side in 17th place heading into Saturday's clash with Wolves.

After arriving and meeting fans outside the stadium, Reynolds and McElhenney took their place in the Racecourse Ground stands hoping to watch their Wrexham side earn back-to-back wins for the first time this season.

Wolves, who were relegated from the Premier League last season, took the lead in the 25th minute before Wrexham's Lewis O'Brien equalised moments later, to the delight of the celebrity owners.

As the matched ebbed and flowed, both sides fought hard for a winning goal but ended up settling for a share of the spoils, the 1-1 draw moving Wrexham to 15th and Wolves to third in the Championship.

After the match, Parkinson backed Harvey to adapt seamlessly to his new temporary CEO role, saying:  'Ryan spoke to me yesterday morning to let me know the news. I had a brief chat with Shaun this morning; he has been an important figure. He understands everything about the club.'

While watching the 1-1 draw, Reynolds was pictured chatting to former Wrexham star James McClean, who left the Racecourse Ground to join his hometown team Derry City in January.

McClean's appearance at Wrexham is particularly poignant on Remembrance Weekend, given the controversy he courted throughout his career by refusing to wear football shirts featuring a poppy.

Reynolds pictured chatting to former Wrexham footballer James McClean in the stands

Wrexham players, displaying poppies, observe a minute of silence on Remembrance weekend

Clubs across English football will observe a period of silence before matches this weekend, with players also wearing poppy-adorned shirts to honour those who lost their lives in conflict.

McClean's objection to wearing a poppy is rooted in his upbringing in Derry, having grown up on the Creggan estate, where six of the 13 civilians shot dead by British soldiers on Bloody Sunday in 1972 were from.

#1668. Opinion: Liverpool handed surprise chance to sign perfect Milos Kerkez successor

Milos Kerkez has been one of Liverpool's biggest disappointments over the last couple of years.

The Hungarian was brought in to replace Andy Robertson last season.

However, by the end of the campaign, the Scotsman managed to make himself Liverpool's first-choice left-back once again.

But, by the time the Reds realised that they needed him, he's already agreed a new deal with Tottenham.

This thrusted Kerkez into becoming the Reds' undeniable first-choice left-back with Kostas Tsimikas serving as his back-up.

Most people thought this added responsibility would help Kerkez but, if anything, he's managed to get worse.

This lack of form has been noticed by fans and pundits alike with the perfect option to replace him now emerging for Liverpool.

Rayan Ait-Nouri now wants to leave Manchester City

Ever since it was made clear that Kerkez's form wasn't going to improve, rumours have been circling about the next left-back that Liverpool could target.

Several different options have popped up recently with Brentford left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf seemingly on top of Iraola's shortlist.

However, since he's only just joined the Bees, a deal for the Senegal international feels highly unlikely to get over the line.

And, he's also had quite a slow start to life with Keith Andrews' men which is likely to have caused a worrisome thought or two.

But, since the footballing world is forever changing, new targets can emerge and, luckily for Liverpool, that seems to be exactly what has happened for them.

"Rayan Aït-Nouri could be a key player in the upcoming winter transfer window. The Algerian left-back is seriously considering leaving Manchester City and even wants to force a move as early as January," Sky Sports CH wrote.

"Two Italian clubs have already expressed interest: Juventus and Napoli. Contacts are underway between the player's representatives and the management of both clubs, who have now added Aït-Nouri to their shortlist to strengthen their left flank.

"The challenge now is to find the right formula to convince Manchester City. While the Citizens would ideally prefer a permanent transfer, this option appears financially difficult to realize this winter. Both Juventus and Napoli may lack the funds to meet the demands of a straight transfer.

"Under these conditions, the most likely scenario would be a paid loan with a purchase option, which could become mandatory under certain conditions."

Rayan Ait-Nouri would fit perfectly into Andoni Iraola's Liverpool plans

One of the best things about Ait-Nouri is that he can attack and defend.

Recently, it's felt like most left-backs have only been able to do one or the other.

For example, even though Kerkez has become Liverpool's first-choice left back, his defensive work has mostly been him recovering the ball thanks to his lightning-quick speed.

However, if he didn't have that, he would have ended up in a rather terrible situation on several occasions this term.

Ait-Nouri on the other hand, can attack and defend equally as well.

He's also got plenty of Premier League experience under his belt and has even chipped in with two assists for his teammates during his limited playing time this season.

Right now, a deal for any player to join Liverpool isn't all that likely but, if Iraola and Julian Ward are wanting to sign a new left-back, Ait-Nouri could be exactly what they're looking for.

#1667. Next Man United manager: "Serious coach" Mauricio Pochettino can be a huge success at Man United

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 14:23

As Manchester United close in on the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses the Argentine's suitability for the role with the 20-time English champions.

It looks like Pochettino. But there are strong indications that the USA want him to remain in charge for the two games against Haiti, on November 14 and November 17.

United go to Liverpool on the 22nd in the Premier League, straight after the international break. So it's very interesting to see what happens now.

I did see a report yesterday suggesting that Darren Fletcher may have another caretaker spell in charge just to take training. The players that are on international duty will return next week to prepare for that Liverpool game.

If Pochettino is not there until after the second game against Haiti, he will have limited preparation time for that Liverpool game.

So it'll be very interesting to see who takes training tomorrow, who takes it when the players are back in on Monday, and how that develops.

Pochettino is a very interesting name, one that wasn't particularly in the forefront. I think interestingly, the people behind the scenes at United couldn't agree on Conte, Eddie Howe or Nagelsmann, whether they were quite right at this stage.

I know Unai Emery is going to be signing a new deal with Villa, so that was always a no-go. Pochettino has gone from underdog with the bookies to the red-hot favourite. Personal terms are agreed. The compensation fee is around about £7.4m.

Then there is an extra, I think, about $2m for the staff that he will want to bring with him, the ones that have been with him throughout his time in management.

For me, I've always admired Pochettino. He's always wanted the United job. He's been linked with it numerous times before. He's always had a feeling that he could do a good job at Manchester United. His record is good. He finished sixth at Chelsea.

He won the league with PSG and finished second. Tottenham was really good, with a Champions League final, a second-place finish and then third a couple of times.

At Southampton, the eighth place finish he had when he first came to English football was really good. His brand of football was also really good, and so was his way of developing young players and getting them playing for him.

He's a serious coach. I think a lot of the criticism aimed at Carrick was almost like the boys' club mentality of "he's our mate, so he won't throw us under the bus".

That is great, and I do appreciate that. But Pochettino is a strong-minded individual who won't be afraid to tell people how it is. He has been in big dressing rooms. He's managed big players. He won't be overawed by the size of the task.

He'll know it's a big job. You get the feeling that he'll relish that challenge. He's not a young manager that's come in to prove his worth. He's 54. He's been around the block. He knows how it works. He's won big titles, and he's been in big games, so he knows exactly what's required.

His win rate at Tottenham was 54%. At PSG it was 65%. At Chelsea it was around about 51%. So he had his issues at Chelsea, and I know a lot of Chelsea fans are critical of him.

But Chelsea has been, for a while now, a difficult club to manage. So he had his problems there, but he also did a lot of good things at Chelsea. It was a really short spell at Stamford Bridge, 51 games.

Ultimately he'll be keen to show that he can still operate at this level. He signed a new deal with the USA through to the 2030 World Cup.

So it's a disappointment for them because I think they're going places. They've got some good young players and a good brand of football there.

But he was never going to turn down the chance to manage Manchester United. It feels like it's been a long time coming with him.

There is always a hint of optimism, but guarded optimism is probably the right phrase, just because it's so difficult to know.

History will tell you, certainly recent history, that it will ultimately probably go wrong at Manchester United. So guarded optimism would be the phrase I'd use at this stage.

I'm looking forward to what it could bring, getting in place for the Liverpool game. The interesting thing for me is the next few days. How does that develop? Do we get Fletcher in to take training on an interim? It's a strange one while they wait for Pochettino.

Bar a huge shock, he will be the next Manchester United manager. All guns ahead, all looking forward to that Liverpool game, which is a nice easy one to get going.

#1665. Opinion: Liverpool loan transfer agreement now imminent for the next Harry Kane

There's a new Harry Kane, and a transfer for him is imminent at Liverpool.

There are plenty of brilliant strikers in world football right now, but surely nobody is operating at the same level as the current Ballon d'Or winner.

Kane is simply a phenomenal footballer. He's always been a ruthless goalscorer, but what makes Kane so special is that he's so much more than your traditional no.9.

His link-up play is exceptional. He can drop deep, dictate the tempo, pick out passes that most midfielders wouldn't even attempt and then somehow still find himself in the perfect position to score.

At Bayern Munich, Kane has taken his game to another level. His movement, intelligence and finishing ability make him an absolute nightmare for defenders.

And the frightening thing is that he doesn't rely on pace. His game is built around intelligence, technique and an extraordinary understanding of space.

There are younger, quicker strikers around, but very few can influence games in quite so many ways.

Why Liverpool need another no.9 soonLiverpool might have Alexander Isak scoring goals right now, and Hugo Ekitike is edging closer to his return from injury, but that doesn't necessarily mean the Reds are sorted in the striker department. Far from it. Isak is undoubtedly a world-class player on his day. However, his injury record remains a concern, and Liverpool simply cannot afford to rely on him staying fit throughout an entire season. Meanwhile, Ekitike is coming back from a devastating Achilles injury. There's no guarantee he'll immediately return to his best, and Liverpool will need to manage his minutes carefully. Looking at the bigger picture, the Reds need more depth and competition in attack. Andoni Iraola's demanding system requires forwards who can press relentlessly, stretch defences and maintain intensity throughout matches. Having just two recognised senior strikers isn't ideal. Ultimately, if Liverpool want to compete on multiple fronts, bringing in another exciting young no.9 makes perfect sense.

#1664. Georgia vs Hungary - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 14:54, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 14:56

Georgia and Hungary both still have plenty to play for as they prepare to lock horns in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League on Saturday night.

The hosts are currently bottom of the section but can still finish second, while Hungary are currently second in the standings behind Northern Ireland.

Georgia boast a record of zero wins, two draws and two defeats from their four matches in Group B2, which has left them in a difficult spot in the group heading into their penultimate fixture.

With six points still to play for, Georgia are still able to book a spot in the promotion playoffs, but they will need to triumph here to stand any chance that occuring.

Ramaz Svanadze's side opened their 2026-27 Nations League with a 1-0 home defeat to Northern Ireland before picking up a point in a goalless draw with Ukraine.

Georgia then lost 1-0 to Hungary before drawing 0-0 with Northern Ireland, so they are actually still looking to score their first goal in this particular tournament.

The Crusaders, as it stands, are facing a relegation playoff, which would determine whether they would remain in League B for the next tournament or be relegated to League C.

Hungary, meanwhile, opened up their tournament with a 1-0 home defeat to Ukraine, before playing out a goalless draw with Northern Ireland in their final match of September.

National Eleven have picked up six points from their last two matches, though, beating Georgia 1-0 in their opening match of October before recording a 2-1 victory over Ukraine.

Marco Rossi's side are only one point behind the leaders Northern Ireland, with the two teams chasing the only automatic promotion position to League A.

Hungary will finish their 2026-27 group-stage campaign against Northern Ireland on November 17, with that match set to be crucial when it comes to top spot in the section.

National Eleven have only actually lost one of their last eight matches in all competitions, recording five victories in the process.

Georgia have one player out of this weekend's fixture through suspension, with Giorgi Kochorashvili unavailable for selection.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is also a notable absentee due to injury, so there will be pressure on Georges Mikautadze in the final third of the field; the 26-year-old has an impressive record of 23 goals in 47 caps for his country.

Georgia are also expected to have Giorgi Chakvetadze in their starting side, with the 27-year-old bidding to add to the 10 goals that he has scored for the national team.

As for Hungary, Milos Kerkez is available again after missing the team's last match through suspension, which is a major boost for the visitors heading into this contest.

Neither Alex Toth nor Milan Toth are in the current squad, so there will have to be changes from the team's last match, with Roland Sallai and Barnabas Vaga both expected to start.

There will be also be a spot in the middle of the midfield for Dominik Szoboszlai.

Published: 10:59 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 11:04 EST, 7 November 2026

Roberto De Zerbi questioned Tottenham’s character after his side’s second-half surrender saw them slip to defeat at Leeds.

Noah Okafor’s late strike sealed the points for the home side as Spurs – who played encouragingly before the break – had no answer to the home side’s rhythm.

De Zerbi said: ‘In the second half, I don’t know why, we suffered too much and deserved to lose. We won no duels, no one-to-ones. There was space to play and we didn’t take the right decisions.

‘We didn’t show personality or what we are, who we are. It’s a part of the journey. It’s not an excuse and it can be normal in football but we have to be honest.

‘If you are not honest today the future is not good. If we analyse our second-half behaviour honestly then I think we can become a top team.

‘We have the physicality and the quality but it’s not just about the physicality game. We didn’t show character, personality or courage.

Roberto De Zerbi says his Spurs side lacked 'character and courage' in their 1-0 loss to Leeds

Noah Okafor netted the winner for the hosts at Elland Road as Spurs lost control of the game

‘My players have the ability to come here, play better and maybe win. But maybe we are not ready yet to be consistent for many games in a row. We know where we have to work and improve.

‘I was surprised by the second half as my players worked very well this week. We spoke all week about the intensity and the type of game we would find here in this stadium so it was not a surprise for us.’

De Zerbi also feared Mathys Tel has suffered a bad injury following a tackle from Jayden Bogle at the end of the first half that was checked by VAR for a possible red card.

Tel was forced off after Bogle’s studs made heavy contact with his ankle, and will undergo scans. De Zerbi would not be drawn on whether Bogle should have been shown a red card but said referee John Brooks’ ‘parameters were not good enough’ in handling the situation.

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. “What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. #1661. Michael Carrick: Man United's shortest manager reigns ever after 45-year-old's sacking

By Joshua Cole | 12 Nov 2026 15:02

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick following a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign, bringing an abrupt end to the Englishman's second spell in charge at Old Trafford less than 10 months after he was appointed.

The 44-year-old initially arrived in January 2026 as a temporary replacement for Ruben Amorim, with the former midfielder making an immediate impression by restoring some confidence and guiding the Red Devils back into the Champions League picture.

Having overseen an encouraging improvement in results, Carrick was rewarded with a permanent contract in May, but his fortunes changed dramatically during the opening months of the new season.

United's disappointing results, inconsistent performances and growing concerns about their tactical direction ultimately proved too much for the club's hierarchy, with Sunday's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa preceding Man United's decision to relieve Carrick of his duties.

His departure adds another name to Manchester United's increasingly lengthy list of managerial casualties since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, although several managers in the club's history have endured even shorter spells in charge.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five of Manchester United's shortest managerial reigns, examining their appointments, records and the circumstances surrounding their departures.

Clarence 'Lal' Hilditch holds the distinction of having one of the shortest managerial spells in Manchester United's history, taking charge in October 1926 following the Football Association's suspension of John Chapman.

The former half-back became United's first player-manager, assuming responsibility for team affairs while continuing to feature on the pitch, but his appointment was never intended to be a long-term arrangement.

Hilditch oversaw 31 matches, winning nine, drawing eight and losing 14, giving him a win percentage of just 29.0%, with United struggling to establish consistency during his brief spell.

His final match came in April 1927, when United played out a goalless draw against Everton, before Herbert Bamlett was appointed as his replacement.

Although Hilditch's six-month spell was largely unsuccessful, he continued playing for the club until 1932, having made more than 100 appearances during his time at Old Trafford.

Walter Crickmer's first spell in charge of Manchester United lasted from November 1931 until the summer of 1932, when the club secretary temporarily assumed managerial responsibilities following the dismissal of Herbert Bamlett.

United had suffered relegation from the First Division in the previous campaign, having lost their opening 12 league matches and finished bottom of the table, leaving Crickmer with the difficult task of restoring some stability.

He managed 43 matches, winning 17, drawing nine and losing 17, which represented a win percentage of approximately 39.5%, as United recovered sufficiently to finish 12th in the Second Division.

Crickmer's time in the dugout ended when Scott Duncan was appointed as the club's new permanent manager in the summer of 1932, allowing him to return to his administrative responsibilities.

His departure was not the result of a dismissal, as Crickmer had primarily been acting as secretary-manager during a difficult period, and he would later take charge again between 1937 and 1945.

David Moyes remains one of the most prominent names on this list, having been selected by Ferguson to succeed him following his retirement in 2013.

The Scot officially took charge in July 2013, inheriting a team that had won the Premier League title by 11 points during Ferguson's final season, but quickly discovered that replicating his predecessor's success would be an enormous challenge.

Moyes began positively by winning the Community Shield against Wigan Athletic, before overseeing an impressive 4-1 Premier League victory against Swansea City in his first league match.

However, United's performances deteriorated as the campaign progressed, with defeats against Manchester City, Liverpool and Newcastle United exposing their difficulties against established Premier League opposition.

The Red Devils also suffered an embarrassing Champions League exit against Bayern Munich in the quarter-finals, while a 2-0 defeat against Everton in April 2014 proved to be Moyes's final match.

He departed on April 22, 2014, having won 27 of his 51 matches in charge, drawn nine and lost 15, giving him a win percentage of 52.9%.

Although Moyes had won the Community Shield, United were seventh in the Premier League and had already missed out on Champions League qualification, prompting the club to end his reign with four matches remaining.

Carrick's second spell at Old Trafford has now ended in disappointment, despite the considerable promise he demonstrated during his initial months in charge.

Appointed on January 13, 2026, following Amorim's dismissal, the former Middlesbrough manager quickly transformed United's fortunes, winning 11 of his first 16 Premier League matches and securing Champions League qualification.

His impressive work earned him a permanent position in May, with the club believing that his understanding of Manchester United's traditions and ability to establish a positive dressing-room atmosphere made him the right candidate for a longer-term project.

However, the challenges of managing United over a full campaign proved considerably more difficult, with his team collecting just three victories in their opening 15 matches of 2026-27.

Defeats against Bournemouth and Chelsea, alongside an embarrassing Champions League loss to Como, intensified scrutiny of his tactical approach, while a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa ultimately preceded his dismissal on November 12.

Carrick leaves with 15 wins, eight draws and nine defeats from 32 matches, representing a 46.9% win rate, although his initial success means his overall record is considerably better than his performances this season suggest.

Ruben Amorim's departure in January 2026 represented another significant managerial setback for Manchester United, with the Portuguese lasting just 14 months after replacing Erik ten Hag in November 2024.

United paid approximately £9.2m to release the former Sporting Lisbon manager from his contract, having been attracted by his impressive work in Portugal and his reputation for developing an organised, attack-minded team.

However, his preferred 3-4-3 system proved difficult to implement consistently at Old Trafford, with United struggling to produce convincing performances and suffering several damaging defeats during his first campaign.

The 2024-25 season ended with the club finishing 15th in the Premier League, their lowest position in the competition, while a 1-0 defeat against Tottenham Hotspur in the Europa League final denied them a route back into the Champions League.

Although there were occasional signs of improvement during the following campaign, disagreements over the club's footballing direction and continued inconsistency eventually undermined his position.

Amorim was dismissed on January 5, 2026, having recorded 24 victories, 18 draws and 21 defeats from 63 matches, giving him a disappointing win percentage of 38.1%.

His reign remains one of the least successful permanent managerial appointments of the post-Ferguson era, with Carrick now becoming the latest head coach to discover how difficult it is to restore Manchester United to their former standing.

#1660. Moretto: ‘Cardinale likes him a lot’ – Tresoldi interest confirmed but Milan face difficult pursuit

Matteo Moretto has provided an update on AC Milan’s pursuit of Nicolo Tresoldi, confirming the concrete interest.

Tresoldi’s rise to stardom is one that has naturally seen him enter Milan’s orbit, given that he is a publicly declared boyhood fan of the club. After an impressive start to the campaign with Club Brugge, it was his hat-trick in the Champions League against Inter at San Siro that made many take note.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The rumours have since followed linking him with what would be a ‘dream’ move to the Rossoneri, in his father’s words. La Gazzetta dello Sport spoke this morning of a €50m January attempt being lined up by Gerry Cardinale, to give Goncalo Ramos an attacking partner.

Speaking in a video on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Moretto shed some light on where things are currently at regarding the future of Tresoldi, and MilanNews transcribed what he had to say.

“A few days ago I told you how Milan were really close to signing Tresoldi a few years ago, so much so that the boy arrived, visited Milanello and was at Casa Milan, the contracts were even ready,” he began.

“I want to clarify that, since he was a very young boy at the time, it was not an operation directly supervised by Paolo Maldini. There were other people who were managing that operation. At the time, Ricky Massara was also Milan’s transfer manager and there were other people as well.

“The operation actually never got to the point because Milan stalled and the player returned to Germany, effectively signing a new contract with Hannover. Beyond this, there is now a lot of talk about Tresoldi in terms of Milan’s present and future.

“However, I want to clarify a few points. I can confirm that it is true that Cardinale likes him a lot and Milan likes him a lot. The club is evaluating what kind of steps to take to attempt this type of coup, but there are several points to clarify.

“First of all, the position of Club Brugge, Because Club Brugge are a very difficult club to deal with. We also need to understand Club Brugge’s results in the Champions League, because if they advance to the next round, they will earn a lot of money and won’t need to sell.

“Club Brugge’s idea is to keep Tresoldi until the end of the season to finish their season well. Regarding the money Club Brugge is asking for, we need to see if €50m will be enough.

“These are important points, and then there’s a lot of competition in Europe, because several clubs in Spain, Germany, and England are interested in Tresoldi. AC Milan are interested, and it’s true that AC Milan are looking for a striker in January.”
